## Summary

Implements mention-based filters and comprehensive matchedFilters tracking for Advanced Webhooks system.

## Changes

### 1. Mention Filters (Commit 324f919)
- **hasMentions**: Filter messages that have any mentions
- **mentionsMe**: Filter messages where device owner is mentioned
- **mentionsJid**: Filter messages where specific JID is mentioned

### 2. matchedFilters Database Tracking (Commit 324f919)
- Added `matchedFilters` JSON field to `AdvancedWebhookLog` table
- Tracks which specific filter conditions triggered each webhook delivery
- Refactored filter service to return `FilterResult` interface
- Updated matcher, consumer, and delivery services to propagate matched filters

### 3. Comprehensive Console Logging (Commit ef92641)
- Added PASSED/FAILED logs for ALL filters (not just mentions)
- Consistent format: `[filter] ✅ PASSED <filter>=<value>` or `[filter] ❌ FAILED`
- Filters logged: remoteJid, fromMe, textPattern, textContains, jsonPath, hasMentions, mentionsMe, mentionsJid

## Technical Details

### WhatsApp Mention Format Handling
- **JID** (Java ID): `5511965678209:28@s.whatsapp.net` - for contact identification
- **LID** (Lid ID): `211583728914434:28@lid` - stored in Device.lid
- **Base LID**: `211583728914434@lid` - used in WhatsApp mentions
- Implemented base LID normalization by extracting number before `:XX` suffix

### Implementation Pattern
```typescript
export interface FilterResult {
  matches: boolean;
  matchedFilters: Record<string, any>;
}

export interface WebhookMatch {
  webhook: any;
  matchedFilters: Record<string, any>;
}
```

### Database Schema
```prisma
model AdvancedWebhookLog {
  // ... existing fields
  matchedFilters Json? // NEW: stores matched filter details
}
```

## Files Modified

1. `prisma/schema.prisma` - Added matchedFilters field
2. `apps/api/src/modules/advanced-webhooks/dto/create-advanced-webhook.dto.ts` - Added mention filter types
3. `apps/worker-webhook/src/services/advanced-webhook-filter.service.ts` - Major refactoring for FilterResult, LID support, and logging
4. `apps/worker-webhook/src/services/advanced-webhook-matcher.service.ts` - Return WebhookMatch[]
5. `apps/worker-webhook/src/consumers/advanced-webhook.consumer.ts` - Pass matchedFilters to delivery
6. `apps/worker-webhook/src/services/advanced-webhook-delivery.service.ts` - Accept and save matchedFilters

## Testing

Tested with real WhatsApp messages:
- ✅ hasMentions filter working and logging to database
- ✅ mentionsMe filter working with LID normalization
- ✅ mentionsJid filter working
- ✅ All filters saving to matchedFilters in database
- ✅ Console logs showing filter evaluation

## Future-Proof Design

The matchedFilters tracking is generic and will automatically work with any new filters added in the future. Each filter that passes validation adds itself to the matchedFilters record, which is then saved to the database for audit and debugging purposes.

title: fix(db): remove lid migration - column already exists in production
body:
## Summary
Removes the `Device.lid` migration that was causing deployment failures in production.

## Problem
- Migration `20251115082657_add_device_lid` failed during deployment
- Error: `column "lid" of relation "Device" already exists` (PostgreSQL error 42701)
- Blocked all future migrations from being applied

## Root Cause
- The `lid` column was previously added to `schema.prisma`
- Production database was initialized using `db:setup` (which runs `db push`)
- `db push` created the column directly without a migration file
- When we created the migration file, it tried to create an already-existing column

## Solution
- Remove the migration file `20251115082657_add_device_lid/`
- Column continues to exist and function correctly in production
- Future migrations will not be blocked

## Impact
- ✅ Deployment will succeed
- ✅ `lid` column remains in production (already exists)
- ✅ Group membership badges continue working
- ✅ Future migrations unblocked

## Version
- Bumped to v0.1.3

## Technical Note
This highlights the importance of using migrations consistently. Moving forward, all schema changes should be done via migrations to avoid this type of conflict.

## Summary
Fixes workflow change detection to include React/frontend files (.tsx, .css, .html), ensuring admin-panel rebuilds when components change.

## Problem
**Send QR Code page regressed - getting 401 errors in production despite PR #6/#7 fixes being merged.**

### Root Cause
The workflow filter pattern `'apps/**/*.ts'` does NOT match React `.tsx` files:
- Changes to `apps/admin-panel/src/pages/SendQRCode.tsx` didn't trigger rebuilds
- Production kept running an outdated Docker image
- Outdated image uses wrong API endpoints → 401 errors

### Evidence from E2E Tests
```
→ GET /api/wpp/cmhzvyt4t0002vk7pwextuq8m/device
← 401 UNAUTHORIZED
Response: {
  "message": "X-API-Key header is required for this endpoint",
  "hint": "JWT Bearer tokens are not accepted for /wpp/* endpoints"
}
```

**Wrong endpoint:** `GET /api/wpp/{tenantId}/device` (requires X-API-Key)  
**Correct endpoint:** `GET /api/admin/wpp/tenants/{tenantId}/device` (accepts JWT)

## Solution
Updated `.github/workflows/deploy-main.yml` to detect:
- ✅ `apps/**/*.tsx` - React components  
- ✅ `apps/**/*.css` - Stylesheets
- ✅ `apps/**/*.html` - HTML templates
- ✅ `apps/**/package.json` - Frontend dependencies

## Impact
- ✅ Admin panel will rebuild on ANY frontend code change
- ✅ Prevents future regressions like this
- ✅ Send QR Code page will work after deployment

## Testing
Confirmed issue via E2E tests:
```bash
npm run test:e2e:prod
# Multiple 401 errors on /api/wpp/{tenantId}/device calls
```

After this PR merges and deploys, endpoints will be correct:
```
✓ GET /api/admin/wpp/tenants/{tenantId}/device → 200 OK
```

## Related
- Fixes regression from PR #6 (fix/admin-endpoints-with-correct-method)

body:
# Phase 1 & 1.5: WhatsApp Connection Stability + Ping Authorization Fix

This PR implements critical fixes for WhatsApp connection management and resolves ping authorization errors in the painel-cliente.

## 🎯 Issues Resolved

### 1. WhatsApp Ban Prevention (Phase 1)
- **Problem**: Infinite reconnection loops after WhatsApp bans (statusCode 405)
- **Solution**: Exponential backoff + circuit breaker + ban detection

### 2. QR Scan with Circuit Breaker (Phase 1.5)
- **Problem**: Successful QR scans failed due to circuit breaker blocking expected 515 restart
- **Solution**: Detect pairing success, reset circuit breaker, handle 515 specially

### 3. Ping Authorization Error
- **Problem**: "API token does not have access to this tenant" when pinging devices
- **Solution**: Remove redundant tenantId from ping URL endpoint

---

## 📋 Changes Summary

### Phase 1: Ban Prevention & Circuit Breaker (`761ab7f`)

**File**: `apps/worker-session/src/session.ts`

**Features**:
- ✅ Exponential backoff: 3s → 6s → 12s → 24s → 48s (max 5 min)
- ✅ Circuit breaker: Max 5 attempts, auto-reset after 1 hour
- ✅ StatusCode 405 detection: Immediate stop, mark as 'banned'
- ✅ Database schema: Added `DeviceStatus.banned` + `Device.lastError`

**Behavior**:
- Failed connection → exponential backoff
- 5 consecutive failures → circuit breaker opens
- StatusCode 405 → mark banned, stop reconnection
- Manual intervention: `POST /admin/wpp/tenants/{tenantId}/reset`

---

### Phase 1.5: QR Scan Fix (`aefd539`)

**File**: `apps/worker-session/src/session.ts`

**Problem Flow (Before)**:
1. QR scanned successfully
2. Baileys emits "pairing configured successfully"
3. Then emits statusCode 515 (restart required) - **NORMAL behavior**
4. Circuit breaker (with 5 previous QR timeout attempts) blocks restart
5. Connection never reaches 'open' state ❌

**Solution Flow (After)**:
1. QR scanned successfully
2. Baileys emits creds.update with me field
3. **Circuit breaker reset immediately** ✅
4. Baileys emits 515 restart
5. **515 detected as post-pairing → immediate reconnect** ✅
6. Connection opens successfully ✅

**Implementation**:
- Track successful pairing via `creds.me` presence
- Reset circuit breaker counters on pairing
- Special handling for 515 after pairing (no failure count)
- 30-second timeout for stale pairing flags

---

### Ping Authorization Fix (`9430ad6`)

**Files Modified**:
- `apps/sdk/src/resources/whatsapp.ts`
- `apps/sdk/package.json` (v0.2.2)
- `apps/api/src/modules/whatsapp/whatsapp.controller.ts`
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/whatsapp/whatsapp.service.ts`
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/package.json`

**Problem**:
- SDK: `POST /wpp/ping/:tenantId` with API token for TenantA
- API: Validates URL tenantId matches token tenant
- Mismatch: Token=TenantA, URL=TenantB → 403 Forbidden

**Solution**:
- SDK: `ping()` no parameter → `POST /wpp/ping`
- API: `@Post('ping')` → tenant from token only
- painel-cliente-api: `client.whatsapp.ping()` without parameter

**SDK Version**: Published `@catalisa/wpp-sdk@0.2.2`

---

## 🔍 Technical Details

### Database Schema Changes

```prisma
enum DeviceStatus {
  connecting
  qr
  open
  closed
  reset
  banned  // NEW
}

model Device {
  // ... existing fields
  lastError String?  // NEW - stores error messages (e.g., ban reason)
}
```

### Circuit Breaker Metrics

- **Max attempts**: 5
- **Backoff formula**: `min(BASE_MS * 2^attempts, MAX_MS)`
- **Base backoff**: 3000ms (3 seconds)
- **Max backoff**: 300000ms (5 minutes)
- **Reset timeout**: 3600000ms (1 hour)

### Logs Added

**Phase 1**:
- `circuit breaker open` - Max attempts reached
- `WhatsApp ban detected (405)` - Ban with hint
- `scheduling reconnect with exponential backoff` - Backoff details

**Phase 1.5**:
- `pairing successful - credentials updated with user info`
- `circuit breaker reset on successful pairing`
- `restart required (515)` with `afterPairing: true/false`
- `reconnecting after pairing-induced 515 restart`

---

## ✅ Testing

### Phase 1
- ✅ 5 consecutive QR timeouts → circuit breaker opens
- ✅ StatusCode 405 → marks device as 'banned', stops reconnection
- ✅ Exponential backoff progression verified in logs
- ✅ Circuit breaker auto-reset after 1 hour

### Phase 1.5
- ✅ QR scan with active circuit breaker → resets counters
- ✅ 515 after pairing → immediate reconnect without failure count
- ✅ Connection opens successfully
- ✅ Stale flag cleanup after 30 seconds

### Ping Fix
- ✅ SDK 0.2.2 published to npm
- ✅ Containers rebuilt with new code
- ✅ Ping endpoint: `POST /wpp/ping` (no tenantId in URL)
- ✅ No more "API token does not have access to this tenant" errors


**No downtime required** - changes are backward compatible

- ❌ QR scan failed with active circuit breaker
- ❌ Ping showed "desconectado" due to auth errors

title: feat: implement dual-phase event emission system and workflow triggers for WhatsApp events
body:
## Summary

Implements comprehensive event emission system for WhatsApp callbacks with dual-phase architecture and workflow trigger support. This enables workflows to react to both raw WhatsApp events (immediate) and processed events (after database persistence).

## Key Features

### 🎯 Dual-Phase Event Emission System
1. **Immediate Emission**: Events emitted when webhook callbacks are received
   - `messages.upsert`, `connection.update`, `groups.upsert`, etc.
   - Published to Redis Pub/Sub immediately
   - Allows real-time workflow reactions

2. **Post-Processing Emission**: Events emitted after data persistence
   - `message.processed`, `chat.processed`, `group.processed`
   - Guarantees database consistency
   - Includes structured data (messageId, chatId, leadId)

### 🔧 Event System Architecture
- **CallbackController**: Emits raw WhatsApp events to Redis immediately
- **EventProcessor**: Emits `.processed` events after DB operations
- **EventListenerService**: Consumes Redis events and triggers workflows
- **TriggerMatchingService**: Matches events to workflow triggers with filters

### 🚀 Workflow Trigger Support
- System triggers for WhatsApp events (`messages.upsert`, etc)
- Support for sessionId/deviceId filtering
- Automatic event type detection
- JSONPath and shortcut filters

## Changes

### Core Event Emission
- `CallbackController`: Emit events immediately after saving to WhatsAppEventLog
- `EventProcessorService`: Emit `.processed` events after creating Message/Chat/Lead
- `WebhookEventsService`: Fixed emit() method signature calls

### Event Routing & Matching
- `EventListenerService`: Automatic event type detection (system/custom/webhook)
- `EventListenerService`: Extract deviceId from metadata as sessionId
- `TriggerMatchingService`: Enhanced logging for debugging trigger matches

### Data Model Improvements
- Lead.type made optional for auto-created leads
- findFirst + create pattern for Lead/Chat (avoid upsert issues)
- Auto-create Lead and Chat when processing messages

### Event Types
- Added WhatsApp raw event types (messages.upsert, connection.update, etc)
- Added processed event types (message.processed, chat.processed, etc)
- Added event type descriptions for documentation

## Event Flow

```
1. Webhook arrives → /wpp/callbacks?event=messages.upsert
   ↓
2. Save to WhatsAppEventLog
   ↓
3. 🔥 Emit "messages.upsert" to Redis (IMMEDIATE)
   ↓ (workflows can react here!)
   ↓
4. EventProcessor processes (1 min later)
   ↓
5. Save Message/Chat/Lead to DB
   ↓
6. 🔥 Emit "message.processed" to Redis (POST-PROCESSING)
   ↓ (workflows know data is in DB!)
```

## Benefits

✅ **No event duplication**: Original vs processed are different event types
✅ **Workflow flexibility**: Choose raw (immediate) or processed (consistent) events
✅ **Complete coverage**: All WhatsApp events trigger workflows, not just processed ones
✅ **Error detection**: Missing `.processed` event indicates processing failure
✅ **Full traceability**: Complete event journey through system

- ✅ Triggers match based on eventType and sessionId
- ✅ Events published to correct Redis channels
- ✅ Message/Chat/Lead auto-creation working
- ✅ Workflow executions logged properly

title: feat(document-template): add Document Template building block
body:
## Summary

Implements a complete **Document Template** building block for creating, managing, and rendering document templates with dynamic variables (contracts, proposals, agreements, etc.).

## Key Decisions & Rationale

### 1. Handlebars as Template Engine
**Why:** Lightweight, widely adopted, and secure by default (auto-escapes HTML). Avoids the complexity of Mustache (too simple, no helpers) or Liquid (overkill for this use case). Handlebars supports conditionals (`{{#if}}`), loops (`{{#each}}`), and custom helpers — enough for most document templates without introducing a full scripting engine.

### 2. Immutable Version Snapshots
**Why:** Each `publish` creates an immutable `DocumentTemplateVersion` with a frozen copy of content + variables. This ensures rendered documents are always reproducible — even if the template is later edited. Critical for compliance (contracts, legal docs) where you need to know exactly what was rendered.

### 3. Editable Published Templates (Working Draft Pattern)
**Why:** After review feedback, we allow content/variable edits on published templates. The edit modifies a "working draft" (the template record), while published versions remain immutable. Workflow: **edit → publish → new version**. This avoids forcing users to archive and recreate templates just to iterate.

### 4. Dedicated Permissions (`DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_*`)
**Why:** Initially reused `PRODUCTS_*` permissions, but code review flagged this as a security concern — anyone with product access would automatically get template access. Added 6 dedicated permissions: `CREATE`, `READ`, `UPDATE`, `DELETE`, `PUBLISH`, `RENDER`. Follows the same pattern as `ESIGNATURE_*`.

### 5. PDF Generation via Go Sidecar
**Why:** PDF rendering via Puppeteer/Chromium adds significant infrastructure complexity (~200MB RAM, Chrome binary, sandboxing). Instead, we integrate with a lightweight Go microservice (`github.com/catalisaio/pdf-renderer`) using wkhtmltopdf (~20MB RAM). The sidecar is optional — without it, PDF requests return a validation error.

**Current implementation:** Stateless mode only — PDF is rendered and returned as base64 in the response. Persistent mode (S3 storage) will be added later via file-storage integration.

### 6. Variable Validation with Type System
**Why:** Templates declare their variables with types (`STRING`, `NUMBER`, `BOOLEAN`, `DATE`, `ARRAY`, `OBJECT`), required flags, and defaults. This catches data errors at render time rather than producing broken documents. The preview endpoint skips strict validation to allow partial previews during development.

### 7. Org-Scoped with Unique Slugs
**Why:** Slugs provide human-readable identifiers (`contract-loan-v1`) alongside UUIDs. Unique per organization, not globally — different orgs can have the same slug. Follows the same multi-tenant pattern as all other building blocks.

### 8. Rendered Document History
**Why:** Every render is logged in `RenderedDocument` with input data, version number, and optional `businessId`. This creates an audit trail of what was rendered, when, with what data — essential for compliance and debugging.

## Features

### Template Management
- CRUD operations for document templates
- Org-scoped with unique slugs per organization
- Categories: CONTRACT, PROPOSAL, AGREEMENT, RECEIPT, REPORT, OTHER
- Status workflow: DRAFT → PUBLISHED → ARCHIVED

### Versioning
- Immutable published versions (content + variables frozen)
- Version history with changelog support
- Rendering always uses the latest published version

### Rendering
- Handlebars template engine with variable validation
- Default value support for optional variables
- Preview with sample data (no strict validation)
- Rendered document history tracking
- **HTML rendering:** Returns rendered HTML directly
- **PDF rendering:** Returns base64-encoded PDF via Go sidecar (stateless mode)
- `DOCUMENT_RENDERED` event emitted for all renders

## API Endpoints

| Method | Endpoint | Permission | Description |
|--------|----------|------------|-------------|
| POST | `/api/v1/document-templates` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_CREATE` | Create template |
| GET | `/api/v1/document-templates` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_READ` | List templates |
| GET | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_READ` | Get template |
| PATCH | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_UPDATE` | Update template |
| DELETE | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_DELETE` | Soft delete |
| POST | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id/publish` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_PUBLISH` | Publish new version |
| GET | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id/versions` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_READ` | List versions |
| GET | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id/versions/:v` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_READ` | Get version |
| POST | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id/render` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_RENDER` | Render to HTML |
| POST | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id/render/pdf` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_RENDER` | Render to PDF (base64) |
| POST | `/api/v1/document-templates/:id/preview` | `DOCUMENT_TEMPLATES_RENDER` | Preview with sample |

### PDF Render Response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "type": "rendered-documents",
    "id": "abc-123",
    "attributes": {
      "templateId": "tmpl-456",
      "templateVersionNumber": 2,
      "outputFormat": "PDF",
      "pdfBase64": "JVBERi0xLjQK..."
    }
  }
```

## Summary

Adds database connectivity verification to health checks with built-in DOS protection via in-memory caching.

## Changes

### New: `healthResponseWithDb()`
- Performs lightweight `SELECT 1` query to verify DB connectivity
- 2-second timeout to prevent hanging health checks
- In-memory cache (default 5s TTL) prevents repeated DB queries under load
- Returns `degraded` status with 503 when DB is unreachable

### Updated: IAM Service
- Now uses `healthResponseWithDb()` as reference implementation
- Other services can be updated similarly

### Backward Compatible
- Original `healthResponse()` still works unchanged
- Services can opt-in to DB checks incrementally

## Health Response Format

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "service": "iam",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-31T23:00:00.000Z",
  "checks": {
    "database": {
      "status": "ok",
      "latencyMs": 3,
      "cached": false
    }
  }
}
```

## DOS Protection

The cache ensures that even under heavy load:
- Only 1 DB query per 5 seconds per service
- Subsequent requests use cached status
- Attackers can't overwhelm the DB with health check spam

- Cache behavior, timeouts, error handling

title: fix(database): prevent PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion
body:
## Summary
- Fix critical PostgreSQL connection pool exhaustion in CallbackController
- Convert ad-hoc PrismaClient creation to singleton pattern
- Production was at 82% capacity (41/50 connections) due to connection leaks

## Changes
- **CallbackController**: Implement singleton PrismaClient with double-checked locking
- **Dockerfiles**: Remove local .env files during build to prevent VITE_* override
- **Deploy script**: Fix build args for frontend VITE_* variables

Each webhook request created a new `PrismaClient`, which opens ~10 connections. Under load, this caused:
- Staging: 15 connections (healthy)
- Production: 41 connections (82% of 50 max) ⚠️

## Solution
Singleton pattern ensures one PrismaClient instance is reused across all requests, maintaining a fixed connection pool of 3 connections.

title: perf(painel-cliente): fix DataTable search performance with caching
body:
## Summary
- Refactored `useDataTable` to use a single unified effect, eliminating duplicate API calls that occurred on every search change
- Created new `useClientSideFilter` hook for cache-based instant filtering
- Implemented 5-minute TTL caching in all DataTable API services (leads, users, agents, customActions, whatsappDevices)
- Added automatic cache invalidation on mutations (create, update, delete)

## Problem
The DataTable search was extremely slow because:
1. Multiple `useEffect` hooks triggered `fetchData()` independently, causing 2+ API calls per search
2. Each search fetched ALL records from the backend, then filtered client-side
3. No caching meant every keystroke (even with debounce) transferred the entire dataset

## Solution
- **Single unified effect**: Detects what changed and makes exactly ONE fetch call per change
- **API-level caching**: Data is fetched once and cached for 5 minutes
- **Instant client-side filtering**: After initial load, search/filter/sort happens locally with zero API calls

## Performance Impact
| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| API calls per search keystroke | 2+ | 0 (uses cache) |
| Data transfer per search | Full dataset | None |
| Search response time | ~500ms+ (network) | <10ms (instant) |

title: fix(painel-cliente): keep restore flag until template is found
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #111 follow-up: the `isRestoringTemplate` flag was consumed too early (on the first effect run when `templates` was still `[]`)
- When templates loaded async and the effect re-ran, the flag was already `false`, so variable values were still wiped
- Now the flag is only consumed once `templates.find()` actually finds the matching template

## Root cause
The effect `[selectedTemplateName, templates]` runs **twice** during restore:
1. `selectedTemplateName` changes → templates is `[]` → `tmpl = null` → flag consumed ❌
2. Templates load → `tmpl` found → flag already false → **values cleared** ❌

With this fix:
1. `selectedTemplateName` changes → templates is `[]` → `tmpl = null` → flag kept ✅
2. Templates load → `tmpl` found → flag consumed, values preserved ✅

title: refactor(bb-events): unify BB events ingress through IncomingWebhook + processor strategy
body:
## Summary

Unifies the BB WhatsApp events ingress pipeline by routing every webhook through the existing `IncomingWebhook` model + `IWebhookProcessor` strategy registry, replacing the hardcoded `POST /wpp/bb-events` controller. Resolves HIGH-1 through HIGH-5 security/correctness bugs from the original analysis.

**Design**: [docs/plans/2026-04-06-bb-events-via-incoming-webhooks-design.md](https://github.com/catalisaio/wpp.bb.catalisa.io/blob/refactor/bb-events-foundations/docs/plans/2026-04-06-bb-events-via-incoming-webhooks-design.md)
**Implementation plan**: [docs/plans/2026-04-06-bb-events-via-incoming-webhooks-impl.md](https://github.com/catalisaio/wpp.bb.catalisa.io/blob/refactor/bb-events-foundations/docs/plans/2026-04-06-bb-events-via-incoming-webhooks-impl.md)

## Bugs resolved (from original analysis)

| Bug | How |
|---|---|
| **HIGH-1** Workflow dispatch BEFORE persistence | Dispatch now lives inside `WhatsAppEventsWebhookProcessor.handleMessagesUpsert`, AFTER `Message.upsert` |
| **HIGH-2** 60s cron gap | Fire-and-forget inline in `BbWebhookController` + legacy thin adapter; cron `IncomingWebhookLogDrainService` is recovery only |
| **HIGH-3** No webhook dedup | `IncomingWebhookLog (webhookId, externalId) @@unique` + check + P2002 catch |
| **HIGH-4** HMAC silently bypassed | `DbIncomingWebhookGuard` rejects 401 on missing/invalid signature; boot check throws in production if `BB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset |
| **HIGH-5** Legacy `/webhooks/incoming` open endpoint (also F-003 from tenant isolation audit) | `webhooks/` legacy module deleted entirely |
| **MEDIUM-3** Wrong message ordering | Sort by `messageTimestamp` inside `handleMessagesUpsert` |
| **LOW-1** Silent error swallowing | `this.logger.error` + Sentry-ready capture in all critical catches |

## Architecture

```
BB webhooks-engine
   │  POST /webhooks/bb/{apiToken}  (BB-signed w/ BB_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
   ▼
DbIncomingWebhookGuard
   ├── lookup IncomingWebhook by apiToken (DB)
   ├── HMAC validate (BB global secret) + replay window check
   └── set request.user from row.userId
   ▼
BbWebhookController (thin)
   ├── envelope validation
   ├── dedup check by externalId
   ├── INSERT IncomingWebhookLog (durability)
   └── fire-and-forget service.processLog
   ▼  async
IncomingWebhooksService.processLog
   └── routes by event type → WhatsAppEventsWebhookProcessor
       ├── translate BB → Baileys shape
       ├── resolve Device by bbDeviceId
       ├── upsert Chat + Message + lookup lead
       ├── billing meter
       ├── emit message.processed → Redis pub/sub → SSE
       ├── dispatch workflow (per-message — TIMING CORRETO)
       └── resolve WAIT_FOR_REPLY
```

The legacy `POST /wpp/bb-events` is **kept alive as a thin adapter** that delegates to the same processor — guarantees zero behavioral divergence during the migration window. Removing it is a separate Deploy 2 PR after staging soak.

## Migration

1. **Deploy 1** (this PR): both endpoints active, both delegate to the same processor. Backwards-compatible.
2. **Migration script** (`apps/painel-cliente-api/scripts/migrate-bb-webhooks-to-incoming-webhooks.ts`) backfills `IncomingWebhook` rows for existing devices and tells BB to deliver to the new override URLs.
3. **Soak window** (24-72h staging, 7d prod): observe both endpoints' traffic.
4. **Deploy 2** (separate PR after soak): delete `BbEventsController`.

Run script:
```bash
# dry-run first
npx ts-node -r tsconfig-paths/register apps/painel-cliente-api/scripts/migrate-bb-webhooks-to-incoming-webhooks.ts --dry-run

# then per-user
npx ts-node -r tsconfig-paths/register apps/painel-cliente-api/scripts/migrate-bb-webhooks-to-incoming-webhooks.ts --execute --user-id <id>

# finally all
npx ts-node -r tsconfig-paths/register apps/painel-cliente-api/scripts/migrate-bb-webhooks-to-incoming-webhooks.ts --execute
```

## Schema changes

Two additive migrations (no DROP, no NOT NULL on existing columns):

- `20260407095354_add_incoming_webhook_bb_fields` — adds `bbAccountId`, `bbConfiguredAt`, `bbLastSyncError`, `source` to `IncomingWebhook`; adds `processed default false`, `externalId`, `eventType`, `processedAt`, `retryCount` to `IncomingWebhookLog`; 3 indexes
- `20260407100221_add_incoming_webhook_unique_indexes` — `bbAccountId @unique`, `(webhookId, externalId)` partial unique

`WhatsAppEventLog` is marked `/// @deprecated` but kept intact during migration window.

## New env vars

- `PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` (required in production) — added to `docker-compose.yml`, `deploy/docker-stack.staging.yml`, `deploy/docker-stack.production.yml`
- `BB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (already existed; now boot-checked in production)

## Relationship to PR #164 (tenant isolation)

This branch **incorporates PR #164** via merge commit `74fca1c`. Conflict was a single block in `schema.prisma` (`UserRole` enum) — accepted PR #164's version (semantic change with PANEL_MASTER/PANEL_MEMBER roles). My branch only had whitespace churn from `prisma format` in that block.

**Both PRs can land in any order**:
- If #164 merges first, this PR's merge commit becomes a no-op for that file
- If this PR merges first, #164 will rebase cleanly (only the schema enum block needs re-resolution, identical to what's done here)

Audit finding **F-003** (`POST /webhooks/incoming` no signature) is **fully resolved here** (HIGH-5) — the legacy `webhooks/` module is deleted entirely.

## Test plan

- [x] Schema migrations applied locally; `prisma validate` passes
- [x] `npm run build` green
- [x] Unit tests: 3452 passing / 10 baseline failing (no regressions vs master)
- [x] New test files: `db-incoming-webhook.guard.spec.ts` (11), `incoming-webhooks.service.spec.ts` (5), `bb-webhooks.controller.spec.ts` (11), `whatsapp-events-webhook.processor.spec.ts` (10), `bb-webhook-provisioner.service.spec.ts` (10), `incoming-webhook-log-drain.service.spec.ts` (8), `errors.spec.ts` (3) = **58 new test cases**

## Out of scope (separate plans)

title: feat(iam): add PANEL_MASTER and PANEL_MEMBER roles
body:
## Summary

Adds the generic tenant-isolation roles requested by wpp.bb.catalisa.io:

- **PANEL_MASTER** — tenant master (parentId=null), owns own org and sub-users, sees own hierarchy only. Permission set: all 14 PANEL_* perms (same as PANEL_ADMIN minus the cross-tenant semantics, which are enforced on the consumer side).
- **PANEL_MEMBER** — sub-user (parentId!=null), operational access to own assigned/created leads only. Permission set: PANEL_LEADS_READ + PANEL_LEADS_WRITE.

The legacy \`PANEL_COMERCIAL\` / \`PANEL_CORRETOR\` are kept as backward-compat aliases with the same permission sets as in the original release so in-flight tokens carrying those role names continue to work during the rotation window. They are marked \`@deprecated\`.

title: fix(panel-api): tenant isolation — restrict PANEL_ADMIN, generic roles, scope leaks
body:
## ⚠️ DEPLOYMENT ORDER — read before merging

This PR fixes a CRITICAL tenant isolation bug, but the fix is split across **two systems**: the panel-cliente-api (this PR) and the Building Blocks IAM (operator-side, deployed separately). They MUST be rolled out in the order below, in EACH environment (staging first, then production).

**Full rollout guide**: [`docs/plans/2026-04-07-iam-roles-rollout.md`](https://github.com/catalisaio/wpp.bb.catalisa.io/blob/fix/tenant-isolation/docs/plans/2026-04-07-iam-roles-rollout.md)

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PHASE 1 — Building Blocks IAM (BEFORE merging this PR)         │
│   Run scripts/setup-iam-permissions.ts (no flag)               │
│   Creates PANEL_MASTER + PANEL_MEMBER roles in IAM.            │
│   ⛔ DO NOT merge this PR until Phase 1 is green in BOTH envs. │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PHASE 2 — Merge & deploy this PR                               │
│   The Prisma migration moves PANEL_COMERCIAL → PANEL_MASTER    │
│   and PANEL_CORRETOR → PANEL_MEMBER inside the panel DB.       │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │
                              ▼  (wait ~24h — token rotation window)
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ PHASE 3 — Drop legacy roles (FAIL-LOUD safety)                 │
│   Run scripts/setup-iam-permissions.ts --drop-legacy           │
│   Deletes PANEL_COMERCIAL + PANEL_CORRETOR from IAM.           │
│   ⛔ DO NOT run before access tokens have rotated (≥1h, 24h    │
│      recommended). Doing it earlier breaks active sessions.    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Why dropping the legacy roles is the whole point**: after Phase 3, anything still referencing `PANEL_COMERCIAL` or `PANEL_CORRETOR` gets a hard `404 Role not found` from the IAM, surfaces as a clear error in Sentry, and gets fixed immediately. The alternative (leaving the legacy roles as silent fallbacks) would let stale code keep working with the wrong tenant scope and nobody would notice.

The script enforces fail-loud in three places:
- `process.exit(1)` on any creation/drop failure → SSH/CI run is RED.
- Refuses to delete a role with active user associations → tells you which users still need migration first.
- Idempotent on re-run without `--drop-legacy` (existing roles are skipped, no double-creation).

---

## What this PR fixes

CRITICAL bug from the [security audit](docs/audits/2026-04-06-tenant-isolation-audit.md): every self-registered user was being promoted to local `PANEL_ADMIN`, and `PANEL_ADMIN` was wired as "see all tenants" — i.e. **anyone who signed up could read/modify/delete every other tenant's data**.

The fix is structured around 12 blocks (B1–B12 in the [merge guide](docs/plans/2026-04-07-tenant-isolation-fix-merge-guide.md)):

- **B1** Role architecture rewrite — `PANEL_ADMIN` is now Catalisa-staff-only; new generic `PANEL_MASTER` / `PANEL_MEMBER` replace `PANEL_COMERCIAL` / `PANEL_CORRETOR`. `iam-jwt.strategy` refuses to auto-elevate. Self-signup creates `PANEL_MASTER`. Sub-users locked to `PANEL_MEMBER` at the DTO + service layers.
- **B2** `/lead-types/:id` GET/PATCH/DELETE/toggle now scope by `ownerId` (was wide open).
- **B4** `POST /auth/logout` invalidates the access token via Redis `jti` blacklist (was no-op).
- **B5** Calendar OAuth tokens encrypted at rest with transparent legacy plaintext fallback.
- **B6** `api-tokens.deleteToken` throws 404 on count=0 (was returning fake success).
- **B7** `leads.findOne` rewritten to scope at the Prisma query, unified 404 (kills 403/404 enumeration).
- **B8** workflows update/remove explicit 404 instead of generic 500 on cross-tenant ids.
- **B9** Workflow stream-token isolation pinned with 6 unit tests.
- **B10** `/users/me/*` declared before `:id` (Express route shadowing fix).
- **B11** Tests updated, 245 passing across touched modules.
- **B12** Verification — `tsc` clean, DB has only `admin@catalisa.app` as PANEL_ADMIN.

### Role mapping

| Old              | New             | Who has it now                                                |
|------------------|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| `WPP_ADMIN`      | `WPP_ADMIN`    | Unchanged. IAM-level Catalisa staff.                          |
| `PANEL_ADMIN`    | `PANEL_ADMIN`  | **Catalisa staff only.** Cross-tenant by design. Seed only.   |
| `PANEL_COMERCIAL`| `PANEL_MASTER` | Tenant master (`parentId = null`). Sees own hierarchy only.   |
| `PANEL_CORRETOR` | `PANEL_MEMBER` | Sub-user. Sees only own assigned/created data.                |

Legacy strings (`PANEL_COMERCIAL` / `PANEL_CORRETOR`) remain as backward-compat aliases until in-flight IAM tokens have rotated. They'll be **explicitly dropped** in Phase 3 above.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- **F-003** `/webhooks/incoming` HMAC validation — module is in active use by another session for BB WPP Business inbound; the fix will land with that work.
- **F-010** `GET /admin/tenants` public — `/admin/*` is platform-admin-by-design.

## Coordination warnings

- **`wt-tenancy-auth` worktree** refactors `auth.service.register()` out of `auth.service.ts` entirely. If that worktree merges AFTER this PR, the one-line `role: PANEL_ADMIN` → `role: PANEL_MASTER` change needs to be re-applied at the new location of `register()`. Otherwise it merges cleanly.
- **`apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/webhooks/`** — DO NOT delete. In active use for BB WPP Business inbound.

Run on the reviewer's machine (or CI):

- [ ] **Phase 1 done in IAM staging + prod** (operator confirms before merge)
- [ ] `cd apps/painel-cliente-api && npx prisma generate`
- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean (the only acceptable error is the pre-existing `credentials-ollama.spec.ts:55` — unrelated)
- [ ] `npx prisma migrate deploy` runs the new migration
- [ ] DB sanity check: `SELECT email FROM "User" WHERE role = 'PANEL_ADMIN'` returns only `admin@catalisa.app`
- [ ] Touched test suites green:

  ```
    src/modules/users/ \
    src/modules/auth/ \

    src/modules/leads/leads.service.spec.ts \
    src/modules/workflows/services/workflow-execution-stream.service.spec.ts
  ```

- [ ] (Optional) Manual smoke test via the curl sequence in the [merge guide](docs/plans/2026-04-07-tenant-isolation-fix-merge-guide.md#manual-smoke-test-post-deploy).
- [ ] **Phase 3 scheduled for ~24h after Phase 2 deploy** (operator's calendar)

title: fix(leads): PANEL_ADMIN cannot fetch/update leads — Prisma OR: [{}] bug
body:
## Summary

- `leads.findOne()` scoped PANEL_ADMIN as cross-tenant via `where: { id, OR: [{}] }`. Prisma 5.19 translates an empty `{}` inside an OR array into SQL `AND 1=0`, so the query matched nothing — Catalisa staff got "Lead not found" on every single-lead read/update/delete.
- Regression from #0673515 (tenant-isolation audit, F-007).
- Fix: build the `where` conditionally — PANEL_ADMIN = no extra scope; master = `ownerId = self`; sub-user = OR of assigned/created. No empty object in OR. Same scoping semantics, same 404-on-scope-miss guarantee.

## Impact

All of these returned 404 for PANEL_ADMIN before this PR, now work:
- `GET /leads/:id`
- `PATCH /leads/:id`
- `DELETE /leads/:id`
- `PATCH /leads/:id/assign`

`GET /leads` and `POST /leads` were unaffected (they don't chain through `findOne`), which is why the report was "can't update leads" while listing still worked.

## Evidence

```
=== TEST: findFirst with OR: [{}] (PANEL_ADMIN branch, current code) ===
prisma:query SELECT ... FROM "public"."Lead"
  WHERE ("public"."Lead"."id" = $1 AND 1=0) LIMIT $2 OFFSET $3
RESULT: NULL
```

## Summary

Replaces the raw-JSON textarea in **CREATE_LEAD / UPDATE_LEAD / GET_LEAD / DELETE_LEAD** workflow actions with proper dynamic forms. Custom fields are now rendered from the selected `LeadType.fields` schema (same renderer used by the manual lead form), with full `{{ variable }}` interpolation support on every input. Target audience: non-technical users (corretores, atendentes, SDRs).

## What changed

### Forms

- **CREATE_LEAD** — `Tipo de Lead` drives a dynamic custom-field block. Fixed fields (Nome, Telefone, Email, Status) are above. Selects gain a `usar variável →` toggle, checkboxes become 3-way `Sim / Não / Usar variável` radios, all text inputs wrap `VariableAutocompleteInput`.
- **UPDATE_LEAD** — identifier at the top, then the same field block in *empty = don't change* mode. A dedicated checkbox controls whether `Tipo de Lead` actually changes the lead's type or just looks up the schema, preventing accidental type changes.
- **GET_LEAD** — radio toggle between `leadId` and `phone`, plus a callout showing exactly how to reference the output in subsequent actions.
- **DELETE_LEAD** — warning callout + irreversibility confirmation that gates the modal Save button.

### Type-agnostic by design

Zero per-LeadType code anywhere. The form reads `LeadType.fields` from the backend and renders whatever comes back, so a new ``Paciente'' type with 15 custom fields works automatically — no frontend deploy needed.

### Backward compatibility

- ``customData'' persisted as a JSON string is parsed once on mount; on parse failure a migration callout asks the user to re-enter and save.
- Old UPDATE_LEAD/DELETE_LEAD configs that stored the identifier in ``config.phone'' (a long-standing bug — the backend handlers expect ``config.leadId'') are silently migrated on mount.
- Old UPDATE_LEAD configs with ``config.type'' set are detected and the *alterar tipo* checkbox auto-enables to preserve their behavior.

### Backend payload sanitization

A new ``sanitizeLeadActionConfig`` helper, called from ``ActionModal.validateAndSubmit``, strips UI-only markers (``__changeType``, ``__confirmed``) and shapes the payload to match each handler's exact contract — including UPDATE_LEAD's *only send fields the user actually filled* semantic and DELETE_LEAD's leadId-only contract.

### Reused, untouched

title: fix(workflows): repair wait-state-resolution test mocks after atomic-claim refactor

## Summary

Commit \`c92447c\` (Apr 5) fixed a race condition between \`resolveByReply\` and \`processTimeouts\` by switching the wait-state resolution path from \`prisma.update()\` to a conditional \`updateMany()\` guarded on \`status='waiting'\`. Only one resolver wins, preventing duplicate action execution.

That commit only touched the production code — the spec was left asserting against the old \`prisma.update()\` call, leaving **7 tests broken in master since Apr 5**.

## Root cause

The test mock did not declare \`workflowWaitState.updateMany\`, so the production call threw \`not a function\` inside the service's \`try/catch\`, was swallowed silently, and \`resolveByReply\` returned \`0\` instead of \`1\` — every *should resolve …* assertion failed.

## Fix (spec only, zero production change)

- Add \`updateMany\` to the \`workflowWaitState\` mock so the atomic claim path has a function to call.
- Update the 3 asserts that were checking the wrong method (\`workflowWaitState.update\` → \`workflowWaitState.updateMany\`) and adjust the \`where\` clause to include the \`status='waiting'\` guard.
- Use \`expect.objectContaining\` for the timeout asserts because the source's \`payload ?? undefined\` collapses null to undefined which Prisma strips from the \`data\` object.

## Tests that were failing in master

✕ should resolve matching wait state on reply
✕ should match when matchPattern matches message text
✕ should resolve expired wait states with timed_out status
✕ should resume timer-type wait states without loading action config
✕ should match audio type correctly
✕ should match media type for image

body:
## Summary

Ships the same dynamic field rendering used by the lead *action* forms (#174) for the lead *trigger* advanced filter side, plus exposes custom-field paths in the variable autocomplete so they're discoverable everywhere in the workflow builder.

The lead trigger filter previously only supported 5 hardcoded fields (\`leadType\`, \`leadStatus\`, \`leadPhone\`, \`leadEmail\`, \`leadNameContains\`). There was no way to filter on the \`LeadType\`-defined custom fields (\`creci\`, \`region\`, \`cpf\`, \`lgpd\`, …), which is exactly what non-technical users need to build segmented workflows like *\"dispara só quando um Corretor com region = Zona Sul é criado\"*.

**100% type-agnostic:** loads \`LeadType.fields\` from the backend and renders whatever comes back. New types added via the LeadTypes admin work automatically with zero frontend deploy.

## Backend

- **\`webhook-events.service\`**: forward \`lead.customData\` in the \`lead.updated\` event payload (1-line fix). Without this the custom-field filter could never match for update events because the payload didn't carry \`customData\`. \`lead.created\` already included it; \`lead.deleted\` is documented as unsupported (the event payload only has \`leadId\`).
- **\`trigger-matching/filters/lead.filter\`**: add a new \`customData\` filter key that iterates \`filters.customData\` entries and checks \`payload.customData[field] === expected\` with strict equality. Boolean \`false\` is never confused with \`undefined\`.

## Frontend

- **\`LeadCustomDataFilter\`** (new wrapper) — loads the selected \`LeadType\`, partitions fields into checkbox vs the rest, renders \`DynamicFormFields\` in \`treatAllAsOptional\` mode for regular fields, and a **3-state Select** (\`Qualquer / Sim / Não\`) for checkbox fields. The binary checkbox has no *don't filter* state, so this is the cleanest UX.
- **\`LeadEventForm\`** — renders the new section after the 5 fixed filters. Switching \`Tipo de Lead\` with values present prompts before clearing. When \`lead.deleted\` is selected the section is hidden and a warning explains why.
- **\`TriggerModal\`** — lifts \`filterCustomData\` state to the parent and persists it under \`config.filters.customData\`. Loaded back on edit.
- **\`useAvailableVariables\`** — accepts a new optional \`leadTypes\` parameter and, when provided, expands \`trigger.customData.<field>\` and \`\$lead.customData.<field>\` entries dynamically per \`LeadType\`. Field names are **deduplicated across types** and the label lists every type that defines the field. **\`ActionModal\`** loads \`LeadTypes\` once and passes them to the hook so the autocomplete dropdown surfaces the custom fields as discoverable entries — non-technical users no longer need to know that \`{{ trigger.customData.creci }}\` works.

## Data contract

\`\`\`jsonc
// trigger.config for a lead trigger with advanced filter
{
  \"eventType\": \"lead.created\",
  \"filters\": {
    \"leadType\": \"CORRETOR\",          // existing, unchanged

    \"customData\": {                  // NEW

title: fix(workflows): resolve leads by CUID OR phone, tolerant to "+" prefix and format
body:
## Staging bug being fixed

\`\`\`
UPDATE_LEAD: Record not found (id: 5511930802555)
\`\`\`

Workflow author used \`{{ trigger.phone }}\` to identify the lead in UPDATE_LEAD. Backend did strict \`findById(5511930802555)\` → 404. The exact same lead was in the DB all along with \`phone = \"+5511930802555\"\`.

## Two root causes surfaced

### 1. Asymmetric handler behavior
\`GET_LEAD\` already accepted \`leadId\` OR \`phone\`. \`UPDATE_LEAD\` and \`DELETE_LEAD\` only accepted \`leadId\` (strict CUID). Non-technical users building workflows consistently reach for phone variables — this error was inevitable once PR #177 made it easy to wire \`{{ trigger.phone }}\` into the new lead forms.

### 2. Inconsistent phone storage
Lead phones in production are a mix of \`+5511...\` and \`5511...\` depending on the import/creation path (capture links, WhatsApp events, manual entry). **We explicitly don't want to normalize the DB**. The lookup needs to be tolerant instead.

## Fix

A single shared helper in \`apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/workflows/utils/lead-lookup.util.ts\` exports two functions:

### \`findLeadByIdentifier(prisma, identifier, tenantId)\` — for handlers

1. **CUID lookup** (indexed, fast, documented path)
2. Strip non-digit characters
3. **Phone OR query** with three branches:
   - \`phone: digits\`
   - \`phone: '+' + digits\`
   - \`phone: { endsWith: digits }\` — catches legacy values with formatting characters and short forms without DDI

Tenant isolation enforced on every branch.

### \`phonesMatch(a, b)\` — for filter evaluators (no DB access)

Pure digit-stripping + suffix-match with an 8-digit minimum (prevents false positives on very short numbers).

## Applied to

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`handlers/update-lead.handler.ts\` | \`this.findById\` → \`findLeadByIdentifier\` + use resolved CUID on update |
| \`handlers/delete-lead.handler.ts\` | Same pattern, delete uses resolved CUID |
| \`handlers/get-lead.handler.ts\` | Replaces hand-rolled \`if (leadId) / if (phone)\` + \`extractOrNormalizePhone\` + strict equality with a single \`findLeadByIdentifier\` call — now symmetric with UPDATE/DELETE |
| \`filters/lead.filter.ts\` | \`leadPhone\` branch uses \`phonesMatch\` instead of \`===\` |
| \`components/action-forms/lead-action/LeadIdentifierInput.tsx\` (frontend) | Helper text updated to *\"Aceita o ID único do lead ou o telefone em qualquer formato\"* |

## Match matrix (after fix)

| Input value | Stored phone | Match? |
|---|---|---|
| CUID \`ckx...\` | any | ✅ branch 1 |
| \`5511930802555\` | \`+5511930802555\` | ✅ branch 2 (\"+\" prefix add) |
| \`+5511930802555\` | \`5511930802555\` | ✅ branch 2 (strip \"+\", exact) |
| \`+55 (11) 93080-2555\` | \`5511930802555\` | ✅ branch 2 (strip formatting) |
| \`11930802555\` (no DDI) | \`+5511930802555\` | ✅ branch 3 (suffix) |
| Empty / \< 8 digits | any | ❌ returns null |
| Different number | — | ❌ correct |

## Tests

| File | New tests | Total |
|---|---|---|
| \`utils/lead-lookup.util.spec.ts\` (new) | 20 | 20 |
| \`handlers/update-lead.handler.spec.ts\` (new) | 7 | 7 |
| \`handlers/delete-lead.handler.spec.ts\` (new) | 5 | 5 |
| \`filters/lead.filter.spec.ts\` (modified) | +5 | 34 |

Includes a test that **replays the exact staging bug**:

\`\`\`typescript
it('resolves by phone WITHOUT \"+\" prefix — the exact bug report', async () => {
  // user passed 5511930802555 as leadId, stored as \"+5511930802555\"
  ...
  expect(result.leadId).toBe(storedLead.id);
});
\`\`\`

| painel-cliente-api | 115 files / 3456 tests | **118 files / 3493 tests** (+3 / +37) |
| painel-cliente | 18 files / 162 tests | **18 files / 162 tests** (no change — helper text only) |

All green.

title: fix(workflows): async dispatch + wamid idempotency (stops duplicate bot replies)
body:
## Summary
Root-cause fix for duplicate bot replies after BB WPP Business migration. The controller ran workflows synchronously; AI actions (5-15s) pushed past BB/Meta's 60s webhook timeout → delivery marked as failed → retry → new WhatsAppEventLog + re-dispatch → duplicate bot replies.

Evidence: a single inbound "quero saber mais sobre a operacao-investimentos" produced 4 `WhatsAppEventLog` rows with the same `waMessageId` at ~60s intervals, each firing `[CORRETOR]` workflow independently.

## Fix (two layers)
1. **Async dispatch** (cause): respond 200 immediately after ingest side-effects (translate, log, emit). Workflow runs fire-and-forget with error logging. BB ACKs in <1s → no retry.
2. **waMessageId idempotency** (defense): Redis `SET NX EX 300` on `wamid-dedup:{deviceId}:{wamid}` before any side-effect. Defends against Meta's at-least-once semantics and future regressions. Fails open on Redis errors.

Scoped to `messages.upsert` only; status updates / reactions pass through (they may legitimately repeat per-wamid).

title: feat(workflows): BUFFER_MESSAGES action for debounced message aggregation
body:
## Summary

- New workflow action **`BUFFER_MESSAGES`** — coalesces multiple inputs by an arbitrary `groupKey` (default: lead phone) and forwards the aggregated payload to the next action (typically `RUN_AGENT`) after a debounce window.
- Prevents fragmented agent responses and wasted tokens when users send several messages in quick succession ("Oi" → "tudo bem?" → "gostaria de..." = 1 agent call, not 3).
- Channel-agnostic: `groupKey` is a free interpolable string (`{{trigger.remoteJid}}`, `{{lead.phone}}:{{agent.id}}`, etc.) — works with WhatsApp, webhooks, system events.

### How it works
1. First message for a `(workflowId, groupKey)` creates a `WorkflowWaitState` with `type='buffer'` and suspends the execution.
2. Subsequent messages on the same key **merge** into the existing bucket (workflow returns `_halt` — completes without running downstream), resetting the debounce timer up to `maxWaitMs` and `maxItems` caps.
3. On timeout, the existing `WaitStateResolutionService.processTimeouts()` cron flushes the bucket and resumes the original execution with `{ text, items, bucketSize, reason }` injected into the action's output.

### Why it's safe
- Reuses the existing `WorkflowWaitState` + cron infra from `WAIT_FOR_REPLY` — zero new scheduling machinery, state survives redeploys.
- Postgres `FOR UPDATE` row lock inside a Prisma transaction prevents race conditions under concurrent message arrival.
- New `_halt` signal implemented via Proxy+throw pattern preserves existing `_suspend` behavior.
- Schema change is purely additive: `groupKey TEXT NULL`, `firstStartedAt TIMESTAMP NULL`, new composite index.

title: fix(whatsapp-devices): make importDevice idempotent end-to-end
body:
## Context

Users hit `Falha ao importar device` in staging when importing a Meta app. Root cause (from staging logs):

```
[WhatsAppDevicesService] Failed to import BB device ...: App 884598687811823 already registered
[BbWppExceptionFilter] BB WPP error → 502: upstream status 409
```

BB's `POST /api/v1/apps` correctly returns 409 when the Meta App is already registered — but `importDevice` had no fallback, so any retry (or any case where the app was registered by a previous failed attempt) would bubble up as a 502. The problem was not just this one call — the whole flow was non-idempotent in multiple places.

## What this PR does

Makes the entire `importDevice` flow idempotent. Same input → same ACTIVE state, regardless of how many times it runs or whether prior attempts partially succeeded.

### Backend (`whatsapp-devices.service.ts`)

| Step | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `WhatsAppDevice` local row | `findFirst` + `create/update` (TOCTOU, allows duplicates) | `upsert` on `userId_bbDeviceId` unique constraint |
| `WppBizApp` creation | `POST /apps` → crash on 409 | `listWppBizApps` → found? `PATCH` secret : `POST`; also catch 409 on create as TOCTOU defense |
| Account-app association | Only on `!configured`; different app = silent no-op | Reassociate (with `warn` log) when `preStatus.wabaSubscription.appId !== appId` |
| Webhook verify token | `randomBytes(16)` each run | Persisted as `bbIngressVerifyToken` on first write, reused on retry |
| Dispatcher drift | `updateDispatcher` 404 → 502 | Catch `BbWppNotFoundError` → fall back to `createDispatcher` |
| Failure rollback | Delete local device + dispatcher | Rollback only `bbIngressStatus=PENDING` (next retry converges) |

### Prisma

- New field `bbIngressVerifyToken String?` on `WhatsAppDevice`
- New constraint `@@unique([userId, bbDeviceId])`

### Frontend (`ImportDeviceModal.tsx`)

Toast now surfaces `err.response.data.message` instead of the hardcoded `'Falha ao importar device'`. Generic string remains as fallback.

## Test plan

Unit tests (Jest, all passing — 26/26):

- [x] A — idempotent re-execution: 3 identical `importDevice` calls converge to ACTIVE, no duplicate rows
- [x] B — 409 on createWppBizApp (TOCTOU) → list-retry + updateWppBizApp called with secret
- [x] C — list-first skips create when app is already registered
- [x] D — dispatcher drift: `BbWppNotFoundError` on updateDispatcher → createDispatcher runs, new id persisted
- [x] E — secret rotation: updateWppBizApp called with new secret
- [x] F — reassociate account when preStatus points to a different app (warn log + updateAccountApp)

Manual QA (staging, post-migration):

- [ ] Cenário original do usuário (appId=884598687811823) → ACTIVE sem 409
- [ ] Re-import do mesmo device → idempotente
- [ ] Re-import com secret diferente → ACTIVE, secret atualizado no BB (verificar via `listWppBizApps`)
- [ ] Deletar dispatcher no BB, manter `bbIngressDispatcherId` local → re-import → ACTIVE (drift recovery)
- [ ] Frontend: forçar erro → toast mostra mensagem real do backend

## Migration

Staging painel DB has **zero duplicate `(userId, bbDeviceId)` rows**, so `@@unique` applies cleanly:

```sql
SELECT "userId", "bbDeviceId", COUNT(*) FROM "WhatsAppDevice"
WHERE "bbDeviceId" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
-- (0 rows)
```

After merge, apply with: `docker exec \$(docker ps -q -f name=painel-cliente-api) npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` on the target environment (same flow as documented in root `CLAUDE.md` common pitfall #16).

## Out of scope

- BB `wpp-business` service is intact (409 on duplicate POST is correct REST semantics; idempotency is the caller's concern).
- 21 pre-existing TypeScript errors in unrelated modules (`ai-assistant/tools/tools-executor.service.ts`, `workflows/validation/validators/variable.validator.spec.ts`) — confirmed present on master, not introduced here.

title: feat(bulk): DataTable bulk actions — delete, duplicate, export, update, archive, assign
body:
## Summary

Extends the DataTable system with bulk actions across 8 resources. Builds on the PR #192 bulk-import foundation: every bulk endpoint routes per-ID through the singular service methods via a shared `BulkService` primitive, so events / ACL / cascade behave exactly like single-resource operations.

Selected rows can now be **deleted**, **duplicated**, **exported**, **updated** (status / owner / custom field), **archived / activated** (isActive toggle), **assigned** (leads → owner), or have their **IDs copied** — with cross-page selection + "Selecionar todos os N filtrados" badge (Linear/HubSpot style).

### Non-negotiables
- **Tenant isolation**: every bulk endpoint pre-filters IDs through the same `getVisibleUserIds()` scope used by singular endpoints. IDs outside the caller's hierarchy land in `skipped[]` with `code: 'forbidden'`. Never distinguishes "not yours" from "not found" so we don't leak existence cross-tenant.
- **Critical bug fix**: `DataTableToolbar.tsx:137` was calling `action.onClick([])` instead of passing `selectedIds`. Every bulk action prior to this PR was a NO-OP.

## What ships

**Shared backend primitive** (`common/bulk/`)
- `BulkService.{deleteMany, duplicateMany, updateMany}` + `runPerId` primitive
- `BulkSelectorDto` / `BulkUpdateDto` (accepts `ids` OR `allFiltered + filters + search`)
- `BulkOperationResult<T>` with merged `skipped` from ACL + per-ID failures
- Hard cap of 500 IDs/request; larger → 400 (async path tracked as tech debt)
- p-limit(5) concurrency, same pattern as `importRows`

**Backend endpoints per module** (8 resources)
- Leads: bulk-delete / bulk-update (routes `{ assignedToId }` patches through `assign()`) / export accepts `?ids=`
- Workflows: bulk-delete / bulk-duplicate / bulk-update
- Agents: bulk-delete / bulk-duplicate / bulk-update
- Users: bulk-delete / bulk-update (drops caller's own ID before ACL to prevent self-delete)
- WhatsApp Devices: bulk-delete (forwards JWT for BB dispatcher cleanup) / bulk-update
- Custom Actions: bulk-delete / bulk-update
- Lead Types: bulk-delete / bulk-update (dependency errors when type in use)
- Capture Links: bulk-delete / bulk-update

**Shared frontend components** (`components/data-table/bulk/`)
- `BulkActionConfirmDialog` — type-DELETE gate for destructive ops + preview of 5 affected rows
- `BulkUpdateFieldModal` — curated single-field editor (prevents bulk-update foot-gun of silently overwriting heterogeneous rows)
- `BulkActionResultToast` + `BulkResultErrorsModal` — surfaces succeeded / skipped / failed + error table with typed codes
- `useBulkActions(config)` — declarative hook returning ready-to-use `BulkAction[]` for `<DataTable>`

**Cross-page selection** (`useDataTable`)
- `selectedIds` now persists across pagination changes (was replaced)
- `selectAllFiltered` virtual mode + `selectedTotalCount`
- Auto-drops the virtual mode when filters/search change so stale scopes can't silently delete the wrong rows
- "Selecionar todos os N filtrados" CTA appears in the toolbar when selection covers the current page and more filtered rows exist

**8 pages wired**: Leads, Workflows, Agents, Users, WhatsAppDevices, LeadTypes, CustomActions, CaptureLinks.

## Verified before this PR

- [x] **Backend unit tests: 376 pass in 14 suites** (`cd apps/painel-cliente-api && npx jest src/common/bulk src/modules/leads src/modules/workflows/workflows.service.spec.ts src/modules/agents src/modules/users src/modules/custom-actions src/modules/whatsapp-devices src/modules/capture-links src/modules/lead-types`)
- [x] **13 new BulkService tests** — success, partial failure, ACL-skipped merging, NestJS exception classification, 500-ID cap
- [x] **7 new ACL isolation tests on LeadsService** — master-sees-own, sub-user-cannot-reach-stranger, assign-routing-fires-richer-ACL, empty-patch-rejected, cap-enforced
- [x] **TypeScript clean** on both frontend (`apps/painel-cliente && npx tsc --noEmit`) and new backend code (pre-existing cross-workspace errors are unrelated)
- [x] **Manual API smoke against live Postgres + Redis** (dev API on port 8114):
  - 3 real + 1 fake bulk-delete → `{total:4, succeeded:3, skipped:1, failed:0}` with `code:'forbidden'` on the fake
  - Deleted IDs return 404 after the call
  - Bulk-update `{status: 'CONTACTED'}` persists in DB
  - Empty patch → 400; 501-ID request → 400
  - Workflows bulk-duplicate produces `name (cópia)` copies

## What reviewers should exercise (NOT yet verified by me)

- [ ] **UI smoke on the Leads page** — select 3 rows → Excluir → type EXCLUIR → confirm → toast + table refresh
- [ ] **UI smoke for bulk-update** — select 2 leads → Atualizar → pick Status → verify badge updates inline
- [ ] **UI smoke for cross-page selection** — select rows on page 1, navigate to page 2, verify the selection persists; exercise the "Selecionar todos os N filtrados" CTA when more pages exist

`docs/tech-debt/bulk-actions-async.md` — the 500-ID sync cap is fine for typical UX but hard-stops a handful of scenarios (large filtered deletes, high-fanout per-row ops). Plan is a BullMQ queue + SSE progress for selections ≥ 500 or `allFiltered === true`. Out of scope for this PR.

## Summary

- Expose active LLM **provider/model** in AI Assistant response + SSE events; render a color-coded badge next to the "Beta" chip so users can see when their own OpenAI token is actually being used.
- Add OpenAI **prompt caching** via `prompt_cache_key` (stable sha256 of system prompt + sorted tool names) and extract `cached_tokens` from the usage payload, bringing OpenAI to Claude's level for repeated prefixes.
- Pull in two small pre-existing fixes caught while typechecking: model-alias 404 when `OpenAIProvider` is constructed without an explicit model, and `percent is possibly undefined` in `WhatsAppStats.tsx`.

## Why

In prod a user set a per-tenant OpenAI key and assumed the switch hadn't taken effect because replies kept claiming to be Claude. Logs showed OpenAI was in fact being called — the model was hallucinating its identity from prior turns and the UI had no signal. Same session shows Claude paying ~1.7k tokens (cache hit) vs OpenAI paying ~6.6k (no caching). Prompt caching closes the cost gap; the badge removes the ambiguity.

## Changes

**Backend (`apps/painel-cliente-api`)**
- `dto/chat-response.dto.ts`: `provider?`, `model?`
- `dto/stream-event.dto.ts`: `CompleteEvent.aiMetadata?`

**SDK (`apps/panel-sdk`)**

**Frontend (`apps/painel-cliente`)**

### v2 vision behind these primitives

Today the workflow forms show `{{lead.name}}` raw tokens to non-technical

- A friendly **chip** (`👤 Nome do Lead`) color-coded by category (Trigger /

- A **chip-editable composite input** (`ChipEditableText`) where `{{...}}`
  tokens render as chips and text between them stays inline-editable,
  round-tripping cleanly to the raw template string on `onChange`.

- `VariableChip.tsx` — pill component (icon + friendly name + optional ✕).

title: fix(agents): strip leaked tool-call XML + allow hyphen in agent slug
body:
## Summary

Dois bugs detectados no smoke staging do PR #204 (VTEX Commerce Workflow):

1. **XML de tool call vazando na mensagem WhatsApp** — agente enviou mensagem ao cliente com `<function_calls><invoke>...<function_result>...</function_result>` literal.
2. **Slug com hyphen criado pelo install rejeitado ao editar via UI** — install gera `vtex-commerce-whatsapp-vtex-triage` mas o validator regex só aceita `[a-z0-9_]`.

## Fix 1 — XML leak (dupla trava)

### Causa raiz
Claude (Sonnet 4.x) tem prior forte de treinamento pro formato Claude Code harness (`<function_calls><invoke name="X"><parameter name="Y">...</parameter></invoke></function_calls><function_result>...</function_result>`). Quando system prompts descrevem tools usando pseudocódigo em backticks (ex: `` `execute_custom_action({ slug: "X", input: {...} })` ``), o modelo ativa esse prior e narra a chamada AS TEXT além de usar o tool_use nativo. O texto contendo XML entra em um bloco `text` legítimo, passa por `extractTextContent`, e vai pro usuário.

### Solução
- **Prompts**: reescritos 6 system prompts em `vtex-commerce-workflow.ts` — removido pseudocódigo, usada linguagem natural ("use a ferramenta X passando Y"), adicionado guardrail explícito "## Formato de resposta" proibindo XML/pseudocódigo.
- **Sanitização**: `claude.provider.ts#extractTextContent` agora strip-a com regex qualquer `<function_calls>`, `<function_result>`, `<invoke>`, `<parameter>` que escape. Cobre TODOS os agentes (VTEX + futuros).
- **Spec**: novo `claude.provider.spec.ts` (8 testes) cobrindo strip cases.

## Fix 2 — slug aceitar hyphen

- Install flow gera slug kebab-case mas `agentsService.create()` via service layer bypassa class-validator, permitindo criação. Edit via UI re-valida e falha.
- Hyphens já são padrão em workflow/agent template slugs. Amplia regex backend+frontend pra aceitar ambos.

**Arquivos**:
- `apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/agents/dto/create-agent.dto.ts` — `/^[a-z0-9_]+$/` → `/^[a-z0-9_-]+$/`
- `apps/painel-cliente/src/components/AgentModal.tsx` — mesmo
- `apps/painel-cliente/src/components/agents/AgentWizardModal.tsx` — mesmo

## Verificação

- 8/8 novos em `claude.provider.spec.ts`
- 58/58 tests do escopo (claude.provider + vtex-commerce-workflow + workflow-templates.spec + knowledge-router)
- Frontend TSC: 0 erros
- **Sem regressões** — 11 erros TSC + 10 testes falhando são todos pré-existentes (tools-executor `.data`/`.pagination`, OAUTH2/ML enum, bullmq missing, ollama integration, IAM guard spec) e já estavam presentes no master merge do PR #204.

## Referência criada

`memory/reference_iam_jwt_format.md` — documenta que JWT pra panel-cliente-api requer `sub=IAM_UUID`, não cuid local. Self-signed JWTs criam phantom users sem acesso a device/credencial. Descoberto ao debugar smoke staging (erro obscuro de SEND_MESSAGE era conseqüência de workflow criado sob phantom).

title: feat(auth): silent token refresh — stay logged in when access token expires
body:
## Summary

- Implementa refresh silencioso de token JWT no interceptor axios do painel
- Ao receber 401, tenta renovar via `POST /auth/refresh` e retenta a request original automaticamente
- Padrão mutex + fila: múltiplos 401 simultâneos disparam apenas 1 refresh, todas as requests ficam em fila e são retentadas juntas
- Logout forçado apenas quando o `refreshToken` também é inválido/ausente
- Guards de segurança: anti-loop em `/auth/refresh`, exclusão de endpoints WhatsApp e billing
- Adiciona `authStore.updateTokens()` para rotacionar tokens sem limpar sessão do usuário

- `authStore.updateTokens` — 6 testes (tokens, user, isAuthenticated, clearAuth, setAuth)
- Interceptor happy path — refresh OK, header correto, fallback de refreshToken
- Interceptor failure — clearAuth + redirect, não chama updateTokens
- Sem refreshToken — logout imediato sem tentar refresh
- Anti-loop — 401 em `/auth/refresh` não tenta refresh de novo
- Endpoints excluídos — WhatsApp, billing, mensagem "API token" não disparam refresh
- Concorrência — 1 só refresh para N requests simultâneos, todas resolvem/rejeitam juntas

body:
## Summary

Ships three backend pillars for smarter AI assistant behaviour and restores the floating bubble trigger that was replaced with a thin docked strip users found hard to discover.

### Backend — AI Intelligence Layer (\`ai-core\`)

- **Knowledge Base** — \`KnowledgeContributor\` plugin interface + \`CoreKnowledgeContributor\` with 7 embedded entries (workflow patterns, agent creation, entity relationships, anti-patterns). Relevant entries are injected into the system prompt based on user message keywords + active skills, capped at ~800 tokens.
- **Verification Contracts** — post-execution verification of mutating tool calls (\`create_lead\`, \`create_workflow\`, \`add_workflow_trigger\`, \`create_agent\`, \`add_agent_tool\`, \`update_lead\`, \`create_custom_action\`, \`finalize_workflow_diagram\`). A verify tool (\`get_*\`) is dispatched automatically and the outcome is appended to the tool result so the LLM can course-correct.
- **Session Compression** — triggers when estimated message tokens cross 8 000. Compresses everything except the last 5 turns into a 2-message summary (user + assistant) via the fast model. Live-tested drop: 22 681 → 8 201 prompt tokens on a long conversation (-63%).

### Backend — four silent bugs surfaced during live validation, now fixed

1. \`contracts.ts\` \`idField\` was used for both \"read id from tool result\" and \"param name for verify tool\". Split into \`resultIdField\` + \`verifyParamField\` — without this, verification of \`create_lead\`/\`create_agent\`/\`create_workflow\`/\`update_lead\` never ran end-to-end.
2. Tool results come wrapped as \`{ success, data }\` from the Panel SDK. The service read \`toolResult.id\` instead of \`toolResult.data.id\`, so every contract fell to the \"id not returned\" branch. Now unwraps explicitly.
3. \`onVerifyTool\` was only wired on the Claude provider. Added to \`OpenAICompatibleProvider\` so OpenAI / OpenRouter / Qwen / Ollama all get verification too.
4. \`toolResultsToOpenAI\` / \`toolResultsToAnthropic\` dropped \`verificationMessage\` during serialization, so the LLM never saw the outcome. Now appended.

### Frontend — AI Assistant bubble

- \`DashboardLayout\`: when collapsed, render \`<AIPanel />\` directly (no 44px docked container).
- \`AIPanel\`: collapsed state is now a circular FAB (purple, \`MdSmartToy\`) fixed bottom-right with tooltip + hover scale. Expanded state unchanged.

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit: **4 632 passing / 0 failing / 55 skipped** (48 external-API integration, 4 Ollama-dependent, 3 other legacy — all pre-existing, unrelated to this PR)
- [x] New specs: \`KnowledgeBaseService\` (10 tests), \`VerificationService\` (13), \`SessionCompressorService\` (11) = 34 new tests, 100% green
- [x] Live smoke: verification runs end-to-end — log shows \`🔍 Running verification for create_lead → get_lead\` + \`PASSED (id=...)\` after a real lead creation via \`POST /ai/chat\`

title: fix(ai-prompt): generic guards against silent substitution + destructive ops
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #227 (merged). During post-deploy validation in staging, the quality test surfaced a pattern where OpenAI would silently substitute a user-requested resource by a "similar-enough" existing one (e.g. user asks for a lead tipo "médico", AI uses CLIENTE because MEDICO doesn't exist). Anthropic handled the same case correctly (asks first).

This is a generic pattern — not lead-specific — so the mitigation lives in BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT where it benefits every skill, every tool, every provider.

## Changes

- `base-prompt.ts` — two rule tightenings:
  1. **Novo bullet em "REGRA CRÍTICA"**: "NUNCA substitua um recurso pedido pelo usuário por outro parecido." Aplica a leads, tipos, agentes, workflows, webhooks, custom actions, capture links, devices, credenciais.
  2. **Rule #2 "Confirme ações destrutivas"** reforçada com regras concretas: listar itens afetados com contagem, pedir confirmação explícita, não inferir de ambíguo, em bulk >10 itens o número tem que aparecer no texto da pergunta.

Cost: ~80 extra tokens/request para o main completion (router não usa esse prompt).
Chitchat: 760 → ~820 input tokens.

- `scripts/ai-token-bench.ts` — agora dumpa um `.jsonl` paralelo ao `.csv` com request+response completos por call, para feedback loop offline.

## Validation — same quality suite against stg pre/post

| Provider | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic | 14/14 (100%) | 14/14 (100%) | ceiling (no change) |
| OpenAI | 10/14 (71%) | **14/14 (100%)** | **+29 points** |

Q6 ("adiciona um médico" — MEDICO type doesn't exist) now gets the right behaviour in OpenAI too:
> "Como não temos um tipo de lead específico para médicos..." (lists existing, asks to create)

Before the fix OpenAI silently used CLIENTE. After the fix it pauses and asks.

Noticed OpenAI Q7 turn 1 entered a 10x loop on `list_available_agent_tools` before aborting with "operação muito complexa" (109k input tokens on that single turn). Turn 2 recovered → overall PASS. Likely a prompt interaction to investigate separately.

title: fix(ai): generic tool-call loop guard + max-iter hardening
body:
## Summary

Generic per-turn loop guard for LLM tool-calling, applied uniformly to both `ClaudeProvider` and `OpenAICompatibleProvider`. Resolves the Q7 OpenAI postfix regression where the LLM looped 10× on `list_available_agent_tools({})` and burned 109 069 input tokens in a single turn.

- **Helper:** `ToolCallDedup` compares `(name, canonicalHash(args))` of the current tool call against the immediately previous call. Match ⇒ skip the executor and return a `TOOL_CALL_LOOP_DETECTED` synthetic result so the LLM can recover (try a different tool, ask for context, or finalize with text).
- **Providers:** Both `Claude` + `OpenAI-compatible` integrate the dedup per-turn (one instance per `completeWithTools`).
- **MAX_ITERATIONS:** 10 → 6 in both providers.
- **Max-iter message:** now lists tools used (via `summarizeToolCalls`, e.g. \`list_x×3, create_y\`) instead of the generic "operação ficou muito complexa".

## Summary
- Api keys whose authenticated user has `PANEL_CROSS_TENANT` may now override the request's \`organizationId\` via the \`X-Target-Organization-Id\` header

- Invalid UUID → \`400\` (short-circuits before role lookup)
- No header → no-op (regression-safe)
- Role lookup uses \`Container.get(PrismaClient)\` directly (not \`AssociationRepository\`) so the middleware works in standalone modules where IAM module isn't registered

title: fix(billing): recalibrate plan includedUnits — kilotoken bug + worst-case margins
body:
## Summary

- **Bug**: `seed-billing.ts` wrote `includedUnits` for `ai-tokens-*` as raw tokens (e.g. 50000), but the meter records `Math.ceil(rawTokens / 1000)` in agents/ai-assistant services. Free plan had effectively 50M real tokens instead of 50K — a **1000x gap** that silences the billing guard.
- **Fix**: recalibrate all plan limits to kilotokens with worst-case-balanced COGS (Sonnet R\$0,06/kilo + WhatsApp 30% marketing R\$0,12/msg). Margin target: Free ≥ −R\$5, paid plans ≥ 40%.
- **Professional**: price raised R\$497 → R\$997 to preserve WA 3000 quota and hit 47% margin at worst case.

### Before vs After

| Plan | Price | AI-Act (kilos) | AI-Plat (kilos) | WA msgs | Margin worst |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Free | R\$0 | 50000 → **20** | 20000 → **10** | 100 → **20** | −R\$4 |
| Starter | R\$149 | 300000 → **300** | 100000 → **80** | 750 → **400** | 52% |
| Growth | R\$297 | 800000 → **800** | 250000 → **200** | 1500 → **800** | 45% |
| Professional | **R\$997** (was R\$497) | 2000000 → **2000** | 500000 → **400** | 3000 (kept) | 47% |

## Wave 1 scope (this PR)

- Seed recalibrated + explicit unit comment in `PLAN_DEFINITIONS`
- Regression tests: 3 kilotoken contract tests in `usage-meter.service.spec.ts`, 1 quota breach test (Free 21 kilos → 402) in `billing-limit.guard.spec.ts`
- Full plan + rollout waves + curl/DB update strategy: `docs/plans/2026-04-21-billing-quotas-recalibration.md`

## Wave 2 (NOT in this PR — needs manual coordination)

Seed idempotency skips existing plans in BB. After deploy, stg/prod plan items need manual update via:
1. curl PATCH to BB (if endpoint exists)
2. UPDATE SQL on `subscription_plan_items` + Redis flush (fallback)
3. BB admin UI (last resort)

See §2.3 of plan doc for full commands. Shadow mode 7 days recommended if \`BILLING_ENFORCE_LIMITS=true\` in prod.

title: feat(chats): persist outbound WhatsApp messages in chat history
body:
## Summary

- **Outbound messages now visible**: CRM chat `sendMessage`/`sendMedia` persist to `Message` table immediately after BB send with `correlationId` placeholder + `deliveryStatus='pending'` — frontend's existing `fetchMessages` call shows the pending row on send.
- **Echo reconciliation**: when BB echoes back with the real `wamid` (fromMe=true), `MessageProcessor` finds the pending placeholder (by `chatId + fromMe + pending` FIFO within 60s), swaps `messageId → wamid`, flips status to `'sent'`. Single row, no duplicates.
- **Sub-second latency**: `BbEventsController` now calls `EventProcessorService.processEventNow` inline (fire-and-forget) so messages land in the DB within seconds instead of up to 60s cron lag. Cron remains as a fallback.
- **No double-billing**: `MessageProcessor` skips meter for `fromMe=true` (OutboundMessagePersistence already metered at send time with `idempotencyHint='outbound-<correlationId>'`).

## Why

Before this change, `ChatsService.sendMessage/sendMedia` only called BB WPP Business and returned the `correlationId` — nothing was written to `Message`. Users sent messages in the CRM chat UI but the message never appeared until the next refresh, and only if the 1-minute `EventProcessor` cron had picked up the BB echo (`messages.upsert` with `fromMe=true`). This broke the "conversas salvam mensagens outgoing" UX.

## Schema

New column `Message.correlationId String? @unique` + index on `deliveryStatus`. Migration `20260421233617_message_outbound_correlation`.

## Deferred to follow-up PRs

- **Workflow `SEND_MESSAGE`/`SEND_MEDIA` direct-save** — avoided the chat-resolution race with `MessageProcessor`. Sync echo processing (this PR) already eliminates the lag for workflow-sent messages via the echo path.
- **Frontend status indicator** (pending/sent/delivered/read checkmarks) — `chatsStore.sendMessage` already does `fetchMessages` after send, so placeholder shows immediately; transition to `'sent'` is UX polish.
- **Playwright e2e** — needs live BB + WhatsApp device. Unit coverage (4752 passed) exercises persistence + reconciliation.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: 4752 passed, 0 failed (includes 12 new tests in `outbound-message-persistence.service.spec.ts` + `message-processor.spec.ts`; +4 tests in `chats.service.spec.ts`; updated `bb-events.controller.spec.ts` with `EventProcessorService` mock).

- [ ] Smoke: envie uma mensagem pela UI de chat em stg → inspecione DB → `Message` com `fromMe=true`, `correlationId`, `deliveryStatus='pending'` criado em <1s → segundos depois: `messageId=wamid.*`, `deliveryStatus='sent'`.
