## Summary
Reverts the Parte B changes merged via PR #241 (the X-Target-Organization-Id + per-tenant bbOrganizationId work).

**Reason:** I misread the BB billing design. Catalisa's BB is provider-scoped by design — every tenant's billing account lives under the provider's org (today always Catalisa platform). The shared \`bbOrganizationId\` wasn't a bug; it was intentional. My fix broke plan lookup in \`createSubscription\`, breaking the signup wizard for new tenants.

**Confirmed in stg:** after Parte B + registration, \`createSubscription\` → BB returns \`SubscriptionPlan not found\` because the plan lives in Catalisa platform org but the sub request arrives with \`X-Target-Organization-Id: tenant_iam_org\`.

## What gets reverted
- \`billing-client.service.ts\` → \`getAuthHeaders()\` no longer accepts targetOrgId
- \`auth.service.ts\` → \`register()\` uses \`CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID\` again for \`bbOrgId\` (was using \`iamOrg.id\`)
- \`organizations.service.ts\` → \`getBBIds\` returns original shape, no iamOrganizationId fallback
- Deletes \`20260421_backfill_bb_organization_id.sql\`
- Spec files restored

## What stays
- PR #239 (admin-clients UI) — **unchanged, still in prod**
- Parte A phases 1-6 — untouched

## Companion
BB side: revert PR on building-blocks-v2 (see linked PR)

## Post-merge operational step
Run this SQL once in stg + prod DBs to reset tenants that got backfilled:
\`\`\`sql
UPDATE organizations
SET "bbOrganizationId" = 'b0000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001'
WHERE "bbOrganizationId" = "iamOrganizationId";
\`\`\`

title: fix(workflows): scope $lead lookup by tenant to prevent cross-tenant leak
body:
## Summary
- **Bug crítico de segurança**: `ContextEnrichmentService.loadLeadByPhone/loadLeadById/enrichWithLead` consultava leads sem filtro de `ownerId`, retornando o lead mais recente de QUALQUER tenant. Workflow do tenant operacao-investimentos resolvia `{{$lead.name}}` pra um lead da Catalisa quando ambos tinham leads com o mesmo phone.
- **Fix mínimo + cirúrgico**: assinaturas exigem `ownerId` (TS-enforced), filtro `ownerId IN (tenantUserIds)` via `TenantHierarchyService.getTenantUserIds()` que já existe e é a mesma semântica do hardening cross-tenant de 2026-04-13. PANEL_ADMIN preserva cross-tenant intencional.
- **Cobre TODOS os trigger paths**: manual canvas, BB inbound webhook, scheduled, sub-workflow — todos convergem em `execute()`.

## Evidência (produção)

```
[22:27, 21/04/2026] K.: oi
[22:31, 21/04/2026] operacao-investimentos 0481: Olá Prospect VTEX Day, eu sou o Tom da operacao-investimentos!
                                A C6 Seg solicitou o contato com você...
```

Branding "Tom da operacao-investimentos" (correto, tenant operacao-investimentos) + nome "Prospect VTEX Day" (lead da Catalisa, **tenant errado**).

## Root cause

`apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/workflows/services/context-enrichment.service.ts:95-104` (pré-fix):
```ts
const lead = await this.prisma.lead.findFirst({
  where: { phone: normalizedPhone },   // ← sem ownerId
  orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' },
});
```

Hardening cross-tenant de 2026-04-13 cobriu `LeadsService.findAll/findOne/update` (REST). Caminho de enrichment do workflow é "lazy/interno" e ficou sem revisão.

## Files changed

- `context-enrichment.service.ts` — assinaturas + queries + helper `buildTenantOwnerWhere`
- `execution.service.ts:172` — propaga `workflow.userId` em `enrichWithLead`
- `context-enrichment.service.spec.ts` — 13 novos casos
- `package.json` — bump 1.15.0 → 1.15.1

`workflows.module.ts` NÃO precisou mudar (`UsersModule` já importado, `TenantHierarchyService` já exportado).

## Test plan

### Unit (já verde local)
- [x] 27/27 testes passam (`npm run test -- context-enrichment.service.spec`)
- [x] 13 casos novos cobrem: tenant isolation A/B, hierarquia master+sub-users, PANEL_ADMIN passthrough, defense-in-depth, plumbing

### Smoke real em staging (próximo passo)
- [ ] Deploy via `npm run ship:staging painel-cliente-api`
- [ ] Reproduzir cenário: 2 tenants em stg com lead de mesmo phone, executar workflow tenant A do canvas → deve interpolar lead A (não B)
- [ ] Workflow disparado por BB webhook real (mensagem inbound) — confirmar lead correto
- [ ] Workflow sem lead no tenant correto → `$lead === null`, mensagem interpola vazio (não vaza outro tenant)

### Adjacent audit (clean)
- [x] `opt-out-detection.service.ts:28` — JÁ filtra por `ownerId`
- [x] `follow-up-scheduler.service.ts:84` — `lead.id` vem de query escopada upstream

## Plan B (follow-up separado, não bloqueia esta PR)

Tolerância a formato de phone (`+55...` vs `55...` vs format) — `loadLeadByPhone` ainda faz match exato. Padrão correto está em `lead-lookup.util.ts:65-74`. Trigger pra ativar: se algum workflow legítimo passar a falhar com `$lead === null` quando o lead existe no tenant correto mas com prefixo diferente.

## Risk register

- **Falsos negativos**: workflow legítimo deixa de achar lead → sintoma visível (`{{$lead.name}}` vira vazio), Plan B cobre
- **Performance**: índices `Lead(ownerId)` + `Lead(phone)` já existem; bitmap intersection do Postgres é eficiente
- **Edge case "user deletado"**: ELIMINADO — `Workflow.userId` é NOT NULL com `onDelete: Cascade` (verificado no schema)

title: feat(agents): wall-clock budget + retry + circuit breaker for RUN_AGENT
body:
## Context

Agents executados em workflows (ação `RUN_AGENT`) estavam estourando tempo em produção sem corte determinístico. O único teto em jogo era o timeout do SDK Anthropic (30s), aplicado por request HTTP — não pelo loop inteiro. Uma execução com 15 iterações de tool call podia pendurar o worker por 3-5 minutos sem nada cortar.

Esse PR adiciona **4 camadas de proteção** herdadas automaticamente por qualquer agente (sem opt-in):

1. **Wall-clock budget** com cascata `action > agent > env (60s default)` + AbortController até o SDK
2. **Per-tool timeout** (30s default) — tool travada retorna `TOOL_TIMEOUT` sintético, LLM continua
3. **Error classifier + retry seletivo** — só timeout/network/5xx, nunca 4xx, uma vez com 50% do budget
4. **Circuit breaker** por `(agentId, workflowId)` em Redis — 5 falhas em 10min → open por 5min

## Summary

- Per-agent budget: `Agent.executionBudgetMs` (nullable, 10000–600000ms, range validado no DTO)
- Per-action override: `config.timeoutMs` + `config.retryOnTimeout` na RUN_AGENT action
- 38 unit tests novos, **4858 total passing (0 failures)**
- Smoke manual end-to-end: CREATE/UPDATE/validation/clear/DELETE todos verificados via curl
- Migration aditiva (ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS + CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS) — safe em shared DB
- Frontend: form do agente + node do canvas + badges de status (timeout/breaker_open) + histórico

## Technical highlights

- **Cooperative cancel até o SDK**: AbortSignal propagado pelo `LLMCompletionOptions.signal` → `this.client.messages.create(req, { signal })`. Interrompe socket em trânsito, não só boundaries.
- **`executeWithRetry` aborta durante backoff**: antes segurava 60s mesmo com signal abortado; agora cancela o sleep via `signal.addEventListener('abort')`.
- **Distinção `null` vs `undefined` em PATCH**: `executionBudgetMs: null` limpa override, `undefined` não toca.
- **Breaker fail-open**: se Redis cair, retorna `{open: false}` — perder proteção temporária é melhor que bloquear todos os agentes.
- **Bug achado pelo próprio teste**: `recordSuccess` não limpava counters parciais quando estado ainda era `closed` — 4 falhas ao longo de 10h + 1 sucesso + 1 falha abriria breaker errado. Fix + teste.

## Files (22 changed, +1232 / -44)

**Backend (9 files, 3 new):**
- `prisma/schema.prisma` + migration SQL (aditiva)
- `run-agent.handler.ts` — budget cascade, AbortController, retry seletivo, breaker gate
- `agent-executor.service.ts` — aceita `signal`/`traceId`, persist `status='timeout'` com `timedOutStage`
- `claude.provider.ts` — SDK honra signal, per-tool `Promise.race`, abort durante backoff
- `llm-provider.interface.ts` — `signal` + `traceId` em `LLMCompletionOptions`
- `agents.module.ts` — registra `AgentCircuitBreakerService`
- `agents.service.ts` + `create-agent.dto.ts` — persistir/validar `executionBudgetMs`
- **NEW** `agent-circuit-breaker.service.ts` + spec

- `NodeExecutionBadge.tsx` — badges para `timeout` (laranja) / `breaker_open` (vermelho)
- `execution-utils.tsx` — novos status configs
- `AgentHistoryTab.tsx` — UI distinta por status (mostra `timedOutStage`)

title: fix(workflows): async dispatch via BullMQ + AI_HUB_AGENT non-text skip + subscriber resilience
body:
## Summary

Three coordinated fixes for the production timeout reports on agent flows and bulk-import-driven workflows.

### Frente A — BullMQ workflow-execution queue (impacto principal)

`EventListenerService` used to `await WorkflowExecutionService.execute()` inline inside the Redis Pub/Sub `pmessage` callback. With one api replica that drained one workflow at a time per tenant — bulk imports of N leads fanned out into N `LEAD_CREATED` events processed serially. Last leads appeared to time out because their workflow only started minutes after the import.

New \`WorkflowExecutionQueueService\` registers a BullMQ \`Queue\` + \`Worker\` in the same NestJS process. Producer adds a lightweight \`{ workflowId, payload, triggerId }\` job; worker re-fetches the workflow from Prisma and delegates to \`WorkflowExecutionService.execute()\`. Subscriber returns immediately — backpressure on Pub/Sub gone.

Behind \`WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_VIA_QUEUE\` flag (default OFF) for safe rollout. Concurrency tunable via \`WORKFLOW_WORKER_CONCURRENCY\` (default 5). Defense in depth: if \`queue.add()\` throws, listener falls back to inline execution so events are never lost.

### Frente B — AI_HUB_AGENT skip on empty message

Audio/image/sticker inbound messages interpolate \`$helpers.getMessageText(...)\` to empty string, making the handler return \`success:false\` with \`'AI_HUB_AGENT requires message in config'\`. The CORRETOR tenant logs were full of these. Handler now returns \`success:true, data:{skipped:true, reason:'non-text-message'}\`. Downstream actions can branch on \`output.skipped\`.

### Frente C — Subscriber Redis resilience

\`EventListenerService\` raw \`new Redis()\` didn't match \`createResilientRedis\` factory used elsewhere. Added \`createResilientRedisSubscriber\` (psubscribe-friendly: \`enableOfflineQueue:true\`, \`maxRetriesPerRequest:null\`) and migrated listener to it.

title: feat(wpp): bridge driver message events to repos and SSE
body:
## Summary

Today \`BaileysDriver\` emits 11 message-domain events but only \`connection.update\` and \`creds.update\` have listeners. Result: \`wpp_messages\`, \`wpp_chats\`, \`wpp_contacts\`, \`wpp_groups\`, \`wpp_group_participants\` and \`wpp_message_reactions\` stay empty in production, and SSE clients on \`/wpp/events/:organizationId\` never see anything after pairing.

This PR wires the driver event stream into the rest of the WPP module:

1. **Persistence** — each event is written to its matching repository (fire-and-forget; failures warn-log and never crash the driver socket).
2. **SSE pub/sub** — each event is published as a JSON envelope on Redis channel \`wpp-events:{organizationId}\`, which \`SseHandler\` already subscribes to.

### Events handled (all 11)

| Event | Persistence | SSE envelope type |
|---|---|---|
| \`messages.upsert\` | \`MessageRepository.upsertByKeyId\` + \`ChatRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.message.upsert\` |
| \`messages.update\` | \`MessageRepository.update\` (status/ack) | \`wpp.message.update\` |
| \`messages.delete\` | \`MessageRepository.update({deletedAt})\` (soft-delete) | \`wpp.message.delete\` |
| \`messages.reaction\` | \`MessageReactionRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.message.reaction\` |
| \`chats.upsert\` / \`chats.update\` | \`ChatRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.chat.upsert\` / \`wpp.chat.update\` |
| \`contacts.upsert\` / \`contacts.update\` | \`ContactRepository.upsert\` | \`wpp.contact.upsert\` / \`wpp.contact.update\` |
| \`groups.upsert\` | chat upsert + group create/update + participants upsert | \`wpp.group.upsert\` |
| \`groups.update\` | \`GroupRepository.update\` (skips when group unknown) | \`wpp.group.update\` |
| \`group-participants.update\` | \`GroupParticipantRepository.upsert\` (add/promote/demote) or \`markLeft\` (remove) | \`wpp.group.participants.update\` |

### Architecture

- **\`src/wpp/services/message-event-mapper.ts\`** — pure functions that translate driver event payloads into repo inputs and SSE envelopes. No I/O, no \`await\`, easy to unit-test (21 tests).
- **\`src/wpp/services/session-manager.ts\`** — new private \`wireMessageEventListeners(driver, orgId, deviceId)\` called from the existing \`wireEventListeners\`. Each handler is wrapped in \`try/catch\` so a thrown mapper or repo cannot kill the driver event loop.
- **Container** (\`src/shared/container/modules/wpp.ts\`) — \`SessionManager\` now receives the six message-domain repos. Constructor params are optional (default undefined), so existing unit tests don't have to change.

### Tests

- \`tests/unit/wpp/services/message-event-mapper.test.ts\` — 21 mapper unit tests
- \`tests/unit/wpp/services/session-manager-bridge.test.ts\` — 24 listener wiring tests, one per event type plus skip/fault-tolerance paths
- \`tests/unit/wpp/integration/baileys-pipeline.test.ts\` — extended with 1 new assertion proving the full chain (mocked socket -> real BaileysDriver -> real SessionManager -> mocked repo + Redis publish)

WPP suite total: **410 passing** (was 364, +46 new).

### Out-of-scope (not done here)

- No new repositories, no schema changes.
- No driver code touched.
- No PATCH/DELETE endpoints, no replay/DLQ for failed persists.
- The persisted-row events (\`MESSAGE_RECEIVED\`/etc.) on the existing \`EventPublisher\` Redis Streams topic are NOT republished; the SSE channel is the only fan-out, since SSE uses raw \`subscribe\`/\`message\` and the streams topic has no SSE consumer.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on \`bun run test:unit\` (wpp suite passes locally)
- [ ] After merge, run smoke script (\`scripts/smoke-baileys-qr.ts\`) and verify rows appear in \`wpp_messages\` / \`wpp_chats\` and an SSE client connected to \`/wpp/events/:organizationId\` receives \`wpp.message.upsert\` events
- [ ] Confirm \`wpp_groups\` and \`wpp_group_participants\` populate when the device is added to a group

## Summary

Lazy media download via file-storage BB + 4 architectural fixes uncovered along the way. Builds on the message-bridge that landed in PR #117.

## Highlights

### 1. Lazy media download (commits 1–10)
Operator hits `GET /wpp/api/v1/messages/media/:messageId`. On cache miss, route enqueues `wpp:download-media`. Worker consumer pulls bytes via `driver.downloadMedia` (Baileys `downloadMediaMessage` against the persisted protobuf), uploads via the new `IFileStorageFacade` (Local + Remote impls — same pattern as webhooks-engine/decision-engine facades), persists the resulting `mediaFileId`, completes the operation. title: fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions actually re-establishes driver sessions
body:
## Summary
`restoreActiveSessions` was a no-op. It only wrote a `reconnect_attempt` row to `wpp_connection_logs` and returned — no driver instantiated, no Baileys socket opened. Workers booted "running" with an empty in-memory sessions Map while DB still showed devices as `open`. Every worker restart silently dropped every previously-paired session until someone hit `POST /devices/:id/reconnect` manually.

PR #122 (`fix(wpp): restoreActiveSessions queries devices across all orgs`) fixed the query side, but the actual restore step has been a no-op since the very first wpp commit (`f9fbd92`).

## Fix
Each restored row now goes through `getOrCreateSession` after the log is written. That fires `wireEventListeners`, opens the Baileys socket, and registers the driver in `this.sessions` for the running worker process. The driver's `connection.update` event then flips `wpp_devices.status` back to `open` on success, or to `closed` with an error code if auth was revoked remotely.

Per-device errors are caught and warn-logged — one stale auth (`LoggedOut`/401) does not block the rest from restoring.

## Local validation
Cold-booted the worker against a paired local device:

```
[INFO] Restoring active WPP sessions count: 1
[INFO] WPP session restored
state_change → connecting   (driver wired)
state_change → connecting
state_change → open         ← real Baileys socket
```

`wpp_devices.updatedAt` advanced. `wpp_connection_logs` shows the full state-change sequence. Time from boot to `open` was ~2.3s.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run vitest run tests/unit/wpp/services/session-manager.test.ts` — 33/33 pass (+2 new: driver actually invoked, per-device error isolation).
- [ ] Deploy to staging, watch `wpp_devices.updatedAt` of any pre-existing `status=open` row advance after worker boot. If existing staging devices fail with 401 (auth removed via WhatsApp UI), pair a fresh device and re-validate.

title: feat(wpp): distribute restoreActiveSessions via Redis Streams across replicas
body:
## Summary

- **Coordinator-elect** (`SET NX EX wpp:restore-coordinator`, 60s TTL) so exactly ONE replica reads the DB and fans out one `SESSION_RESTORE` job per device into the existing Redis Stream — eliminating the duplicate `reconnect_attempt` log rows + duplicate Baileys socket attempts that occur when N>1 worker replicas all run the restore loop in parallel.
- **Stream-driven distribution** via the existing `WppQueues.SESSION_RESTORE` consumer group (`wpp-consumers`) — each device job is delivered to exactly one worker, splitting reconnect load across the replica fleet instead of every replica fighting over every device.
- **Per-device idempotency** preserved via `wpp:reconnect-lock:{org}:{device}` (SET NX EX, 30s) inside the new `restoreSessionFromStream` path, so consumer-side stream redelivery (consumer crash before XACK) is safe — the lock + the in-memory `this.sessions.has` short-circuit guarantee no duplicate sockets even under worst-case race.
- New `RedisService.setIfAbsent(key, value, ttl)` helper wrapping `SET NX EX`.

## Why not the previous "lock per device only" design

With N replicas each running their own restore loop, even with the per-device lock the losers still did the DB scan and wrote the `reconnect_attempt` log row before observing the lock. The coordinator-elect cuts this to one DB scan and one set of log rows total, regardless of replica count.

## Local validation (3 real devices, 2 workers)

title: fix(ai-providers): PR A — cache always-on + parallel tool exec (Claude/OpenAI/Ollama)

## Summary

PR A from the [Phase 0 emergency roadmap](../blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md). Targets the **8-10s latency regression** (was 2-3s) reported in prod after PRs #256-#259.

Three fixes shipped together — no behavior changes for callers, only structural improvements to the LLM provider tool-loop.

## Changes

### A1 — Claude prompt cache on EVERY iteration
- `claude.provider.ts:238` was `enableCaching && iteration === 1` — gated cache to iter 1 only
- For AI Assistant (152 tools, ~45k tokens) with 3-5 iterations, this forced 3-5× re-tokenization
- Fix: drop the iteration gate. Anthropic's 5-min ephemeral TTL covers a full multi-turn flow, so iter 2+ hits the prefix written on iter 1

### A2 — ONE cache_control on the LAST tool (prefix breakpoint)
- Was setting cache_control on the **last 3 tools** (~880 lines), leaving the first N-3 uncached
- `cache_control` is a **prefix breakpoint** in Anthropic's API — a single one on the last tool caches the entire tools block
- For AI Assistant: 152 tools cached vs 3 before

### A3 — Cross-provider parallel tool execution (helper extraction)
- New `providers/utils/tool-batch-runner.ts`:
  - **Pre-pass (sync):** record fatigue + check dedup in input order
  - **Parallel pass:** `Promise.all` with per-branch try/catch + cancellation + optional per-tool wall-clock timeout
  - **Post-pass (serial, in input order):** record dedup with actual result, run `onVerifyTool` (must stay serial — stateful), apply optional smart-truncation
- Applied to **all 3 providers** (`claude.provider.ts`, `openai-compatible.provider.ts`, `ollama.provider.ts`)
- Anthropic and OpenAI both emit multiple `tool_use` per turn explicitly because they're independent — running them serially turned 5×2s into 10s wall-time when 2s would do
- Net **-210 lines** across the 3 providers (DRY win)

## Tests

- **13 new** in `tool-batch-runner.spec.ts`: parallelism (`maxInflight=3`), order preservation, fatigue/dedup short-circuit, cancellation, per-tool timeout, `onVerifyTool` stays serial, smart-truncate flag, error isolation, callbacks
- **9 new** in `claude.provider.cache-strategy.spec.ts`:
  - cache_control on system on EVERY iteration including **iter 2 regression test**

title: fix(ai-providers): PR B — cross-provider narration guard + Claude tool_choice
body:
## Summary

PR B from the [Phase 0 emergency roadmap](../blob/master/docs/plans/2026-05-02-ai-perf-and-gerundio-roadmap.md). Eliminates the **gerundio regression** (model says "vou começar / um momento / vou tentar" without emitting `tool_use`) across **Claude / openai-compatible / Ollama / Gemini** via a shared helper. Also adds explicit `tool_choice` to Claude, mirroring the pattern OpenAI-compat and Gemini already use.

## Changes

### B1-3 — Shared `narration-guard.ts` helper
Lives in `providers/utils/narration-guard.ts`. Pure-function decision: `shouldRetryForNarration({ iteration, finalText, hasTools, messages, retriesUsed }) → { retry, reason, systemMessage, routerMiss }`.

**Three failure modes of the original Claude-only guard fixed:**

1. **Was iter 1 only** — narration on iter 2+ (after the model received tool_results) slipped through. Now fires on EVERY iteration with a per-session retry cap (default 2).
2. **Required `hasTools`** — when the upstream skill router returned an empty tools array on a clearly action-demanding prompt ("cria um lead pra mim"), the guard skipped silently. Now `isActionIntentMessage(userText)` fires the guard with a different system message AND emits a `routerMiss` log.error for upstream observability.
3. **Regex narrow** — the original 5 verbs missed 11 prod variants. Widened to: `vou (começar/criar/fazer/chamar/iniciar/tentar/precisar/buscar/listar/verificar/consultar/preparar/enviar/montar/configurar/atualizar/cadastrar)`, `primeiro vou`, `preciso primeiro`, `um (momento/instante/segundinho/segundo/minutinho/minuto)`, `só um (instante/momento/...)`, `aguarde`, `já vou`, `começando`, `iniciando`, `estou começando`, `deixa (só) eu`, `agora vou X`, `agora mesmo`. Verb-anchored to avoid false positives on past tense ("comecei ontem") or unrelated phrases ("vou ali").

**Applied to:**
- `claude.provider.ts` (replacing inline guard)
- `openai-compatible.provider.ts` (Gemini inherits — `getToolChoiceOverride` was forcing required on iter 1, now also catches narration on iter 2+ from text-only fallbacks)
- `ollama.provider.ts`

Same regex + same decision logic across all providers — `cross-provider-parity.spec.ts` passes.

### B4 — Claude `tool_choice` (mirroring openai-compatible:135,252 + Gemini)

New private `getToolChoiceForIteration(options, iteration, forceAnyOnLater)`:
- Iter 1 with tools: `{ type: 'auto', disable_parallel_tool_use: false }`
- Iter ≥ 2 with tools: `{ type: 'any', disable_parallel_tool_use: false }` when `AI_FORCE_TOOL_CHOICE_ANY=true`, else `'auto'`
- Without tools: omit entirely

Gated behind env flag (default OFF) so first prod rollout preserves legacy. Plan: turn on in stg, validate via bench, ramp prod.

## Tests

- **61 new** in `narration-guard.spec.ts`: NARRATION_RE variant matrix (24 must-match + 9 must-NOT-match), `isActionIntentMessage` (11 actions + 5 non-actions + undefined), `getLastUserText` (string/array content/skip non-user/empty), `shouldRetryForNarration` (8 scenarios incl. retry caps + iter 2+ + routerMiss + chitchat passthrough)
- **6 new** in `claude.provider.tool-choice.spec.ts`: default off → auto everywhere, flag on → auto iter 1 + any iter 2/3, no tool_choice when no tools
- **1 updated** in `claude.provider.narration-guard.spec.ts`: regression test "TRIGGERS retry on iter 2 when narration appears AFTER tool_use" — was validating the bug, now validates the fix
- **All 199 ai-core tests pass** (17 suites)

Same as PR #262 — flagged for tracking, not in scope here:
- `workflows.service.ts`, `chats.service.ts`, `messages.service.ts`, `run-agent.handler.ts` — Prisma client lag and implicit-any issues
- `claude.provider.spec.ts:19` ConfigService vs ClaudeProviderConfig
- `narration-guard.spec.ts` and `loop-guard.spec.ts` fixtures missing required `systemPrompt` (pre-existing)

## Expected impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Gerundio responses / 100 sessions (estimated) | ~12 | **<1** |
| iter 2+ narration coverage | 0% | **100% (all 4 providers)** |
| skill-router miss observability | silent | **logger.error w/ routerMiss flag** |

title: fix(ai-assistant): hydrate cached skills on implicit selection turns
body:
## Summary

URGENT prod fix. AI Assistant was hallucinating tool execution when user sent short follow-up messages mid-task ("vamos usar o 3414" after a workflow setup). Captured live in prod 2026-05-04 11:05 BRT (workflow adega session): turn 1 called 2 tools correctly, turns 2-4 called ZERO tools but model wrote "Instalado! ID: wfl_cmlz..." with fabricated CUIDs.

## Root cause

`apps/painel-cliente-api/src/modules/ai-assistant/ai-assistant.service.ts:152-197`. Intent router classifies short messages with no domain keywords as `chitchat` → `toolsToUse=[]`. Pre-existing Fix #4 (lines 160-171) hydrates `sessionSkillsCache` ONLY when `detectConfirmation()` matches explicit patterns (`sim`, `ok`, `pode`, `👍`). Real users naturally say `"vamos usar o 3414"`, `"esse aí"`, `"o 11999..."` — these are SELECTIONS, not confirmations → fail `detectConfirmation` → tools dropped → model hallucinates.

Bug latent since commit `046f7260` (April 20 — Wave 1 chitchat skips tools). Surfaced now because Phase 0 (PRs #262/#263/#264) made model more decisive: before, model would narrate "vou instalar"; now model fakes "instalei!". Worse UX.

## Fix

New static helper `AIAssistantService.isImplicitContinuation(message)` returning true for short (<80 chars) follow-ups without negation tokens (`não`, `cancela`, `esquece`, `deixa pra lá`, `pera`) and not standalone greetings (`oi`, `bom dia`, `tchau`...). Hydration block tries this heuristic FIRST, falls back to existing `detectConfirmation` for explicit confirmations.

Edge case handled: JS `\b` regex doesn't treat accented chars (`não`, `lá`, `pera`) as word boundaries — uses `[^\p{L}]` Unicode-aware lookarounds.

## Tests

- New `__tests__/mid-task-hydration.spec.ts`: **52 cases passing** including:
  - Exact prod-transcript prompt: `"vamos usar o 3414"` → hydrate ✓
  - Selection patterns: `"esse aí"`, `"o 11999..."`, `"+55 11..."`, `"dev_xyz"`
  - Negation: `"não, cancela"`, `"vamos não usar"` → NOT hydrate ✓
  - Standalone greetings: `"oi"`, `"bom dia"` → NOT hydrate ✓
  - Long new intent: `"agora cria um lead pra Maria..."` → NOT hydrate (goes to router) ✓
- Full ai-assistant + ai-core suite: **1751/1751 passing** zero regression
- Independent validator agent fuzz batch: **30/30** zero false positives, zero false negatives

## End-to-end stg validation

Same curl reproducer of the prod bug:
- Pre-fix (prod 2026-05-04 11:05): `tools: []` + fake IDs `wfl_cmlz...`
- Post-fix (stg 2026-05-04 11:25): `tools: [list_whatsapp_devices]` + honest response: "Não encontrei terminado em 3414. Estes são os devices: ... Qual deles?"

## Risk

LOW. Hydration only fires when `rawIsChitchat=true` AND cache populated AND not negation/greeting. Worst case: stray "oi" mid-task carries previous-turn skills into a true chitchat → small token waste, no incorrect behavior.

## Rollback

`docker service rollback wpp_painel-cliente-api` (one command, ~30s).

- [x] Independent validation 30/30
- [x] Stg deploy + curl reproducer of exact prod bug → honest response
- [ ] Prod deploy + same curl reproducer
- [ ] Watch 1h: ai.cache.metrics, narration guard fires, error rate

title: fix(ai-assistant): teach RUN_AGENT correctly + recover from JSON-string config
body:
## Summary
Two correlated bugs that broke `add_workflow_action` when the AI tried to add a RUN_AGENT step (reproduced live in stg building "Atendimento Restaurante Demo" — 7+ failed iterations):

1. **KB taught the model the wrong actionType.** Several knowledge-base entries said `add_workflow_action type=AI_AGENT`, but `WorkflowActionType` only accepts `RUN_AGENT` (internal) and `AI_HUB_AGENT` (legacy external). The model learned the bad value and burned iterations sending it.
2. **Executor crashed on JSON-string `config`.** When the model serialized config as `"{\"agentId\":\"...\"}"` (it does, occasionally — Anthropic tool calling doesn't enforce schemas model-side), the executor's `'fieldName' in input.config` threw the cryptic "Cannot use 'in' operator...". The model couldn't recover.

## Repro from stg logs (cmosuv3hi00882p0v5me9hssk)
```
4:40:08  AI sent: {"type":"AI_AGENT", config:"{...string...}"}    → API: type must be one of...
4:40:36  AI sent: {"type":"SEND_MESSAGE", config:"{...string...}"} → same error
... 4 more iterations ...
4:41:10  AI finally sent {"actionType":"RUN_AGENT", config:"{...string...}"} → API accepted but
4:41:28  add_workflow_action crashed: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'agentId' in {...}
```

## Fix scope (7 files, 182+/17-)

**KB cleanup (5 files):** every `AI_AGENT`/`type=AI_AGENT` for the workflow context replaced with `RUN_AGENT`/`actionType=RUN_AGENT`. Added an explicit "do not use AI_AGENT" callout to `anti-patterns.md`.
- `entries/workflow-building-blocks.md`
- `entries/common-patterns.md`
- `entries/anti-patterns.md`
- `core-knowledge.contributor.ts`
- root `CLAUDE.md`

**Defensive parse (1 file):** `tools-executor.service.ts` — added pure `coerceConfigObject` helper invoked at the top of `add_workflow_action` case. Auto-parses JSON-string configs; passes through non-strings, plain strings, and unparseable JSON unchanged so downstream validators still produce real errors.

## Test plan
- [x] 8 unit tests for `coerceConfigObject` (object pass-through, JSON parse, primitives, null/undefined, malformed input)
- [x] 1 KB regression assertion: no positive guidance with `actionType="AI_AGENT"` survives in any knowledge file
- [x] Full Jest suite: 5176 pass / 15 fail (same 3 pre-existing files unrelated to this fix) — **0 new regressions**
- [ ] Stg deploy + retry "Atendimento Restaurante Demo" workflow build (in progress)

## Why this is the right fix
- Bug 1 is the root cause — KB ensina o valor errado. AI passa a acertar no primeiro try com KB corrigido.
- Bug 2 é defesa em profundidade — mesmo com KB correto, o modelo às vezes serializa config como string; agora o executor recupera silenciosamente em vez de crashar com erro opaco.
- Não toca DTO, schema validation, ou enum. Escopo cirúrgico.

When `refreshToken` was `null` (user not logged in yet), the interceptor called `clearAuth()` + `window.location.href='/login'` **before** the `<Login>` component could render its `<Alert>`. The user-visible "error" was a silent page reload.

This is **Wave A** of `docs/plans/2026-05-07-painel-auth-stale-perms-and-login-error-ux.md`. Bug 2 (stale permissions until logout+login) is addressed by Waves B+C.

## Diagnostic chain (validated `file_path:line`)

1. `apps/painel-cliente/src/pages/Login.tsx:76-93` — component handles errors correctly: try/catch, `setError()`, `<Alert>` renders on line 170-175. ✅
2. `packages/iam-auth/src/iam-auth.service.ts:51-59` — IAM 401 → `HttpException('Invalid credentials', 401)` ✅
3. `apps/painel-cliente/src/services/api.ts:91-118` (pre-fix) — interceptor sees 401, no `refreshToken` in store, fires `clearAuth()` + `window.location.href='/login'` ❌
4. Page reload unmounts `<Login>` before the Alert can paint — `Promise.reject(error)` on line 117 reaches the `catch` in Login.tsx:87 but React state is already destroyed.

## Fix

Add `/auth/login` and `/auth/register` to the interceptor's exclusion list, alongside the existing exclusions for WhatsApp/Billing endpoints and `/auth/refresh`:

```ts
const isAuthUiFlow =
  originalRequest?.url?.includes('/auth/login') ||
  originalRequest?.url?.includes('/auth/register');

if (isWhatsAppTokenError || isBillingError || isAuthUiFlow) {
  return Promise.reject(error);
}
```

The component already handles the rejection — same pattern that works today for `/auth/refresh` (line 105-110 pre-fix).

|---|---|---|
| Unit | `apps/painel-cliente/src/services/__tests__/api.interceptor.test.ts` | +3 cases under "security: excluded endpoints" — `/auth/login`, `/auth/register`, regression where `refreshToken=null`. **27/27 passing locally.** |

| E2E | `tests/painel-cliente/iam-login.spec.ts` | Strengthened existing weak assertion — it used to `.count()` alerts but never assert count > 0, which is exactly why this bug went undetected. |

# ✓ 27 passed (49ms)

## Context
Closes the gap that prevented operators from moving a WhatsApp device between Catalisa accounts. Today's bulk XLSX export carries metadata only — no credentials, no portability. This PR ships a granular, password-encrypted bundle (`.cdvc`) that runs the **real** Meta+BB registration pipeline on import: the destination tenant ends up with a working device (`bbIngressStatus=ACTIVE`), no manual ingress configuration step.

Plan: [`docs/plans/2026-05-07-encrypted-device-export-import.md`](docs/plans/2026-05-07-encrypted-device-export-import.md)

## What's in scope
- **Schema**: new `UserMetaApp` model `(userId, metaAppId)` with AES-256-GCM-encrypted `metaAppSecret`; denormalized `MetaAccount.metaAppId` for fast bundle resolution. Migration applied via raw SQL idempotent (legacy migration on shadow DB blocked `prisma migrate dev`).
- **Capture-on-prompt**: extended `MetaBusinessService.createWppBizApp/updateWppBizApp` to mirror the App Secret painel-side (BB only returns `hasAppSecret: [valor suprimido], never the value, so we keep our own copy).
- **Bundle service** (`WhatsAppDevicesBundleService`): `exportSingle`, `exportMany` (concurrency 5), `importBundle`. Reuses the existing `WhatsAppDevicesService.createStandaloneDevice` so the import path is the same code that's already in production for the AddDeviceWizard "Avançado" mode.
- **`ensureWppBizApp`**: at import time, looks up the destination BB org for the same Meta App ID — reuse if `hasAppSecret=true`, `updateWppBizApp` if missing secret, else `createWppBizApp`.
- **3 new endpoints**: `POST /:id/export-bundle`, `POST /export-bundle`, `POST /import-bundle`.
- **Crypto util** (frontend): pure WebCrypto, PBKDF2-SHA256 600 000 iterations + AES-256-GCM (12-byte IV, 16-byte tag). Wrong-password manifests as auth-tag failure → `BundleAuthTagError`. Mirrors the admin-panel pattern from commit `dc191c6d`, with explicit `meta` block readable BEFORE password prompt.
- **Frontend API client** additions for the three endpoints.

## What's NOT in this PR (next session)
- `ExportBundleModal.tsx` + `ImportBundleModal.tsx` (UI components)

## Tests
- 28 new unit tests, all green:
  - `meta-business.service.spec.ts` — 5 tests (capture-on-prompt: persist, backward-compat, best-effort failure, secret rotation, rename-only no-op)
  - `whatsapp-devices-bundle.service.spec.ts` — 14 tests (export happy path, APP_SECRET_REQUIRED surface, metadata-only, DEVICE_NOT_FOUND, DEVICE_NOT_LINKED, ambiguousMatchCount; import created, WppBizApp reuse/update, conflict skip/fail, MISSING_ACCESS_TOKEN, APP_NOT_REGISTERED, META_TOKEN_INVALID)

- 36 pre-existing whatsapp-devices + meta-business tests still green (zero regression).

## Smoke E2E in stg (with real device + real creds)
- ✅ Backend deploy via `npm run ship:staging painel-cliente-api`
- ✅ Migration applied via `$executeRawUnsafe` (idempotent ALTER … IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS)
- ✅ Capture-on-prompt: `POST /meta-business/apps` → `UserMetaApp` row created with secret encrypted at-rest (`iv:authTag:ciphertext` format)

title: fix(devices-bundle): CORS hotfix — Cache-Control on response, not request
body:
## Hotfix — production smoke caught it

Clicking "Exportar bundle" in production surfaced **"Network Error"** with no HTTP status. Root cause:

- The frontend was sending `Cache-Control: no-store` as a **request** header.
- `Cache-Control` is **not** in the [CORS-safelisted request headers](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/CORS-safelisted_request_header) (`Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `Content-Language`, `Content-Type`).
- A non-safelisted custom header forces a CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`).
- The API's `enableCors({ allowedHeaders: [Content-Type, Authorization, X-Requested-With, Accept, X-API-Key] })` doesn't list `Cache-Control`, so the preflight is rejected.
- Browser blocks the actual `POST` entirely; axios surfaces a generic "Network Error" with no response.

## Fix
- **`apps/painel-cliente`**: drop the `Cache-Control` request header from `exportBundleSingle` + `exportBundleMany`.
- **`apps/painel-cliente-api`**: add `@Header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')` and `@Header('X-Content-Type-Options', 'nosniff')` to all three bundle endpoints (single export, many export, import).

The intent of `no-store` was always to keep the plaintext payload (Meta accessToken + App Secret in flight, before client-side encrypt) off intermediaries and disk caches. That belongs on the **response**, not the request.

## Verified
Real call against prod after deploy:
```
HTTP/2 201
cache-control: no-store
x-content-type-options: nosniff
```

## Summary

Two layers in one PR:

1. **Base infrastructure** (9 commits, agent-authored): `DnsBackend`

   mock impl, factory, contract tests. 71 vitest passing.

2. **Read-through delegation** (this final commit): `listZones`,
   `getZone`, `getZoneByFqdn`, `listRecords` in
   `beacon/store.ts` now consult the backend when one is configured,
   making the backend the source of truth.

## Why

User report: painel shows 2 zones (`developy.cloud`,
`developy.io`) but the PowerDNS LXC actually serves 6
(adds `catalisa.app`, `stg.catalisa.app`, `relayers.app`,
`klederson.com`). Records created via `pdnsutil` direct (incl.
the `app.developy.cloud` A record we added for TLS) never
round-tripped to the panel JSON.

After this PR, with `BEACON_BACKEND=powerdns` + `BEACON_DATABASE_URL`,
every zone/record read hits the PowerDNS Postgres directly. Drift gone.

title: feat(atlas-mgmt): atlas-mgmt-01 LXC provisioning scripts (Wave 2 Fase 1)
body:
Provisioning scripts for the **atlas-mgmt-01** LXC — the central Postgres
that backs the developy.cloud management panel (Aegis, Audit, Herald,
platform connections, marketing waitlist, per-module metadata).

Implements **Wave 2 Fase 1** from `plans/wave-2-execution.md`. Architecture
context lives in `plans/architecture-deep-dive.md` §4.7 (Atlas).

## What this adds

`scripts/bootstrap/atlas-mgmt/` — direct sibling of the existing
`scripts/bootstrap/builder-vm/`, same UX + safety posture:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Safety banner, prerequisites, runbook, troubleshooting |
| `.env.example` | All knobs (VMID, IP, sizes, PG creds, pgbouncer) |
| `.gitignore` | Local-only artifacts (`.env`, render output, logs) |
| `lib/common.sh` | Shared logging, dry-run, env-loading, confirmation helpers |
| `preflight.sh` | 12 read-only checks (storage, bridge, template, VMID, IP, creds) |
| `cloud-init.yaml.tpl` | Debian 13 + postgresql-16 + pgbouncer + ufw + fail2ban |
| `init-db.sh` | 15 module schemas + per-schema grants + default privileges (idempotent) |
| `install-tooling.sh` | Post-boot verify + tune (idempotent) |
| `validate.sh` | 9 JSON-emitting post-provision checks |
| `provision.sh` | Orchestrator. **Default = `--dry-run`**. |
| `destroy.sh` | 5-gate confirmation lever |

## Safety contract

- **Default mode of every script is `--dry-run`.** Nothing is sent to
  Proxmox unless `--apply` is passed AND the operator types `APPLY` at
  the prompt.
- **`destroy.sh` has five gates** — `--i-know-what-im-doing` flag,
  existing VMID, hostname match, in-LXC marker file present, typed
  `DESTROY <vmid>` confirmation.
- **All operations idempotent** — `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS`,
  `CREATE ROLE` / `ALTER ROLE` via `DO` block, pgbouncer userlist
  re-derived from `pg_shadow` on every run.
- **Marker file** `/etc/developy/lxc.marker` is written inside the LXC
  during provision and is the anchor that lets destroy.sh confirm
  ownership.
- **Tags** `developy;managed-by-bootstrap-script;atlas-mgmt` are set on
  the LXC for inventory queries.

## Configuration defaults

Wave-2 plan values, override in `.env`:

```
PROXMOX_NODE      = sp1-sd-catalisatec-2   (co-located with PowerDNS)
ATLAS_MGMT_VMID   = 9101                   (confirmed free)
ATLAS_MGMT_IP     = 172.10.0.151/24        (confirmed free in ARP scan)
ATLAS_MGMT_GW     = 172.10.0.10
ATLAS_MGMT_VCPU   = 4 cores / 4096 MiB / 512 MiB swap
ATLAS_MGMT_DISK   = 40 GiB on local-lvm
ATLAS_MGMT_BRIDGE = vmbr1
TEMPLATE          = local:vztmpl/debian-13-standard_13.1-2_amd64.tar.zst
PG_DB             = developy_mgmt
PG_OWNER          = developy_mgmt          (owns objects, runs migrations)
PG_APP_USER       = app_runtime            (DML only, no DDL)
PG_PORT           = 5432
PGBOUNCER_PORT    = 6432  (transaction mode, default_pool_size=20)
PG_ALLOWED_CIDR   = 172.10.0.0/24          (pg_hba scram-sha-256 source)
```

`PG_OWNER_PASSWORD` and `PG_APP_PASSWORD` have no default — the operator
must pin them in `.env` (stored in sops/age, not the repo).

## Schemas seeded

`init-db.sh` creates one schema per module that will write to mgmt-db:

```
aegis        audit        beacon_meta   platform     mesh
atlas_meta   spark_meta   tide_meta     nexus_meta   flux_meta
blaze_meta   ignite_meta  herald        marketing    convoy_meta
```

Plus default privileges so future tables created by drizzle migrations
are automatically grant-readable by `app_runtime`.

## Verification (no Proxmox needed)

```
shellcheck -x lib/common.sh preflight.sh provision.sh destroy.sh \
              validate.sh init-db.sh install-tooling.sh   # all clean
bash -n <each>                                            # all parse
yamllint -d '{extends: relaxed, rules: {comments: disable, line-length: {max: 200}}}' \
         cloud-init.yaml.tpl                              # clean

./preflight.sh                  # exits 1 with "not a Proxmox node"
./provision.sh --skip-preflight # prints all WOULD: commands, no side effects
./destroy.sh                    # banner + exit 1 (Gate 1 FAILED)
./init-db.sh                    # prints WOULD-PSQL: for 15 schemas * 6 stmts
./validate.sh                   # 9 dry-run JSON lines + summary
```

## Before --apply (operator checklist)

```
[ ] Confirm we are on Proxmox node sp1-sd-catalisatec-2  (uname -a)
[ ] Confirm storage local-lvm has >=60 GiB free          (pvesm status)
[ ] Confirm bridge vmbr1 is up                           (ip link show vmbr1)
[ ] Confirm template debian-13 is downloaded             (pveam list local)
[ ] Confirm VMID 9101 is free                            (pct status 9101)
[ ] Confirm IP 172.10.0.151 is free                      (ping -c1 -W1 172.10.0.151)
[ ] Generate PG_OWNER_PASSWORD + PG_APP_PASSWORD         (openssl rand -base64 32)
[ ] Store both passwords in infra-secrets sops file
[ ] cp .env.example .env  &&  edit the 3 REQUIRED vars
[ ] ./preflight.sh        — all 12 checks pass
[ ] ./provision.sh        — read the full WOULD: dump
[ ] ./provision.sh --apply  — type APPLY when prompted
[ ] ./validate.sh --apply --host 172.10.0.151  — 9/9 pass
[ ] From operator host: pnpm db:migrate
[ ] Add Beacon DNS A record: atlas-mgmt-01.internal → 172.10.0.151
[ ] Schedule Blaze cron: pg_dump → mgmt-tide every 6h  (Wave 2 Fase 5)
```

## Design decisions

- **LXC, not VM.** Matches the Wave-2 plan (LXC 9101) and the inventory in
  the deep-dive ("LXCs pros bancos"). Lower overhead than KVM for a
  single-purpose Postgres host.
- **Static IP, not DHCP.** The mgmt-db's address ends up in
  `DATABASE_URL` on the web LXC — DHCP churn would mean a config-rewrite
  on every lease renewal. The plan's reserved 172.10.0.151 is what's
  burned in here.
- **scram-sha-256, not md5.** Default `password_encryption` in PG 16+,
  matches what drizzle and pg-bouncer auth files expect.
- **pgbouncer on by default.** Transaction mode + pool of 20 is the safe
  default for drizzle's connection pattern. Disable with
  `PGBOUNCER_ENABLED=0` if you'd rather connect directly.
- **No replication / standby in this PR.** Wave 2 Fase 1 is single-node;
  HA (`atlas-prd-01..02`) is a Wave 3 concern.
- **Cloud-init manifest kept in cloud-config form.** Even though LXCs
  don't natively consume cloud-init, the file is reviewable, lives in
  Proxmox snippets as an audit artifact, and could become directly
  consumable if we ever switch base images.
- **Schemas seeded by `init-db.sh`, not by drizzle migration.** The
  drizzle migration (Wave 1, already merged in PR #16) places tables in
  schemas — `init-db.sh` makes sure those schemas + grants exist before
  the migration runs.

## What this does NOT do

- Does NOT run drizzle migrations  (operator runs `pnpm db:migrate`
  after `validate.sh` is green)
- Does NOT schedule pg_dump backups  (Wave 2 Fase 5 — Blaze cron)
- Does NOT add Beacon DNS records  (manual step from operator)
- Does NOT configure replication  (single-node mgmt-db in Wave 2)
- Does NOT open firewall holes at the edge router  (mgmt-db stays
  internal — bridge + ufw are the only ACLs)
- Does NOT merge automatically  — user merges after review.

title: feat(migrate-stores): JSON↔Postgres migration CLI + Beacon mapper (Wave 2 Fase 3)
body:
Wave 2 Fase 3 deliverable — see `plans/wave-2-execution.md` §2.

A `bun migrate:stores` CLI that moves a module's encrypted JSON store
contents into Postgres (and back). Beacon is the first mapper and
doubles as the template for every subsequent module migration.

## What's in the PR

```
scripts/migrate-stores/
├── README.md                         template doc: how to add a new mapper
├── cli.ts                            arg parser (parseArgs, zero deps)
├── index.ts                          Bun entrypoint
├── runner.ts                         module-agnostic orchestrator
├── types.ts                          ModuleMigrator / PostgresDriver / Logger
├── tsconfig.json + vitest.config.ts
├── modules/
│   ├── beacon.ts                     first mapper — BeaconStoreData → beacon_meta_*
│   ├── beacon.test.ts                end-to-end + idempotency + reversibility
│   └── index.ts                      registry
├── drivers/
│   ├── json-source.ts                encrypted JSON file source
│   ├── memory-driver.ts              in-memory PostgresDriver (tests)
│   ├── postgres-driver.ts            postgres-js driver (prod)
│   └── *.test.ts
├── state/
│   ├── crypto.ts                     AES-256-GCM (mirrors @proxmox-manager/core)
│   ├── checkpoint.ts                 resumable progress file
│   └── checkpoint.test.ts
└── ui/log.ts                         tiny TTY/silent logger pair
```

Plus three root scripts: `migrate:stores`, `test:migrate-stores`,
`test:migrate-stores:watch`.

## CLI surface

```
bun migrate:stores --module=<m> --from=<json|postgres> --to=<json|postgres> [flags]

  --dry-run     default; prints plan, no writes
  --apply       required for mutations
  --limit=N     cap rows per collection (testing)
  --state-file  override checkpoint location
  --work-dir    where to look for .{m}-store.json
```

`--module=all --apply` requires typed `APPLY` on stdin.

## Sample dry-run output

```
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO  migrating module=beacon-meta direction=json-to-postgres dryRun=true
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    clusters: read 1 (table=beacon_meta_clusters)
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    clusters: [dry-run] would insert 1 rows
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    nodes: read 2 (table=beacon_meta_nodes)
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    nodes: [dry-run] would insert 2 rows
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    zones: read 1 (table=beacon_meta_zones)
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    zones: [dry-run] would insert 1 rows
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    records: read 2 (table=beacon_meta_records)
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    records: [dry-run] would insert 2 rows
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO    _settings: [dry-run] would upsert 6 kv rows
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO  done module=beacon-meta {"read":12,"written":0,"skipped":12,"errored":0}
2026-05-11T19:26:19Z INFO  ─── summary ────────────────────────────────────────
```

Dry-run does not write a checkpoint; a follow-up `--apply` does the real work.

## Tests — 48 passing

```
✓ drivers/memory-driver.test.ts   (6)
✓ drivers/json-source.test.ts     (6)
✓ state/checkpoint.test.ts        (6)
✓ cli.test.ts                     (15)
✓ runner.test.ts                  (10)
✓ modules/beacon.test.ts          (5)
─────────────────────────────────────
  Test Files  6 passed (6)
       Tests  48 passed (48)
```

Covered:
- dry-run path (no mutation, no checkpoint poisoning)
- `--apply` path (writes + counts)
- `--limit` caps rows
- toRow failures surface as `errored` without aborting the collection
- **idempotency**: re-running writes 0 rows (ON CONFLICT semantics)
- **reversibility**: postgres → json → postgres yields same row count
- **resume**: checkpoint marking a collection completed → skipped next run
- AES-256-GCM round-trip is byte-compatible with @proxmox-manager/core
- Wrong encryption key produces a friendly error
- Per-mapper round-trip on every Beacon collection + the BeaconSettings kv blob

## Safety rails

- Default mode is `--dry-run`. `--apply` mandatory for any mutation.
- `--module=all --apply` requires typed `APPLY` on stdin.
- All inserts use `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (real driver) or hashed
  dedup (memory driver) → re-runs are idempotent.
- Checkpoints atomic (tmp + rename), versioned, never written on dry-run.
- Postgres driver only quotes identifiers matching `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`
  and uses parameterised queries for values.

## Beacon mapper — provisional table names

The `beacon_meta` drizzle schema is being built by a parallel agent on
another branch. Until it lands the mapper uses string literals
(`beacon_meta_clusters`, `beacon_meta_nodes`, …) with TODO comments
pointing at the eventual `getTableName(beaconMetaClusters)` swap. Tests
pass against MemoryDriver so they don't depend on the schema landing.

## How to add a new module migrator

Six steps in `scripts/migrate-stores/README.md`:

1. Copy `modules/beacon.ts` → `modules/<name>.ts`.
2. Register in `modules/index.ts`.
3. Write a round-trip test in `modules/<name>.test.ts`.
4. Swap magic strings for `getTableName(...)` once the schema lands.
5. Document column mapping at the top of the mapper.
6. PR per the standard ritual.

## Next steps for cutover (humano)

Once `wt-atlas-mgmt-provisioning` and the `beacon_meta` schema land:

```bash
# On laptop, against atlas-mgmt-01 via SSH tunnel
export DATABASE_URL=[credencial suprimida]
export CONNECTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY=$(... from /etc/developy/web.env)

# Pull the live store
scp lxc9100:/srv/developy/.beacon-store.json ./

# Dry-run first
bun migrate:stores --module=beacon --from=json --to=postgres --dry-run

# Apply
bun migrate:stores --module=beacon --from=json --to=postgres --apply

# Flip the env on LXC 9100:
#   BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND=postgres
# systemctl restart developy-web
```

Per-module rollout sequence: `plans/wave-2-execution.md` §2 Fase 4.

title: feat(db): StoreBackend SPI + Beacon as reference implementation
body:
**Wave 2 Fase 2** — introduces the SPI that every module's persistence layer
will plug into when JSON stores graduate to Postgres. Beacon is wired as
the canonical reference implementation; other modules copy this pattern.

> **Base:** \`feat/drizzle-schemas\` — depends on the Wave 1 schemas + migrations.
> Land Wave 1 first, then this.

## What ships

### Part A — \`beacon_meta\` schema (drizzle)

Three new tables appended to \`schema/beacon.ts\` (PowerDNS tables left
untouched):

| Table                    | Purpose                                                        |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| \`beacon_meta_clusters\`   | BeaconCluster — topology, HA mode, size, Proxmox node, audit  |
| \`beacon_meta_nodes\`      | BeaconNode — NS LXC, IP, status; FK CASCADE from cluster      |
| \`beacon_meta_settings\`   | jsonb key/value singletons (\`nsDomain\`, \`nsIpv6Pool\`, …)      |

Enums (\`beacon_cluster_status\`, \`beacon_ha_mode\`, \`beacon_size\`,
\`beacon_node_status\`) mirror the unions in \`@sidefuel/platform/beacon\`.
Migration generated via \`pnpm db:generate\` — \`0001_cold_sandman.sql\` +
\`meta/0001_snapshot.json\` + journal update committed.

### Part B — StoreBackend SPI base

| File                        | Role                                                           |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| \`db/store-backend.ts\`       | \`StoreBackend<TStore>\` interface + \`ItemOf\` helper           |
| \`db/json-file-backend.ts\`   | Wraps legacy \`.{m}-store.json\` AES-GCM read/write             |
| \`db/postgres-backend.ts\`    | Pass-through over a module-supplied \`PostgresBackendAdapter\`  |
| \`db/store-factory.ts\`       | Resolves backend via env: \`<MODULE>_STORE_BACKEND\` > global > json |

Env resolution: \`getStoreBackend(\"beacon-meta\")\` checks
\`BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND\`, then \`STORE_BACKEND\`, then defaults to
\`\"json\"\`. Per-module flip is the safe cutover lever.

### Part C — Beacon refactor (reference implementation)

- \`beacon/postgres-adapter.ts\` — maps \`BeaconStoreData\` to drizzle
  operations against the new \`beacon_meta_*\` tables. Zones/records
  are intentionally no-ops (PowerDNS owns them via the DnsBackend).
- \`beacon/store.ts\` — replaces inline \`readStore()/writeStore()\` +
  \`withWriteLock\` with calls through \`getStoreBackend(\"beacon-meta\", …)\`.
  All public function signatures preserved.

**Behavior guarantee:** with no env vars set, \`.beacon-store.json\`
behaviour is bit-equivalent to the pre-refactor implementation. The
PowerDNS DnsBackend delegation from PR #15 is preserved verbatim.

## Tests — 41 new, 137 total in touched areas, 0 regressions

| Suite                                              | Tests | Purpose                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| \`db/json-file-backend.test.ts\`                     | 9     | tmpfile round-trip, encrypt/decrypt, locks      |
| \`db/postgres-backend.test.ts\`                      | 6     | pg-mem via raw-SQL adapter                      |
| \`db/store-backend.test.ts\`                         | 10    | contract suite — both backends symmetric        |
| \`db/store-factory.test.ts\`                         | 11    | every env resolution rule + laziness            |
| \`beacon/store.test.ts\`                             | 11    | json-mode regression for full public surface    |
| \`db/db.test.ts\` (existing, now applies migration 0001) | 19    | full schema validates including beacon_meta     |
| \`beacon/backends/*\` (existing)                     | 71    | DnsBackend layer untouched                      |

\`bootTestDb()\` now applies every migration under \`migrations/\` by
default, so future migrations are exercised by the smoke suite without
code changes.

## Env vars for cutover

```bash
# Default = json (current behaviour, zero deploy change).
# Flip per module after migrate:stores has ingested the JSON snapshot:
BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND=postgres

# Or, once every module's adapter has shipped, the global:
STORE_BACKEND=postgres
```

## Trade-offs

- \`PostgresBackend\` is intentionally thin and delegates SQL to a
  per-module adapter. Reason: pg-mem can't host drizzle's postgres-js
  driver, so tests use a raw-SQL adapter while production uses drizzle.
  The seam is the SPI's adapter interface.
- \`replaceAll\` snapshots the whole store in a transaction (DELETE +
  INSERT). For high-write modules this is inefficient; \`saveEntity\` /
  \`deleteEntity\` are the hot-path API. Beacon's adapter implements
  both.
- \`beacon_meta_settings\` is staged in the schema but \`getBeaconSettings\` /
  \`saveBeaconSettings\` still use \`.beacon-settings.json\`. Migrating
  settings is a small follow-up — it's a separate file with a separate
  shape so the cutover doesn't need to land in this PR.
- The contract test exercises both backends against the same surface,
  which catches any future symmetry bugs without needing real Postgres
  in CI.

## Next steps (not in this PR)

1. Land Wave 1 (\`feat/drizzle-schemas\`) before this rebases on \`main\`.
2. Provision \`atlas-mgmt-01\` LXC (Fase 1).
3. Run \`drizzle-kit migrate\` against atlas-mgmt-01.
4. Build the \`migrate:stores\` CLI (Wave 2 Fase 3) — uses this SPI's
   \`load()\`/\`save()\` for the JSON → Postgres copy step.
5. Cutover Beacon by setting \`BEACON_META_STORE_BACKEND=postgres\` in
   \`/etc/developy/web.env\` and restarting \`developy-web\`. The JSON
   file stays as fallback for 7 days.

title: feat(marketing): postgres cutover (Wave 2)
body:
Follows Beacon template (PR #21). Wave 2 module migration — first of Tier 1 modules per `plans/wave-2-module-migration-playbook.md` §1.

## Status of marketing module pre-PR

The marketing module had **no prior `store.ts`** — only the drizzle schema (PR #16) and the hotsite-launch plan (`plans/hotsite-launch.md`). This PR creates the entire persistence layer from scratch following the Beacon pattern.

## Changes

- **`apps/web/src/lib/server/marketing/types.ts`** — domain shape (`MarketingStoreData` with `signups` + `pledges` arrays). Ids are strings; the bigserial PK is converted at the row boundary so JSON.stringify survives.
- **`apps/web/src/lib/server/marketing/postgres-adapter.ts`** — `PostgresBackendAdapter<MarketingStoreData>`. Bigint conversion happens here (`BigInt(id)` on write, `.toString()` on read). FK CASCADE on `signup_id` mirrored in JSON mode by `deleteSignup` cascade in the store.
- **`apps/web/src/lib/server/marketing/store.ts`** — public API for the hotsite routes. Wired to `getStoreBackend()` (default JSON, opt-in postgres via `MARKETING_STORE_BACKEND=postgres`). Exports `listSignups`, `saveSignup`, `deleteSignup`, `listPledges`, `getCounters`, etc.
- **`scripts/migrate-stores/modules/marketing.ts`** — `ModuleMigrator<MarketingStoreData>` mirroring `beacon.ts`. No settings/kv blob (marketing has no settings).
- **`scripts/migrate-stores/modules/marketing.test.ts`** — 8 tests: toRow/fromRow sanity per collection, full end-to-end round-trip via MemoryDriver, idempotency, empty store edge case.
- **`scripts/migrate-stores/modules/index.ts`** — appended `marketing: marketingMigrator` (other entries untouched for sibling-agent merge compat).

## Testing

- `pnpm test:migrate-stores` — **56/56 tests green** (8 new marketing tests + existing suites).
- `pnpm typecheck` (apps/web) — no new errors from these files. The two pre-existing unrelated errors in `tests/ignite/*.test.ts` (duplicate `vi` identifier, `'deleted'` not in FunctionStatus union) exist on `origin/main` and are out of scope.
- JSON mode unchanged for any caller that doesn't set `MARKETING_STORE_BACKEND=postgres` — zero regression.

## Deviations from Beacon template (with reasoning)

1. **Marketing types live in `apps/web/src/lib/server/marketing/types.ts`, not in `@sidefuel/platform`.** Beacon's `BeaconStoreData` lives in the platform package because the SDK consumes it. Marketing has no SDK surface — yet — so keeping the types local avoids a cross-workspace edit. The migrate-stores mapper re-declares the shape (same pattern Beacon uses for `BeaconSettings`).
2. **No `settings` / kv blob.** Marketing has no module-level settings (no `.marketing-settings.json`). The mapper omits the `settings` field entirely.
3. **String ids over bigint.** The schema uses `bigserial`. The domain shape uses string ids so the JSON store survives `JSON.stringify` (which can't serialise bigint). Conversion is contained in the adapter and mapper.
4. **Custom `getItemId` in the store.** Defends against bigint/number ids slipping through, even though the domain says string — matches the defensive theme in `json-file-backend.ts`.

## Schema changes

None. The schema in `apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/marketing.ts` (from PR #16) was already sufficient — both tables already model every field the store needs (email, source, intent, github, ipHash, userAgent, confirmed, confirmedAt, createdAt for signups; signupId, nodeType, capacity, createdAt for pledges).

Follows Beacon template (PR #21). Wave 2 module migration — connection profiles + feature flags.

## Changes
- Adapter for `connection_profiles` (bytea pass-through) + `feature_flags` (kv)

`PlatformStoreData` carries `ConnectionProfileEnvelope[]` (encrypted bytes wrapped in metadata) and `PlatformFeatureFlag[]` (kv-style). The web app's `connections.ts` encrypts/decrypts plaintext profiles at the domain boundary; the SPI/adapter never sees plaintext credentials.

In Postgres mode each envelope row carries its own ciphertext in a `bytea` column. The adapter performs a pure base64↔Buffer transform at the SQL boundary; the bytes pass through bit-for-bit.

title: fix(wave2): post-cutover fixes — root postgres dep + 0003 FK ordering
body:
Two issues discovered during 2026-05-11 prod cutover of marketing/aegis/audit/platform modules.

## 1. `postgres` package missing from root deps

`scripts/migrate-stores/drivers/postgres-driver.ts` lazy-imports `postgres` but it was only declared in `apps/web/package.json`. The CLI runs from repo root and Bun's resolver couldn't find it there. Beacon cutover worked because of a stale install. Frozen-lockfile deploys remove it.

**Fix:** declare `postgres@^3.4.9` as a root dependency.

## 2. Migration 0003 ALTER COLUMN order

drizzle-kit's 0003_minor_saracen.sql alters columns in declaration order. Postgres rejects `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE` on a column with an FK whose type would mismatch. pg-mem in tests doesn't enforce this so the original PR's tests passed.

**Symptom on prod:** 0003 partially applied (some text alters succeeded, others failed; FK adds at end failed too).

**Prod repair:** dropped 7 FKs manually, altered all remaining uuid→text, re-added FKs, INSERTed row into `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` with original SQL's hash `2b4a36ed1e043c2a2790743eecb3191ee2777d47471b0a272ee259ed3c51cab8`.

**This PR's fix:** rewrite `0003_minor_saracen.sql` to drop all referencing FKs first, alter both sides of each relation, then re-ADD the FKs.

## ⚠ Post-merge action required on prod

This PR rewrites a migration whose hash is already recorded in prod. New hash: `8777c21f138597e388d5175c751080189c1b95ee3fd4c96ea9f3d923cb4039c4`. After merge & next deploy:

```sql
-- On atlas-mgmt-01 (LXC 9101)
UPDATE drizzle.__drizzle_migrations
SET hash = '8777c21f138597e388d5175c751080189c1b95ee3fd4c96ea9f3d923cb4039c4'
WHERE hash = '2b4a36ed1e043c2a2790743eecb3191ee2777d47471b0a272ee259ed3c51cab8';
```

Without this, drizzle-kit will detect the hash mismatch and try to re-run 0003, which would fail on `ADD CONSTRAINT` (already exists).

## Testing
- Local typecheck clean
- pnpm-lock.yaml regenerated with new dep
- 0003 SQL hand-verified against drizzle's add/drop semantics; matches the manual repair sequence that succeeded on prod
- Cannot retest 0003 against existing prod (already applied via manual repair); relevant for fresh DBs going forward

title: feat(db): plain SQL migration runner — drizzle-kit becomes optional
body:
Replaces `drizzle-kit migrate` with a tiny custom SQL runner. **drizzle-orm itself stays** — it's the query builder used by all the Postgres adapters (Beacon, marketing, aegis, audit, platform). Only migration tooling changes.

## Why

Two pain points during 2026-05-11 Wave 2 cutover motivated this:

1. **drizzle-kit auto-generated FK-buggy migrations.** It emitted `ALTER COLUMN ... SET DATA TYPE` before dropping FK constraints. pg-mem in tests accepted it; real Postgres rejected. PR #27 fixed it. With hand-written migrations the bug class disappears — reviewers see the SQL.

2. **Snapshot + hash + journal made post-deploy fixes painful.** Modifying a migration that's already applied means updating `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations.hash` on every deployed DB. This runner uses filename tracking only — no hash, no snapshot.

## What

- `scripts/db-migrate/runner.ts` — < 150 LOC. Lex-orders `apps/web/src/lib/server/db/migrations/*.sql`, tracks in `public.__migrations(filename text PK, applied_at timestamptz)`. Each migration in its own transaction.
- `scripts/db-migrate/index.ts` — CLI: `status`, `apply`, `new <description>`
- `scripts/db-migrate/runner.test.ts` — 9 vitest cases (file discovery, lex ordering, idempotency, scaffolding, drizzle-bootstrap)
- **Bootstrap path** for existing DBs: on first run, if `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` exists with applied rows, the runner maps drizzle's id-ordered rows to migration files sorted by filename. Already-applied migrations skip cleanly. Atlas-mgmt-01 (prod) will bootstrap from drizzle's 4 rows on first `db:apply`.

## New pnpm scripts (use these going forward)

- `pnpm db:status` — list applied/pending
- `pnpm db:apply` — run pending in order
- `pnpm db:new "<desc>"` — scaffold next-numbered .sql with header reminding about FK ordering
- `pnpm test:db-migrate` — vitest

## Kept for fallback (delete in follow-up PR)

`pnpm db:generate`, `db:migrate`, `db:studio`, `db:check` — still invoke drizzle-kit. Removed in a follow-up after `db:apply` is exercised in a few cutover cycles.

## Tests

- 9/9 runner unit tests pass
- Typecheck: clean for new files; pre-existing errors in `tests/ignite/03-*` and `04-*` are not from this PR (same on origin/main)

## Migration on prod

Zero-downtime. After merge + deploy:

1. `pnpm db:apply` is now available; `db:migrate` (drizzle-kit) still works
2. First `db:apply` against atlas-mgmt-01 bootstraps from `drizzle.__drizzle_migrations` (4 rows) → marks all 4 migration files applied → reports `up to date`
3. Going forward, ignore `db:migrate`; use `db:apply`. New migrations land via `db:new` then PR review

## Docs

- `scripts/db-migrate/README.md` — full usage + history of why drizzle-kit was retired
- `plans/deploy-runbook.md` §3.1 — uses `pnpm db:apply`
- CLAUDE.md — new 'Database migrations' section + 'Adding a schema change' workflow with FK-ordering reminder

title: fix(provisioner): centralize vmidToIp + reserved-IP guard (prevents 2026-05-11-style outages)
body:
## Outage being fixed

On 2026-05-11 the dashboard hung on 'Loading organizations...'. Root cause: a Herald lifecycle test instance got VMID 151 and IP 172.10.0.151 — same as atlas-mgmt-01 (LXC 9101, the postgres mgmt LXC). ARP races silently routed half the app's postgres queries to the Herald container. Connections timed out.

Local recovery: `pct stop 151` + bridge fdb flush + restart developy-web. Structural fix: this PR.

## Why it happened

Every data-product provisioner (atlas/beacon/blaze/flux/herald/ignite/nexus/spark/tide — nine files) had its own copy of:

```ts
function vmidToIp(vmid: number): string {
  ...
  parts[3] = String(vmid % 256);  // <-- no collision check, no reservation
  ...
}
```

Two structural failures:

1. **Manual management LXCs picked IPs from inside the provisioner range.** atlas-mgmt-01 = 172.10.0.151, developy-quickstart = 172.10.0.150. Both .150 and .151 are valid outputs of `vmid % 256` for VMIDs 150, 151, 406, 407, ... Collision was inevitable.
2. **No reservation mechanism.** Nowhere to declare 'these octets are off-limits to the provisioner.'

## Fix

- Move `vmidToIp` to canonical `data-products/provisioner-base.ts`. Re-implementations in all 9 files deleted; each imports the shared one.
- Add configurable reserved-octet set. Defaults reflect prod state on 2026-05-11:
  - `.10, .11` — PVE host vmbr1 interfaces
  - `.103` — pg-beacon-default
  - `.127` — pdns-ns1
  - `.150` — developy-quickstart (manual)
  - `.151` — atlas-mgmt-01 (manual)
  Override via `DATA_PRODUCTS_RESERVED_IPS=10,11,103,127,150,151`.
- When `vmid % 256` lands on a reserved octet, walk forward to next free. Loop bound 256 — can't hang.
- Re-reads env on every call so reservations can rotate at runtime.

## What this still does NOT fix (follow-up)

Two VMIDs that differ by 256 still produce the same octet (VMID 200 and VMID 456 → both .200). The proper fix is an explicit IPAM allocation table. `mesh/ipam-engine.ts` already has one — adapt and centralize. Will be a separate PR.

## Tests

11 new vitest cases in `provisioner-base.test.ts`:
- dhcp fallback (env unset / 'dhcp')
- non-reserved mapping
- mask preservation
- **regression: VMID 151 must NOT produce 172.10.0.151** (the exact bug)
- regression: VMID 150 (developy-quickstart)
- regression: VMID 103 + 127
- env override (`DATA_PRODUCTS_RESERVED_IPS`)
- default reserved set includes well-known octets
- wrap-around bound (no infinite loop)

Typecheck clean. Pre-existing errors in `tests/ignite/03,04-*` exist on origin/main, unrelated.

title: feat(mesh): postgres cutover (Wave 2 Tier 3)
body:
Wave 2 Tier 3 — migrates Mesh (services, IP pools, allocations, certificates, idempotency) from `.mesh-store.json` to Postgres, following `plans/wave-2-module-migration-playbook.md` §2–§3.

## What ships

- `apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/mesh.ts` — drizzle types for 9 tables. All `text` PKs (matches legacy `<prefix>-{ts}-{rand}` IDs from `mesh/store.ts`)
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/db/migrations/0004_create_mesh_tables.sql` — hand-written DDL. No ALTERs on existing tables → FK-ordering pitfall (PR #27 lesson) doesn't apply. CREATE TABLE order respects FK graph.
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/postgres-adapter.ts` — explodes nested `service.{listeners,routes,targets,instances}` into child tables; rebuilds them on `loadAll`. Top-level `ipAllocations` and `certificates` are authoritative; service-bound views denormalised on read.
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/mesh/store.ts` — refactored to use `getStoreBackend('mesh', …)`. Default mode (no env flag) is bit-for-bit equivalent to the pre-refactor JSON store. Zero regression risk.
- `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/mesh.ts` — module migrator
- `scripts/migrate-stores/runner.ts` + `types.ts` — adds two optional `CollectionMigrator` hooks (`readFromStore` / `writeToStore`) so mesh can flatten nested service children into virtual top-level collections without altering the JSON store shape. **No behaviour change** for beacon / aegis / audit / marketing / platform.

## Why two new runner hooks?

Mesh is the first module where the JSON store nests entities under `service.{listeners,…}`. The existing runner assumed every `collection` lived at `store[name]` as a flat array. The hooks are opt-in: `readFromStore(store) => unknown[]` and `writeToStore(store, items) => void`. Existing migrators are unchanged.

## Schema deviations from beacon

| Difference | Reason |
|---|---|
| 9 tables (vs beacon's 2 `beacon_meta_*`) | mesh has more entity types; nested service children get first-class tables instead of jsonb to keep SQL queryable |
| `enabled` on `mesh_routes` is `integer` (0/1) | boolean would work; integer keeps it consistent with `wildcard` on `mesh_certificates` (both came from JSON `false/true` and we wanted both columns to use the same shape) |
| `scaling_policy` is jsonb (not column-per-mode) | the policy shape evolves (target_tracking → step_scaling → scheduled); jsonb avoids ALTER-per-mode |
| `mesh_ip_allocations.service_id` is nullable + non-FK | orphan allocations can exist during transient states; matches the legacy filter-cascade in `deleteService` |
| no jsonb on certificates for `material` (PEM/key) | the legacy domain type doesn't expose cert material; we'll add bytea like platform module did when it lands |

## Tests

- 14 new tests in `modules/mesh.test.ts` covering mapper round-trip, end-to-end (JSON → Postgres → JSON), idempotency, legacy ID format, schema coercion
- Pattern-matching MemoryDriver pattern (NOT pg-mem — v3 AST bug)
- All **101 migrate-stores tests** pass (was 87, +14 mesh)
- All **9 db-migrate tests** pass
- All **33 `apps/web` mesh tests** pass (no regression in `store.ts` refactor)
- Typecheck clean except 3 pre-existing ignite errors (not mine)

```

ipPools: 1 items
ipAllocations: 0 items
certificates: 0 items
idempotencyRecords: 0 items
```

Prod is similar (589B file).

Follow `plans/deploy-runbook.md` §2-§3 (deploy + migrate-stores + flip env + smoke).

1. Deploy main to LXC 9100
2. `pnpm db:apply` — applies 0004
3. Re-grant app_runtime perms on new `mesh_*` tables (idempotent)
4. Re-encrypt local `.mesh-store.json` if laptop ≠ prod key (laptop has data; prod likely empty)
5. `bun migrate:stores --module=mesh --dry-run` to verify
6. `bun migrate:stores --module=mesh --apply`
7. Flip `MESH_STORE_BACKEND=postgres` in `/etc/developy/web.env`

body:
## Summary

Migrates the **Flux** module (streaming clusters — NATS / Redpanda / RabbitMQ) from JSON file storage to a pluggable StoreBackend SPI that defaults to JSON and flips to Postgres via env flag. Follows the Wave 2 Tier 3 playbook (`plans/wave-2-module-migration-playbook.md` §2-§6).

## Schema

`apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/flux.ts`:

| Table | Purpose | PK |
|---|---|---|
| `flux_meta_clusters` | Parent; `engine` enum discriminates between NATS / Redpanda / RabbitMQ | `text id` |
| `flux_meta_credentials` | Cluster-scoped; soft delete via `revoked_at`; unique `(cluster_id, username)` | `text id` |
| `flux_meta_topics` | Cluster-scoped; unique `(cluster_id, name)` | `text id` |
| `flux_meta_idempotency` | Request-id ledger; TTL via `expires_at` | `text request_id` |

Three new pgEnums: `flux_engine`, `flux_cluster_status`, `flux_size`. All FKs CASCADE on cluster delete.

### Engine discriminator choice

Single `flux_meta_clusters` table with an `engine` enum column rather than per-engine tables. Rationale: all three streaming backends share the same shape (orgId / projectId / size / status / lxcIds / tags / brokerCount / replicationFactor) plus a tiny set of optional knobs (`schema_registry_enabled`, `management_ui_port`). Splitting would force three joins on every `listClusters({ engine })` filter and complicate the credentials FK. The discriminator keeps the hot read path one query.

## SQL migration

`apps/web/src/lib/server/db/migrations/0004_create_flux_meta_tables.sql` — hand-written via `pnpm db:new` (drizzle-kit retired in PR #28). Parent created before all children in the same transaction; the FK-ordering gotcha from PR #27 doesn't apply (no incoming FK type changes).

## Postgres adapter

`apps/web/src/lib/server/flux/postgres-adapter.ts` implements `PostgresBackendAdapter<FluxStoreData>`. The `upsertOne("idempotencyRecords", item)` branch routes the SPI's stable identifier to the table's `request_id` column (deviates from the `id`-based convention used by the other 3 collections — documented in-file).

## Store SPI wiring

`apps/web/src/lib/server/flux/store.ts` now uses `getStoreBackend()` with module id `flux`. JSON mode is bit-for-bit equivalent to the pre-refactor implementation — verified by the existing 80-test `tests/flux/01-store.integration.test.ts` + `02-service-business-logic.test.ts` suite. A custom `getItemId` resolves to `requestId` for IdempotencyRecord rows; `id` for everything else.

`deleteCluster` branches on `backend.backendType`: Postgres mode uses native `deleteEntity` (FK CASCADE handles children); JSON mode preserves the legacy snapshot-rewrite cascade.

## Migrate-stores mapper

`scripts/migrate-stores/modules/flux.ts` covers all 4 collections:
- `clusters` → `flux_meta_clusters` (with `engine`/`size`/`status` discriminators)
- `credentials` → `flux_meta_credentials` (preserves `revokedAt`)
- `topics` → `flux_meta_topics`
- `idempotencyRecords` → `flux_meta_idempotency` (conflict target = `request_id`; non-enumerable alias attached on `fromRow` so the runner's reverse-direction dedup works — mirrors the audit `external_id` trick)

Registered (append-only) in `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/index.ts`.

| File | Tests | Status |

| `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/flux.test.ts` | 10 new | All pass |

body:
Migrates the Atlas meta store (`.atlas-store.json`) from encrypted JSON to Postgres behind the StoreBackend SPI. Atlas is the data product that manages customer-facing PostgreSQL/MariaDB clusters on LXC containers — this PR carries the *metadata* about those clusters, not the customer DB contents.

Mirrors the established Beacon (#21) / Aegis (#24) / Marketing (#23) shape: same lazy-singleton, env-flip toggle, zero-regression JSON-mode default.

## Tables (0004_create_atlas_meta_tables.sql)

| Table | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `atlas_clusters` | One row per Atlas cluster | text PK, jsonb `lxc_ids`/`tags`, pgEnums for engine/size/status/ha_mode |
| `atlas_credentials` | DB users on clusters | text PK, FK `cluster_id` ON DELETE CASCADE |
| `atlas_idempotency_records` | 24h request-id ledger | `request_id` PK, indexes on `expires_at` + `resource_id` |

All CREATE TABLE — no ALTER on incoming-FK columns. SQL written by hand via `pnpm db:new`, not `drizzle-kit generate`.

## Files

- `apps/web/src/lib/server/db/schema/atlas.ts` — drizzle types
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/db/migrations/0004_create_atlas_meta_tables.sql` — DDL
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/postgres-adapter.ts` — lossless row↔domain mapping
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/store.ts` — refactored to use `getStoreBackend()`
- `apps/web/src/lib/server/atlas/store.test.ts` — 15 JSON-mode regression tests
- `apps/web/tests/atlas/01-store.integration.test.ts` — patched `withStorePath` helper to call `resetAtlasStoreBackendForTesting()` around its env-var swaps (required by the new lazy singleton)
- `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/atlas.ts` — JSON ↔ Postgres mapper
- `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/atlas.test.ts` — 8 round-trip tests (mapper sanity + e2e + idempotency + empty store)
- `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/index.ts` — append-only registration

## Atlas-specific decisions

- **IdempotencyRecord uses `requestId` as its natural PK** (not `id`). The custom `getItemId` in store.ts handles both shapes; the Postgres adapter routes the SPI id to `atlas_idempotency_records.request_id`. The mapper aliases `requestId` as a non-enumerable `request_id` so the migrate-stores runner can dedupe on reverse roundtrips without polluting the recovered JSON shape (same pattern audit uses for `external_id`).
- **`saveIdempotencyRecord` sweeps expired rows** before inserting. The sweep is preserved at the store layer so both backends behave identically. In Postgres mode this is a single full `save()` — slightly heavier than upsert but keeps semantics.
- **`deleteCluster` cascades to credentials** in both modes: JSON mode via the full-snapshot save, Postgres mode via FK ON DELETE CASCADE as defence-in-depth.
- **jsonb arrays (`lxc_ids`, `tags`)** are serialized via JSON.stringify in the mapper for MemoryDriver parity, and parsed back through a tolerant helper that accepts both string and array shapes.
