- 8/8 mapper tests pass (`pnpm test:migrate-stores`)
- 15/15 store regression tests pass + 24/24 existing integration tests pass (`pnpm vitest run src/lib/server/atlas/ tests/atlas/`)
- 95/95 migrate-stores tests pass overall
- Typecheck clean except the 3 pre-existing ignite-test errors (not introduced here)

`ATLAS_STORE_BACKEND=postgres` switches to the new backend at runtime. Default (unset or `=json`) stays on the legacy encrypted file.

This PR runs in parallel with `mesh`, `spark_meta`, `tide_meta`, `nexus_meta`, `flux_meta` migrations. Expected conflicts on:
- `scripts/migrate-stores/modules/index.ts` (each adds an entry — append-only)

title: fix(deploy-swarm): source /root/.env before ${PLACEHOLDER} substitution
body:
## Problem

Prod painel-cliente-api 1.16.8 (BB Calendar migration, PR #253) returned 500 on `/calendar-integrations/oauth/start` with:

```
BbCalendarError: BbCalendarClientFactory: CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID / CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_SECRET
must be set to obtain a service token for BB Calendar
```

## Root cause

`scripts/envs/.env.prod` intentionally leaves `CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID=${CATALISA_BB_CLIENT_ID}` and `_SECRET=${...}` as placeholders to avoid committing real service-account credentials in git. The actual values are kept in `/root/.env` on each swarm host (per `reference_stg_env_files.md`).

But the deploy script (`deploy-swarm.sh:371`) only sourced `${REMOTE_ENV_FILE}` (the SCP'd `.env.{stack}.deploy`), never `/root/.env` — so the `${PLACEHOLDER}` references never resolved and docker stack deploy passed empty strings.

Stg worked accidentally because `/root/.env` was always present in shell session env (perhaps from a different prior deploy).

## Fix

Source `/root/.env` BEFORE `${REMOTE_ENV_FILE}`, guarded by `[ -f /root/.env ]` so hosts without it still work:

```diff
-ssh "${SSH_OPTIONS[@]}" "$SWARM_HOST" "set -a && source ${REMOTE_ENV_FILE} && set +a && docker stack deploy ..."
+ssh "${SSH_OPTIONS[@]}" "$SWARM_HOST" "set -a && [ -f /root/.env ] && source /root/.env; source ${REMOTE_ENV_FILE} && set +a && docker stack deploy ..."
```

title: feat(ship): real drivers + OAuth-link CLI auth flow
body:
## Summary

Wires up real infra drivers behind `DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=true` and adds a device-flow auth subcommand so the CLI no longer needs a manually-managed bot token to talk to mgmt-api.

**Why now**: `bun ship:prod` previously always ran with mock drivers (`buildDrivers` threw when realInfraEnabled=true). Result: every `ship` invocation was theatrical, no real prod work happened, and migrations like `0010_cleanup_atlas_repl_test_zombies.sql` never reached prod. This PR is what's blocking real deploys.

## What changed

### Real drivers
- **`drivers/registry.ts`** — Docker Registry V2 `HEAD` manifest check. Follows a Bearer challenge once when the registry returns 401 (Harbor / GHCR / Docker Hub all speak the same dance). `parseImage` handles digests and nested repos.
- **`drivers/herald.ts`** — Posts deploy events to Loki using the same wire format as the web emitter. Nanosecond timestamps via BigInt to avoid 2^53 precision loss. Failures are swallow-by-default (best-effort observability — a Loki outage must not kill the deploy).
- **`index.ts` `buildDrivers(ResolvedConfig)`** — When realInfraEnabled, returns real ssh-builder + mgmt-api + registry + git + herald (Loki if configured, otherwise herald-mock). Fails fast with a friendly error if no bearer token is resolvable.
- **`config.ts` + `types.ts`** — New env knobs: `DEVELOPY_REGISTRY_USER/PASSWORD`, `DEVELOPY_HERALD_LOKI_URL/LABELS/USER/PASSWORD`, `DEVELOPY_BUILDER_IDENTITY_FILE`. All optional.

### OAuth-link CLI auth — `bun ship auth login | logout | status`

GitHub-device-code-style flow, no new UI build:

1. `POST /api/deploy/cli/init` → `{ code, verifyUrl, interval, expiresInSec }`
2. CLI prints the verifyUrl + 8-char code
3. User opens verifyUrl → existing Aegis login bounces them back to `/auth/cli?code=ABCD-1234`
4. The `/auth/cli` page POSTs `/api/deploy/cli/authorize` (`requireWriteSession`) which mints an HMAC-signed bearer via the existing `issueSession()` and binds it to the pending code
5. CLI poll loop hits `/api/deploy/cli/poll` until `status=approved`, then writes `~/.developy/auth.json` (mode 0600)

**Token resolution** in the CLI: `DEVELOPY_DEPLOY_BOT_TOKEN` env → `~/.developy/auth.json` → friendly error.

### Backend (`apps/web`)
- `lib/server/deploy/cli-auth-store.ts` — in-memory pending sessions, 10-min TTL, 32-bit codes, one-shot consume on poll. Documented swap-out point if web ever goes multi-instance behind an LB.
- 3 API routes under `/api/deploy/cli/`
- `/auth/cli` page (~140 LOC, no new design tokens — uses existing Card/Button)

## Tests

| Suite | New | Total |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/ship` | 32 | 113 (all passing) |
| `apps/web` cli-auth-store | 10 | 10 |
| typecheck | 0 new errors in `apps/web` or `scripts/ship` | |

## How to actually use this after merge

```bash
# One-time on workstation:
bun ship auth login           # opens browser to /auth/cli, you click Authorize
bun ship auth status          # confirms token saved

# Then any real deploy:
DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=1 bun ship prod web
```

For CI, set `DEVELOPY_DEPLOY_BOT_TOKEN` instead of running auth login.

## Notes

- The Loki Herald driver is purely additive over the deploy log file — if HERALD_LOKI_URL is unset, falls back to herald-mock with no behavioral change to the deploy itself.
- The CLI auth store is in-memory single-process — appropriate for v1 (sessions ≤10 min, single-shot). Persistence becomes necessary only when the web app scales horizontally; the swap-out point is documented in `cli-auth-store.ts`.
- This PR does NOT trigger any prod deploy by itself. It's what makes future deploys possible.

title: feat(deploy): migration + verify/current/tag-current/rollback endpoints
body:
## Summary

Server-side counterparts to the CLI's MgmtApiDriver. Previously the CLI's mgmt-api.ts (shipped in PR #37) was calling 6 endpoints that didn't exist — every `bun ship` hit a 404/hang on the migrate, verify, finalize and rollback phases. This PR closes that gap.

## What changed

**6 new API routes** (`apps/web/src/app/api/deploy/`):

| Route | Method | Auth | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/migrations/dry-run` | POST | write | Lists applied/pending + diff for env. Uses `scripts/db-migrate/runner.ts`. |
| `/migrations/apply` | POST | write | Applies pending in one-tx-per-file. Captures diff for audit. |
| `/verify` | GET | read | Returns errorRate/p95 + healthy bool. Synthetic until Radar/Pulse wired. |
| `/current` | GET | read | Current deployed sha per env+target. |
| `/tag-current` | POST | write | Finalize callback — records env→sha. |
| `/rollback` | POST | write | Records rollback intent + returns image to redeploy. |

**State store** (`apps/web/src/lib/server/deploy/current-store.ts`): small on-disk JSON keyed by `env:target`. Persists across mgmt-panel restarts (in-memory would forget on every deploy). Atomic write via tmp + rename. Write failures logged but non-fatal.

## Safety: per-env DATABASE_URL with no silent fallback

Migration endpoints resolve **`DATABASE_URL_<ENV>` only** — they refuse to fall back to a generic `DATABASE_URL`. The mgmt panel deployment must explicitly set `DATABASE_URL_PROD`, `DATABASE_URL_STAGING`, `DATABASE_URL_MGMT`. This prevents the catastrophic class of bug where a dev mgmt panel accidentally migrates against prod DB (or vice versa). Verified locally: missing var → HTTP 400 with clear message.

## End-to-end verification

Tested locally against `pnpm dev` on :3000:

```
$ bun ship auth login    # OAuth-link flow, token saved to ~/.developy/auth.json
$ DEVELOPY_REAL_INFRA_ENABLED=1 \
  DEVELOPY_MGMT_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 \
  bun ship staging web --skip=build,deploy,verify,finalize
▶ preflight   passed (branch+sha+push)         ✓
▶ build       skipped (--skip)                  ✓
▶ migrate     POST /api/deploy/migrations/dry-run
              → HTTP 400 'DATABASE_URL_STAGING not set'  ← correct refusal
```

End-to-end: CLI auth → bearer attached → `requireWriteSession` validates → endpoint executes safety check → CLI surfaces error cleanly. **All wire-up works.**

## How prod cleanup of the 6 atlas zombies actually finishes

This PR makes the chain functional, but the actual prod cleanup still needs (one of):

1. `DATABASE_URL_PROD=<prod url> pnpm db:apply` — directly on workstation with prod creds. Simplest path. Bypasses ship entirely.
2. `bun ship prod web` from a mgmt panel that has `DATABASE_URL_PROD` configured + real SSH keys to builder VM. Most complete path. Still needs real driver wiring on the *server side* (apps/web/src/lib/server/deploy/drivers.ts has its own stubs — out of scope here, follow-up).

## Tests

- Atlas suite: 28/28 (04-discovery.unit.test.ts) + cli-auth-store: 10/10. No regression.
- Typecheck: zero new errors in `apps/web` or `scripts/ship`.
- End-to-end ship CLI → real endpoint hit on localhost confirmed.

## Out of scope

- Server-side SSH/Proxmox/Mgmt drivers in `apps/web/src/lib/server/deploy/drivers.ts` are still stubs. The deploy worker that processes `/api/deploy/jobs` calls these — making the deploy phase real needs that wiring. Separate PR.

title: feat(wpp): Baileys outbound webhooks via webhooks-engine parity
body:
## Summary

Brings `wpp` (Baileys) to feature parity with `wpp-business` for outbound webhook delivery. Subscribers register a `WppDispatcher`; the `webhooks-engine` BB handles signing, retry, and HTTP delivery. Same architecture, but **without** the four debts inherited by wpp-business:

| Debt avoided | wpp-business has it | wpp does NOT |
|---|---|---|
| `httpMethod` column (dead field) | yes | dropped |
| Per-dispatcher `signingSecret` duplicating `WebhookSigningKey` infra | yes | dropped |
| `customHeaders` as `String? @db.Text` (JSON-in-text) | yes | proper `Json?` column |
| `retryConfig` duplicated in dispatcher + subscription | yes | single source on subscription |

## Key design choices

- **`WppDispatcher` model** with `deviceId` pre-filter (Baileys equivalent of `phoneNumberId`) and JSONPath `conditions` for ADVANCED mode.
- **Dispatch-specific re-publish trick**: when `deviceId` or `conditions` is set, the subscription filter becomes `wpp.dispatch.{id}` and the matched event is re-published in `evaluateDispatchers` — engine only sees events that passed pre-filtering. No payload leak across subscribers.
- **`wpp.v1.*` event namespace** published in parallel to legacy `wpp.*`. Internal consumers stay on legacy; external subscribers filter on `wpp.v1.*`. Painel adaptation is out of scope.
- **`emitWppPublic` helper** in `src/wpp/lib/public-events.ts` wires every user-facing publish point (message/device/chat/group/contact) without touching service constructors.
- **`DispatcherService` registered in `registerPostFacadeServices`** so it can resolve `WebhooksEngineFacadeToken`. Same pattern as `WppBizDispatcherService`. **Bug found and fixed during smoke** — initial attempt registered in `registerWpp` which runs before `registerFacades`.
- **Anti-SSRF validation** on `endpointUrl` (Zod refine blocks localhost, RFC1918, link-local, `.internal`, `.local`).
- **Permissions** `WPP_DISPATCHERS_READ` / `WPP_DISPATCHERS_WRITE` added to IAM types.

## Smoke tested end-to-end (real traffic)

1. ✅ Monolith boot — 28 modules load, facades register
2. ✅ Login admin@catalisa.app — token carries `WPP_DISPATCHERS_*`
3. ✅ `POST /wpp/api/v1/dispatchers` → 201 + subscription auto-created in webhooks-engine via facade
4. ✅ Subscription in DB: `event_filters = {wpp.v1.message.received.text}`
5. ✅ Real device-create code path: `POST /wpp/api/v1/devices` triggered `wpp.v1.device.status.changed` → consumer delivered HTTP 200 to httpbin (541ms)
6. ✅ Device delete: `wpp.v1.device.disconnected` delivered (200)
7. ✅ Per-device dispatcher with `deviceId=target-A`: raw `wpp.v1.*` events for device-B did NOT route to it (only re-published `wpp.dispatch.{id}` events did)
8. ✅ `GET /wpp/api/v1/dispatchers/:id/delivery-logs` returned the log via the facade
9. ✅ `DELETE /:id` soft-deletes dispatcher + cascades `DISABLED` on webhooks-engine subscription

## Out of scope (follow-up PRs)

- **Painel adaptation**: `bb-events.controller.ts` `translateBbEvent` needs to accept `wpp.v1.*` shapes so workflows can be triggered by Baileys messages
- **wpp-business debt cleanup**: drop `httpMethod`, drop per-dispatcher `signingSecret`, convert `customHeaders` to `Json`, remove duplicated `retryConfig`. Requires data migration for existing rows
- **Integration/E2E tests**: blocked by pre-existing `prisma/migrations/20260410000000_add_meta_account` shadow-DB bug
- **`MESSAGE_STATUS_UPDATED`** is declared but unused in services (pre-existing; not regression)
- **`WEBHOOK_MASTER_KEY`** placeholder in prod — should rotate before exposing dispatchers to non-painel clients

title: feat(mesh+atlas): networks as first-class IPAM + IPv6 default + UI
body:
## Summary

Atlas — and any future data product — now allocates IPs from named **networks** in Mesh instead of hash-modulo'd vmid math. Default network is the operator's **public IPv6 /56**, so new databases get publicly-routed IPv6 addresses with **no NAT mangling**.

Closes the gap the user raised: "queremos disponibilizar a capacidade de todo usuário poder ter e configurar a sua rede ou usar IPs alugados nossos."

## What changed

### Schema (3 migrations)

| # | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 0011 | `mesh_ip_pools` gains `bridge`, `nameservers`, `dns_search` | A pool now fully describes a Proxmox network — provisioners read one record. |
| 0012 | `atlas_clusters` gains `network_pool_id`, `ip_allocation_id` | Each cluster remembers which pool it pulled from + the allocation id so deprovision releases properly. |
| 0013 | `mesh_ip_pools` gains `source` enum (`platform-rented` / `byo`) + `parent_pool_id` FK | Sets up the SaaS model where orgs rent /64s from us or bring their own range. |

### Mesh

- **`lib/server/mesh/networks.ts`** (new) — `getOrCreateDefaultNetwork()` bootstrap. First call seeds the default pool from `DATA_PRODUCTS_*` env; subsequent calls read it.
- **`/mesh/networks` UI** (new) — single page listing every pool with family badge, source badge, used/total counter. Create dialog with family/CIDR/bridge/gateway/nameservers/source. Delete gated on zero active allocations.
- Engine, validation, postgres-adapter all extended for the new fields.

### Atlas

- Provisioner now allocates IPs through Mesh (`reserveAddress` / `releaseAllocation`). serviceId=clusterId, so the deprovisioner can find every allocation tied to this cluster (including replica IPs) and release them.
- **Family-aware**: when the pool is IPv6, uses `ip6=`/`gw6=` on Proxmox net0 instead of `ip=`/`gw=`. Sets `ip=manual` so Debian's `iface eth0 inet dhcp` doesn't block ifupdown from reaching the `inet6` stanza (root cause of the first IPv6 e2e failure).
- Endpoint string respects the family:
  - IPv4 private pool: NAT, `<public-host>:<5000+vmid>`
  - IPv6 public pool: no NAT, `[<ipv6>]:5432` per RFC 3986
- `CreateAtlasClusterInput` accepts optional `networkPoolId`; null falls back to default.

## End-to-end validation (against prod 2026-05-15)

```
POST /api/atlas/clusters {engine:postgresql, size:xs}
13:43:56 requested
13:43:56 provisioning, IP=2804:1740:f:2000::4/56 from pool 'default'
13:44:11 configuring (apt over IPv6, AAAA-resolved deb.debian.org)
13:46:02 active — [2804:1740:f:2000::4]:5432   ← 1m 12s total
13:46:02 herald cluster.provisioned → success
```

TCP to `[2804:1740:f:2000::4]:5432` accepted from a public-IPv6 host. `SELECT version()` returns Postgres 17.10. Delete path also validated end-to-end.

## Operational state changes already applied to prod

These ran against `developy_mgmt` during the validation and stay in place:

- `MESH_STORE_BACKEND=postgres` set in LXC 9100's `/etc/developy/web.env` (Mesh was silently running JSON-mode; that's why the test pool that worked in-memory "disappeared" between sessions).
- 3 platform pools created:
  - `default` — `2804:1740:f:2000::/56` IPv6 on `vmbr0`, gw `::1`
  - `platform-ipv4-internal` — `172.10.0.0/24` on `vmbr1` (legacy NAT)
  - `platform-ipv4-public` — `177.104.184.32/29` on `vmbr0` (your 5 usable public IPv4s)
- 72 infra IP allocations marked `service_id=infrastructure-reserved` covering known hosts, gateways, and the .1 trap.

The 3 new migrations are recorded in `__migrations`.

## Tests

- typecheck on `apps/web` clean (zero new errors).
- Atlas suite still 198/243 (45 skipped Proxmox-only, 1 e2e fail unchanged from before).
- Live e2e against prod with IPv6 — green.

## Known gaps tracked for the next PR

- **Tenant scoping on pool API** — today `/api/mesh/ipam/pools` trusts whatever `tenantId` the body carries. Once Aegis has an org-membership resolver, POST should force `tenantId=session.org` and GET should filter by it. Schema is already tenant-aware (unique on `tenant_id, name`).
- **Subnet carving** — `POST /pools/:id/sub-pools` that simultaneously reserves the child range in the parent and creates a child pool with `parentPoolId=parent`. Today operators do it manually in two steps.
- **Default-network selector in Atlas create dialog** — currently implicit. Drop-down on cluster create would let users pick any of their networks.
- **IPAM reconciliation cron** — `reconcileAgainstInventory` exists in the engine; needs a scheduled run to import existing Proxmox state into mesh_ip_allocations (today the 172.10.0.x LXCs aren't tracked).

title: fix(atlas+mesh): unblock /128 pools, surface silent provisioner crashes, DNS-safe names
body:
## Why

User reported via UI: created an Atlas cluster pinning network=teste6 (a /128 IPv6 pool, `2804:1740:f:2000::301/128`) using the new \`<NetworkSelect>\` widget. Cluster row saved with the right \`networkPoolId\`, returned 200, then sat in \`status=requested\` forever with zero logs and zero UI signal.

Three orthogonal bugs combined to hide the failure end-to-end.

## What

### 1. \`enumerateIPv6Addresses\` returned \`[]\` for /128 pools
Loop was \`for (let i=1; i<cap; i++)\` to skip offset 0 (network address). For /128 \`cap=1\`, loop never runs. \`reserveAddress\` then threw \`POOL_EXHAUSTED\` on a pool with 0/1 allocated.

Fix: \`startOffset = poolSize <= 1n ? 0 : 1\` — for /127 and /128, include offset 0. IPv6 has no broadcast and the network address of a small prefix is routable.

### 2. \`createAtlasCluster\` swallowed every async provisioner error
\`provisionAtlasCluster(id).catch(() => {})\` — any throw before the first \`[Atlas] Cluster X: provisioning\` log (in getIPPool, detectPoolConflict, reserveAddress) was completely invisible. Operators had to grep pg_stat_activity or guess.

Fix: log the error with stack so the next blip is actionable.

### 3. Cluster names allowed \`_\` but Proxmox hostnames don't
The name is embedded in \`hostname: \`atlas-\${name}-primary\`\`. Proxmox validates as RFC-1123. \`teste-select_network\` saved fine via the schema but Proxmox 400'd LXC create with \`\"invalid format - value does not look like a valid DNS name\"\`.

Fix:
- tighten the schema regex to DNS-safe at request time (clear error message instead of opaque Proxmox 400 later)
- sanitize defensively at hostname construction (\`name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/g, '-')\`) so legacy rows still provision

### 4. \`requested\` + \`provisioning\` now deletable
Previously \`deletableStatuses = [active, failed, degraded]\`. Stuck rows had to be cleaned via direct DB DELETE. Now operators can clean them via the API/UI path. Safe — those statuses imply no LXC nor allocation.

## End-to-end validation (prod, 2026-05-16)

After deploying the fixes, recreated the same cluster (\`teste-select-network\` → teste6):

\`\`\`
t=  5s status=provisioning  lxcIds=[]    alloc=ipalloc-..mp27ug
t= 20s status=configuring   lxcIds=[147] alloc=ipalloc-..mp27ug
t=125s status=active        lxcIds=[147] endpoint=[2804:1740:f:2000::301]:5432
\`\`\`

Pool teste6 went from \`0/1\` → \`1/1\` allocated. TCP probe \`nc 2804:1740:f:2000::301 5432\` returns OK from the hypervisor.

- [x] Manual: name with \`_\` rejected at POST with clear message

## Summary
Wave B migration `0015_atlas_v2_databases.sql` failed on real Postgres with `syntax error at or near "collation"`. The column name is a SQL-reserved word — pg-mem accepts it (so unit tests passed), but `developy_mgmt` rejects the CREATE TABLE.

## Summary

Follow-up to #54 with two fixes caught immediately after deploying to prod.

### Behavior change requested by the user
- Don't render the queue position to the user — they're collecting interest, not running a literal numbered queue
- Drop the "convite em até 72h" + "primeira VM em 4 minutos" promises — the team will invite one-by-one when they can support each user properly
- Drop the "1.847 / 2.000 vagas" anchor in the /services FAQ

The success screen now says:
> **tá com a gente.** _vamos te chamar._
>
> Boa. O beta tá fechado — a gente abre vaga por vaga, conforme o time consegue dar suporte humano. Quando chegar a sua, mandamos um email direto.

The position is still captured server-side (for idempotency + the queue is real, just not customer-facing) and sent to GA4 for analytics purposes only.

### Bug fix — analytics.js was 404-falling-back to index.html
The Caddy Dockerfile copies static assets explicitly:
```
COPY public/styles.css   /srv/styles.css
COPY public/favicon.svg  /srv/favicon.svg
…
```
`analytics.js` (added in #54) wasn't listed, so requests to `/analytics.js` hit `try_files {path} {path}.html /index.html` and silently received the 53KB SPA shell with `content-type: text/html`. No GA custom events would have fired in prod.

After the fix, `curl -sI https://developy.cloud/analytics.js` returns `content-type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the right 24KB payload.

title: fix(wpp): persistir pairing code no device (paridade com QR)

## Diagnóstico (confirmado ao vivo)

A geração do pairing code **funciona** (Baileys retorna o código; gerei `Y1G2PSVX` real para 5511930802555 no org 0001). O bug: o código é gravado **só na operation result**, nunca em `device.pairingCode`. O QR, em contraste, é persistido em `device.lastQr` (`session-manager.ts`). - **Não toca** socket/connect/QR.

title: fix(wpp): browser Chrome p/ pairing code (companion_platform_id=1)
body:
## Diagnóstico (fundamentado no código do Baileys)

Pairing code era **gerado** mas o vínculo falhava ("não foi possível conectar"); **QR funciona**.

- `requestPairingCode` (Baileys `socket.js`) envia `companion_platform_id = getPlatformId(browser[1])`.
- Socket usava `Browsers.macOS('Desktop')` → `browser[1]='Desktop'` → `getPlatformId` = **DESKTOP (7)**.

- Bug conhecido da 7.0.0-rc.9: WhiskeySockets/Baileys#2306 ("browser format must be 'Name (OS)'", usa `Browsers.macOS("Chrome")`). **Sem downgrade.**

## Fix (1 linha)
`baileys-driver.ts`: `Browsers.macOS('Desktop')` → `Browsers.macOS('Chrome')` → `['Mac OS','Chrome','14.4.1']`, `companion_platform_id=1`.
- Compartilhado com QR; risco baixo (Chrome/1 é o padrão; QR já tolera 7, tolera 1).

title: fix(email/calendar): point OAuth callback at standalone (:7621/:7620), not monolith :3099
body:
## Problem

The bootstrap email/calendar provider-configs baked `redirect_uri = http://localhost:3099/...` (the old **monolith** port) **inside the encrypted credentials**. Standalone runs email on `:7621` and calendar on `:7620`, so that callback 404s and the OAuth round-trip can't complete. `redirect_uri` is read from the stored credentials (`google.auth.ts`) and Google enforces it again at token-exchange, so this can't be patched at request time — the stored value must change.

## Change

- **`scripts/fix-oauth-callback-standalone.ts`** — idempotent, **reversible** rewrite of the `redirect_uri` inside the encrypted email/calendar provider-config credentials.
  - Backs up the exact prior ciphertext before changing (byte-exact restore, **no master key needed** to revert): `--restore <backup.json>`.
  - **Parameterized by host** (`EMAIL_CALLBACK_BASE` / `CALENDAR_CALLBACK_BASE`, `OAUTH_FIX_ORG`) so the *same* script targets a **prod public https callback** later — nothing dev-only is baked one-way.
  - `--dry-run` to preview.
- **`email-oauth-bootstrap.ts`** — `HOST` is now env-driven (`EMAIL_BB_HOST`, default standalone `:7621`) so a re-bootstrap can't reintroduce `:3099`.
- **`.gitignore`** — ignores the backup JSON (it contains credential ciphertext).

## Scope / safety

- Applied to the **dev** org `b0000000-…001` (2 email configs → `:7621`). Verified end-to-end via the operacao-digital app proxy: `/email/connect` now emits `redirect_uri=…:7621`.
- **Prod is untouched** — separate DB, its own configs (public https). The script + bootstrap are parameterized for a prod https callback.
- Reversibility proven by round-trip: apply → `:7621`, `--restore` → `:3099` (byte-exact), re-apply → `:7621`.

## Follow-ups (out of band, console-only)

- Whitelist `http://localhost:7621/email/api/v1/email/connections/callback` (+ `:7620` calendar) in the Google + Microsoft OAuth apps' authorized redirect URIs (Google allows http only for localhost → device reaches it via `adb reverse`).
- Calendar has **no** provider-config yet — create one, then run this script to set its `:7620` callback.

title: fix(spark+ipam): valkey DNS resolve + collision-free LXC IP allocation
body:
Dois fixes que destravam o provisionamento de data-products (descobertos provisionando o staging da operacao-digital):

## 1. Spark DNS (`fix/spark`)
Provisionar Spark falhava com `Could not resolve host: packages.valkey.io`. O LXC herdava resolver do ISP porque `DATA_PRODUCTS_NAMESERVER` está vazio no control-plane deployado e `createLxcContainer` só seta nameserver se truthy. Fix: default `1.1.1.1 8.8.8.8` + fixa `/etc/resolv.conf` no container antes do apt/curl (valkey+memcached).

## 2. IPAM colisão (`fix/ipam`) — root cause do outage do mgmt-db

title: fix(create): drop per-NIC firewall (breaks NAT egress)
body:
## Problem
Every VM/Container created by the wizard lost internet access. Root cause: the wizards defaulted **`firewall=1`** on net0, which makes Proxmox build a firewall bridge (`fwbr`) in front of the NIC. On this cluster that fwbr **breaks the NAT/conntrack path** for the guest — the masquerade rule matches but `nf_nat` never translates the source, so packets egress the WAN bridge with the **private IP** → no reply → no internet. (This also broke the cicustom guest-agent install from #67.)

## Evidence
- Internal container `172.10.0.100` (no per-NIC firewall) → NAT translates → `[ASSURED]`, internet works.
- VM with `firewall=1` → masquerade matches but no SNAT → private src egresses → 100% loss.
- Flipping the **same VM** to `firewall=0` → instant egress (`ping`, `https`, `apt`). NAT itself was never broken.

(An earlier kernel-regression hypothesis was wrong — ruled out by comparing against a working guest.)

## Fix
- Default **firewall off** and **remove the firewall toggle** from both the VM and Container create wizards; `net0` never adds `firewall=1`.
- Safe here: the cluster/node firewall is disabled and traffic policy lives in Mesh, so the per-NIC firewall provided no real filtering — only the broken NAT path.

## Test
- Typecheck clean (pre-existing mesh/ignite test errors unrelated).
- Verified live on a real VM: firewall=0 → egress + guest-agent install both work.

title: fix(db): make migrations 0013–0017 idempotent
body:
## What
Make migrations `0013`–`0017` safe to re-apply (idempotent), and document the convention.

These used bare `CREATE TYPE` / `CREATE TABLE` / `ADD COLUMN` / `ADD CONSTRAINT` (no `IF NOT EXISTS`). When their schema had been applied to a DB whose `__migrations` tracker didn't record them, `pnpm db:apply` aborted on `"already exists"` and couldn't reconcile.

- `CREATE TABLE/INDEX/UNIQUE INDEX` → `IF NOT EXISTS`
- `ADD COLUMN` → `IF NOT EXISTS`
- `CREATE TYPE` / `ADD CONSTRAINT` (no `IF NOT EXISTS` form) → wrapped in `DO $$ … EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN null; END $$;`
- README: idempotency authoring convention for future migrations.

## Why
On 2026-06-09 prod's `__migrations` had drifted *behind* the actual schema (the atlas-v2 / mesh wave-2 changes were applied outside the unified runner). The tracker was reconciled record-only, but the underlying non-idempotency is what made `db:apply` unusable for reconciliation. This prevents a recurrence: a fresh-DB apply and any re-apply are now safe no-ops.

These migrations are already applied everywhere; the runner tracks by filename, so editing the SQL does **not** trigger a re-run on existing DBs — it only affects fresh setups and any future re-apply.

## Testing
Verified on a throwaway Postgres 16: applied `0000–0019` once (all clean), then re-applied `0013–0017` against the populated schema — **all clean no-ops**. (`pnpm test:db-migrate` covers runner logic with a mocked driver; it's untouched.)

title: fix(spark): deprovisioner must not swallow LXC delete failures
body:
## What
The Spark deprovisioner swallowed `pct destroy` failures: a failed delete was only `console.error`'d, then the cluster was marked `deleted` and a `success` Herald event emitted **unconditionally**. So a container that couldn't be removed (e.g. the stale-dm `lvremove ... contains a filesystem in use` case) survived as an **untracked orphan** while the system reported the cluster gone.

This is exactly how the 2026-06-09 smoke left CTs `160/164/165/166` behind (see `docs/storage-and-node-placement.md` §5).

## Fix
- Track which LXCs failed to delete.
- IP-allocation release + DNS unsync still run best-effort (no resource leak).
- If **any** container survived: mark the cluster **`failed`** (a DELETABLE state, so the delete can be retried — the stale-dm case needs a node reboot first), emit a **`failure`** Herald event carrying the orphaned vmids, and **throw**.
- Only a fully-removed cluster becomes `deleted` / `success`.

Mirrors the existing provision-failure path (status `failed` + failure event).

## Testing
New regression test (`provisioner.deprovision.test.ts`): real JSON store + mocked Proxmox boundary — asserts that a failing LXC delete yields `status=failed` (not `deleted`), a `failure` event listing the orphan, and a throw; and that full success yields `deleted`/`success`. `pnpm typecheck` clean.

title: feat(workflows): OPENAI_ASSISTANT action — run an OpenAI Assistant (asst_...) via Assistants API
body:
## Summary

Adds a native workflow/canvas action **`OPENAI_ASSISTANT`** that runs an existing **OpenAI Assistant** (`asst_...`) through the OpenAI **Assistants API** (thread → message → run → poll → response), reusing the existing `AI_PROVIDER` credential and a generalized credential selector.

**Why a new action:** an `asst_...` lives entirely in OpenAI's Assistants API (stateful threads/runs + server-side `file_search` vector store). The existing `openai` provider uses Chat Completions (stateless, no RAG) and `AI_HUB_AGENT` is just a generic HTTP POST — neither can drive an `asst_...`. So this talks to the Assistants API directly.

### What it does
- Resolves an `AI_PROVIDER` credential (`provider=openai`) — **no credential enum change**.
- Reuses/creates a thread (`threadId` in/out → conversation memory, mirrors `AI_HUB_AGENT`).
- Creates a run on the assistant, polls to terminal state (honoring `timeoutMs`, default 120000).
- Strips `file_search` citation markers (`【…】`) from the reply.
- **Scope (v1):** retrieval/conversation assistants (`file_search`/`code_interpreter`). A run ending in `requires_action` (custom function tools) fails with a clear message — `submit_tool_outputs` loop is documented as Plan B.

### Config / Output
- **Config:** `credentialId` (req), `assistantId` (req), `message` (req), `threadId?`, `additionalInstructions?`, `timeoutMs?`
- **Output:** `response`, `threadId`, `runId`, `status`, `responseTime` (or `{ skipped: true }` on empty message)

### Wiring (full integration)
- **Backend:** Prisma enum + idempotent migration, `OpenAIAssistantHandler` (TDD, 11 unit tests), registry + module, validation `ACTION_SCHEMAS` + output-schemas + validator preview, `tools-executor` AI category, handler-type-consistency list, AI prompts/knowledge (incl. fixing `anti-patterns.md` so the AI builder no longer refuses the new type).
- **Frontend:** `OpenAIAssistantForm` + form registry, palette template, generalized `BbCredentialSelector` (backward-compatible — defaults preserve Catalisa BB behavior for its 10 existing callers), action taxonomy (Action Picker discoverability), icons, labels (ActionModal/EditableActionItem/ActionCard), defaults, help.

## Test Plan
- [x] Backend unit: handler 11/11 (new-thread, reuse-thread, empty-skip, missing credential/assistant/apiKey guards, annotation strip, `requires_action`, run failure, timeout)
- [x] Regression sweep: `workflows` + `ai-assistant/tools` modules — **1331 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed**
- [x] Backend type gate `tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` clean (on the original verified base)
- [x] Frontend `tsc && vite build` clean
- [x] Cross-layer config-key consistency (form ↔ handler ↔ template) verified
- [ ] **Live e2e smoke (manual):** with the stack up + an `AI_PROVIDER`/openai credential + a real `asst_...` — run an `OPENAI_ASSISTANT` action, confirm `output.response` (no `【…】`) and `output.threadId`, then a second action reusing the `threadId` to confirm conversation memory.

## Deploy notes
- Apply the migration to target DBs (additive, idempotent): `ALTER TYPE "WorkflowActionType" ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'OPENAI_ASSISTANT';` — do **not** `prisma db push` on shared DBs.
- Frontend: hard refresh (Ctrl+Shift+R) after deploy to bust the bundle cache.

title: fix(deploy): add basePath prefix to MODULE_*_URL in prod stack
body:
## Problem
Prod BB moved to the `ghcr:production` image (standalone basePath migration), which mounts every service under its `/{service}` basePath. But the prod stack's inter-module `MODULE_*_URL` env vars still pointed at bare `http://<service>:3000`.

Result: `wpp-business → webhooks-engine` `createSubscription` hit `/api/v1/subscriptions` (no prefix) → **404 text/plain** → `response.json()` threw **"Failed to parse JSON"** → 502 → ingress dispatcher never registered → **inbound WhatsApp webhooks never delivered to the panel → MESSAGE_RECEIVED workflows stopped firing in prod**. Outbound + 'test integration' (polling) kept working, masking it. Staging was unaffected (still on the older pre-basePath image).

## Fix
Add the basePath to each `MODULE_*_URL` so the URLs match the served routes:
- `MODULE_IAM_URL` → `/iam`
- `MODULE_WEBHOOKS_ENGINE_URL` → `/webhooks-engine`
- `MODULE_DECISION_ENGINE_URL` → `/decision-engine`
- `MODULE_WPP_URL` → `/wpp`

Config-only (33 lines). Makes permanent the live hotfix already applied via `docker service update` on `bb-production_wpp-business`, so the next `docker stack deploy bb-production` won't revert it.

## Note
`docker-stack.staging.yml` intentionally NOT changed: staging still runs the older image that serves at root, so adding prefixes there would break it until staging adopts the basePath image.

title: feat(harbor): Phase 1 — registry module + read-only catalog
body:
First slice of the Harbor (container registry / ECR-equivalent) implementation. Full plan in **`docs/harbor-plan.md`** (also added here).

## What's in Phase 1 (this PR)
A working, read-only registry **catalog** module, wired into the dashboard nav, following the data-product module pattern:

- **Module** `harbor.module.ts` (Overview + Repositories) registered in `modules/registry.ts` → **appears in the menu**. Color already existed in `design-tokens`.
- **DataSource** (mirrors Radar/Pulse `DataSource`): `HARBOR_DATASOURCE=mock|registry`.
  - `mock` (default) — static catalog so the UI works **before** a real registry exists.
  - `registry` — resilient **Distribution (`registry:2`) v2** client (`/v2/_catalog`, `/v2/<name>/tags/list`, manifest digest + layer sizes). Network failures degrade to empty results + `unreachable` health (never throws). Optional Basic auth via `HARBOR_REGISTRY_URL` / `_USERNAME` / `_PASSWORD`.
- **API** `GET /api/harbor/{overview,repositories,repositories/<name…>}`, `{data}`/`{error}` envelope; repo-name validation blocks path traversal.
- **Hooks** `use-harbor.ts` + `queryKeys.harbor`.
- **Pages**: dashboard (stats + `docker login` hint), repositories (list), repository detail (tags/digests/sizes — catch-all `[...name]` because repo names contain `/`).

## Plan doc highlights (`docs/harbor-plan.md`)
- **Wrap Distribution**, not full Harbor OSS (thin control-plane, like Tide=MinIO / Spark=Valkey).
- **Aegis = single security plane** (per your question): **UI** uses the existing console login + `registry:read`/`registry:write` entitlements; **`docker` push/pull** uses a **Registry v2 token service** backed by Aegis with device-code/robot credentials (Phase 2).
- **Beacon DNS record** for `registry.developy.cloud` made an explicit deliverable (via the `getDnsBackend()`/PowerDNS write path).
- Blob storage → **Tide/MinIO** (S3 driver) in Phase 3.

## Not in this PR (next steps, per plan)
- Provisioning the real `registry:2` LXC + the Beacon DNS record (infra/ops sub-step of Phase 1) → makes `registry.developy.cloud` real and unblocks `bun ship`/Ignite.
- Phase 2: Aegis token service + namespaces + push/pull.

## Test

- `pnpm build`: compiled successfully; `/harbor/dashboard`, `/harbor/repositories`, `/harbor/repositories/[...name]`, `/api/harbor/[...path]` all build.

title: feat(harbor): Phase 2a — Registry v2 token service (Aegis-backed)
body:
Phase 2 of Harbor (plan: `docs/harbor-plan.md`). Implements the **Docker Registry v2 token auth service** so `docker login`/pull/push authenticate against **Aegis** — the security model you asked about.

## What
- **`registry-token.ts`** — RS256 JWT signer with `x5c` header, hand-rolled on `node:crypto` (no new dependency, so no lockfile churn).
- **`registry-scopes.ts`** — parse Docker scope strings, namespace(=org) extraction, entitlement→granted-actions mapping.
- **`GET /api/harbor/token`** (the registry `realm`) — Basic-auth password = a platform bearer; resolves the subject's registry entitlements **per namespace** (baseline ∪ IAM role, same engine as `vm:delete`) and issues a scoped JWT.
- **`POST /api/harbor/registry-token`** — mints a 24h `docker login` credential for the logged-in user (reuses `issueSession`, like the `bun ship` CLI token).
- IAM roles gain `registry:pull|push|delete` (viewer=pull, member=pull+push, admin/owner=+delete).
- **Registry datasource self-token**: the app is the issuer, so it self-signs a short read token for server-side catalog reads → switching the registry to `auth: token` (Phase 2b) won't break the Harbor UI.

## Safety
- Deploying this is **inert**: `/api/harbor/token` returns 503 until `HARBOR_TOKEN_KEY`/`CERT` are set, and the live registry stays no-auth until Phase 2b flips it (skopeo-verified first, reversible via `config.yml`).

## Test
- 7 new unit tests (scope parsing, entitlement mapping, **real RS256 signature verification** against the cert). 13 Harbor tests total, all green. `pnpm typecheck`/`build` clean.

## Next (Phase 2b)
Generate the signing keypair+cert, set `HARBOR_TOKEN_*` env, configure CT 172 registry `auth: token`, verify `skopeo login`/pull/push end-to-end, then external traefik ingress + TLS.

## What

- **\`DELETE /api/harbor/repositories/<name…>/tags/<tag>\`**: requires a session + \`registry:delete\` for the repo's namespace (baseline ∪ IAM role) → 401/403 otherwise.

title: feat(harbor): Phase 3 — push/delete webhooks (multi-tenant)
body:
Phase 3 webhooks — registry push/delete events fan out to user webhooks, **fully multi-tenant** (per your reminder that Harbor is multi-tenant).

## Tenant isolation
- A webhook belongs to a **namespace (= org/tenant)**. An event for `org/repo` only reaches that tenant's webhooks (`matchWebhooks` filters by namespace).
- A caller sees/creates/deletes **only** webhooks for namespaces they can push to (`registry:push` per namespace) — the operator baseline spans all, tenant users are scoped to their orgs. Same gate as the delete route (extracted to `authz.ts`).

## What
- `POST /api/harbor/events` — Distribution `notifications` sink (shared secret `HARBOR_EVENTS_SECRET`); keeps tagged manifest push/delete (drops per-blob noise) and dispatches.
- `webhook-store.ts` (encrypted JSON, `.harbor-store.json`) + `webhook-delivery.ts` (namespace/repo matching + **HMAC-SHA256** signed POST `X-Harbor-Signature: sha256=…`, delivery-status recording).
- `GET/POST /api/harbor/webhooks` + `DELETE /api/harbor/webhooks/[id]` — session + `registry:push` for the namespace; secret returned **only** on create.
- `/harbor/webhooks` management page + nav entry; hooks.
- **Tests**: cross-tenant exclusion, repoPattern, enabled/event filters, deterministic HMAC. 18 Harbor tests green; typecheck/build clean.

## Deploy step (after merge)
Set `HARBOR_EVENTS_SECRET` on LXC 9100 + add `notifications.endpoints` → `https://app.developy.cloud/api/harbor/events` to the registry config. Then push → webhook fires (e2e verify).

Follow-ups: GC, retention, Postgres-back the webhook store (Wave 2).

title: feat(harbor): Phase 3 — tag retention policies (multi-tenant)
body:
Phase 3 retention — auto-prune old tags, **multi-tenant**.

## What
- **Pure logic** `computeTagsToDelete`: `keepLast` always protects the N newest tags; `maxAgeDays` prunes the rest by age; **undatable tags are never pruned by an age rule** (fail safe).
- **Auto-runs on push** — the events route triggers retention for the pushed repo (non-blocking) — plus a manual **Apply now** endpoint.
- **Multi-tenant**: a policy belongs to a namespace (=org); CRUD + apply gated by `registry:delete` for that namespace (admin-level, like manual delete). Operator baseline spans all.
- Stores consolidated into one encrypted file (`harbor-json-store.ts`: webhooks + retention); `webhook-store` refactored onto it.
- **Registry `resolveTag` now reads the image config blob** for the real `created` (pushedAt) + os/arch — needed for recency ordering, and fills the previously-empty "Pushed" column in registry mode.
- API (`/api/harbor/retention` + `[id]` + `[id]/apply`), hooks, `/harbor/retention` page + nav.

## Test
- 5 new unit tests (keep-last, max-age, combined, fail-safe undatable). 23 Harbor tests green; typecheck/build clean.

GC (`registry garbage-collect`) to reclaim blob disk after pruning; Postgres-back the store; cron for pure age-based policies (today they run on next push / manual apply).

title: feat(harbor): Phase 3 — garbage collection trigger (admin)
body:
Phase 3 GC — reclaim disk from blobs orphaned by deleted/pruned tags.

## Design
The app can't run `registry garbage-collect` itself (it's a CLI on the registry host that needs the registry read-only), so `POST /api/harbor/gc` calls a small **GC agent** on the registry CT (`HARBOR_GC_URL` + `HARBOR_GC_SECRET`). ## What
- **Platform-admin only** (`requireAdminSession`) — GC is registry-wide and briefly takes the registry read-only, so it is **not** a per-tenant op (tenant `write` users → 403).
- `lib/server/harbor/gc.ts` (agent call, 180s timeout), `/api/harbor/gc` route (503 until configured, 502 on agent error), `useRunHarborGc` hook, and a **"Run GC"** card on the retention page showing reclaimed bytes.

## Deploy step
Install the GC agent (script + systemd service + weekly timer) on the registry CT, set `HARBOR_GC_URL`/`HARBOR_GC_SECRET` on LXC 9100. Then verify a real GC run.

title: feat(harbor): Phase 4 — Trivy vulnerability scanning (multi-tenant)
body:
Phase 4 — **Trivy vulnerability scanning** on push.

## Design
The app can't run Trivy (CLI that pulls images), so it calls a **scan agent** on the registry CT (`HARBOR_SCAN_URL` + `HARBOR_SCAN_SECRET`), passing a short-lived `system:scanner` pull bearer (the agent uses it to `docker pull` via the token flow).

## What
- `summarizeTrivy` (pure): Trivy JSON → per-severity counts. `scan.ts` mints the pull bearer → calls the agent → stores a `ScanResult` keyed by **digest** (immutable; re-tagging reuses the scan).
- **Auto-scan on push** via Next `after()` (runs post-response — scans are slow and must not block the registry notification's 5s timeout) + manual `POST /api/harbor/repositories/<name…>/tags/<tag>/scan` (gated `registry:pull`, **tenant-scoped**).
- Repo detail attaches the latest scan per tag; UI shows colored **C/H/M/L** badges + a per-tag **Scan** button.
- Tests: severity summarization + null/empty safety. 25 Harbor tests green; typecheck/build clean.

## Deploy step
Install the Trivy agent (binary + DB pre-warm + HTTP agent + secret) on the registry CT; set `HARBOR_SCAN_URL`/`HARBOR_SCAN_SECRET` on LXC 9100. Then scan a real image and confirm CVE counts.

title: fix(spark): IPv6 cluster support — bind, DNS-probe timeout, no duplicate IPs
body:
Fixes Spark provisioning on IPv6 Mesh pools, surfaced by a real prod valkey-sentinel cluster created via the UI that failed.

## Bugs fixed
1. **`bind 0.0.0.0` is IPv4-only** → on an IPv6 pool the primary never listened on its IPv6 address, so replicas couldn't attach (`connected_slaves:0`, Sentinel verification fails). valkey + sentinel now `bind * -::*`; memcached `-l 0.0.0.0,::`.
2. **wait-for-DNS used a bare `getent`** → hangs forever when the IPv6 resolver is unreachable, wedging the provision in `configuring`. Each probe is now wrapped in `timeout 5`.
3. **provision failure released Mesh IPs but left the LXCs running** → the next cluster reserved the same "freed" address while the orphan container still held it → duplicate IP / broken egress (observed: two CTs on `2804:…::401`). Now delete the LXC first and release its allocation only if the delete succeeded.
4. Same duplicate-IP guard applied to the **deprovision** path (a stale-dm `lvremove … in use` survivor keeps its IP reserved).

Adds an IPv6 `sentinelConf` regression test. 31 spark unit tests green; typecheck clean.

> Note: a companion **prod env** change (`DATA_PRODUCTS_STORAGE=local-lvm → nvme`) was also needed — data products were provisioning on the small/corrupted system thin pool instead of nvme, causing stuck-dm + hung container starts. That's an env fix (already applied), not code.

title: feat(launch): PR 4 — N replicas + load-balancing + scale (backend)
body:
Runs a Launch service as **N replica containers** (each its own managed LXC + Mesh IP) behind the public traefik route, which **load-balances across all healthy replicas** — and **scales up/down** by reconciling desired-vs-actual replica count.

## What's in this PR
- **Reconciler** (`reconcileLaunchService`): diffs `service.replicas` vs the live `LaunchReplica[]` — scale-down deprovisions highest-index replicas, scale-up provisions the missing indices (sequential, vmid-race-safe), then `finalizeService` rebuilds the traefik route from healthy replicas + derives status (all-healthy=`active`, some=`degraded`, none=`failed`).
- **Multi-replica provisioner**: the single-replica logic is now `provisionReplica(svc, index, …)` with per-replica rollback; lifecycle ops (stop/start/restart) loop over all replicas.
- **Load-balanced route**: `finalizeService` passes every healthy replica's `IP:port` as a traefik `loadBalancer.servers` entry (the PR 3 renderer already emits `loadBalancer.healthCheck`).
- **Scale**: `scaleLaunchService` (clamps [1,10], reconciles) + `POST /api/launch/services/:id/scale` + `useScaleLaunchService` hook.
- **Store**: per-replica `deleteReplica`; `replicas` flows through the create contract (1–10).

## What

Fixes the bug behind the **2026-06-12 Beacon DNS outage**: `app.developy.cloud`, `operacao-digital.ai` and other zones went intermittently NXDOMAIN/SERVFAIL.

`domains.notified_serial` is `BIGINT`, which **node-postgres returns as a string**. In `bumpSerial()`, `oldSerial + 1` therefore **concatenated** (`"2026061201" + 1 → "20260612011"`) instead of incrementing — appending a digit per zone mutation until the serial overflowed the 32-bit SOA serial space. PowerDNS then **REFUSED** the affected zones (`developy.cloud` serial reached `202606120111111`, `developy.io` `20260520011`).

## Changes

- New pure helper `nextSerial()` — coerces to a number, caps at `MAX_DNS_SERIAL` (4294967295), and falls back to today's serial for corrupt/overflowed inputs (self-healing).
- `getDomain` / `listDomains` coerce `notified_serial` with `Number()`.
- SQL fake now returns `notified_serial` as a **string** (mirroring real pg) so the regression is actually exercised.
- Unit tests for `nextSerial` (incl. the exact prod-corrupt values) + an end-to-end overflow regression test.

## Verification

- TDD-checked: reintroducing the bug fails the new e2e test; with the fix **19/19** backend tests pass, **88/88** across the beacon suite.
- Prod already remediated live (DB serials fixed + `systemd-resolved` masked on the NS CTs). Full write-up: `docs/incidents/2026-06-12-beacon-dns-outage.md`.

## Follow-ups (operational, not in this PR)

- Decommission the duplicate `::10` CT (123 vs 127).
- Add IPv4 glue for `ns1/2/3.developy.cloud` at Name.com (current glue is IPv6-only = single point of failure).

title: feat(launch): PR 5 — rolling redeploy (zero-downtime for N>1)
body:
Deploy a new image tag (or image/command/args) to a running service with **no user-facing downtime for multi-replica services** — an **in-place rolling update**: re-pull + re-run the new image inside each replica's existing LXC, **one replica at a time**, so the others keep serving via the load-balanced traefik route.

## What's in this PR
- **`redeployLaunchRollout`** (provisioner): walks the replicas sequentially, re-running `buildRunScript` (rm → pull new → run new) inside each LXC, health-checking, recording the new `runningTag`; `finalizeService` rebuilds the route + status. Reuses LXCs — no new provisioning, no apt install (just a re-pull), so it's fast and light on the cluster's flaky egress DNS.
- **`redeployLaunchService`** (service-layer): patches `tag` (+ optional `image`/`command`/`args` — the "command/args override"), marks `updating`, kicks the rollout.
- **API** `POST /api/launch/services/:id/redeploy` (guarded), **`useRedeployLaunchService`** hook, and a **Redeploy dialog + button** on the service detail page.

## e2e — zero-downtime proven live on prod
Created a 2-replica service → `active`. Triggered redeploy; curled both replica IPs every tick throughout the roll:
```
[2-3] r0=000 (rolling)  r1=200 (serving)
[6]   r0=200 (serving)  r1=000 (rolling)
[8]   active, both 200
```
**At every tick at least one replica returned 200** — the service never had a total outage. Replicas rolled one at a time, sequentially.

## Tests
77 launch unit/route tests (rollout service-layer + redeploy route + the existing suite). Typecheck launch-clean; build green.

Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-12-launch-pr5-rolling-redeploy.md`

## Note
This deploy also shipped the Beacon SOA-serial fix (#107) live to 9100 (the running build still had the buggy beacon). Verified: after the e2e's DNS create/delete churn, `pdnsutil check-zone developy.cloud` → 0 errors — the serial no longer corrupts on writes.

PR 6 (persistent volumes). Follow-ups: surge/blue-green for true zero-downtime at N=1; a tag-picker dropdown in the redeploy dialog; expose command/args in the create wizard.

title: fix(wpp): session-affinity routing — elimina "No active session" intermitente
body:
## Problema

Sockets Baileys vivem em memória por réplica (`session-manager.ts` `sessions: Map`). Jobs device-bound (`SEND_*`, `GROUP_OPS`, `PING`, `PAIRING_CODE`, `RECONNECT`, `RESET`, `DISCONNECT`, `DOWNLOAD_MEDIA`) iam para um consumer group único consumido por **qualquer** réplica → ~(N-1)/N caíam numa réplica sem o socket → `"No active session"` (`wpp-consumer.ts:269`). Prova em staging: 12 envios → 4 ok / 8 falha (3 réplicas). Não é LID nem Baileys — é roteamento.

## Solução

Roteamento por afinidade de device:

1. **Owner directory (Redis)** — `wpp:device-owner:<org>:<dev>` → `consumerName`, TTL 45s, refrescado pelo heartbeat do worker (30s < 45s). `OwnerRegistry.{claim,refresh,release,resolve}`.
2. **Inbox por réplica** — o producer resolve o dono e roteia jobs device-bound para `wpp:inbox:<consumerName>`, carregando o stream lógico original no campo `__stream`. O consumer lê só `[wpp:connect, wpp:session-restore, wpp:inbox:<self>]` e despacha pelo `__stream`.
3. **Park + restore quando offline** — sem dono → enfileira em `wpp:pending:<org>:<dev>` + dispara `SESSION_RESTORE`. Quando uma réplica estabelece o socket e reivindica o device, **dreina** o pending para seu inbox.
4. **Reclaim de órfãos (`XAUTOCLAIM`)** — entradas idle no PEL do inbox são re-resolvidas: se o dono mudou, re-roteia ao inbox do novo dono; se não há dono, re-parka + restore.
5. **Cluster-wide continua balanceado** — `CONNECT` e `SESSION_RESTORE` seguem no consumer group compartilhado.

### Correção vs. o plano: `PAIRING_CODE` é device-bound
O plano classificava `PAIRING_CODE` como cluster-wide. `handlePairingCode` faz `getSession` e chama `driver.requestPairingCode()` no **socket vivo** (`baileys-driver.ts:398`, lança `"socket not initialized"` sem socket) — logo precisa cair na réplica dona, senão sofre o mesmo bug. Reclassificado como device-bound (**13 device-bound / 2 cluster-wide**). QR **não** muda: não é job de fila; é efeito do `connection.update`, persistido em `device.lastQr` e lido do banco (replica-agnóstico).

## Invariante (verificada ponta-a-ponta)
A identidade `consumerName` é a mesma entre o claim do `SessionManager`, a chave `wpp:inbox:<owner>` que o producer escreve, e o inbox que o consumer lê. Group único `wpp-consumers` para create/read/ack/autoclaim. `OwnerRegistry` é instância única compartilhada via DI por `SessionManager`, `WppQueueService` e `WppConsumer`.

## Testes

Desenvolvido em TDD estrito (teste falha → mínimo → passa → commit), 8 tasks com revisão dupla (spec + qualidade) por task.

- **Módulo WPP: 40 arquivos, 518 testes, 0 falhas.**
- **Prova multi-réplica (`affinity-e2e.test.ts`)** — 1 Redis, 2 consumers R1/R2, socket só em R2:
  - 30 `SEND_MESSAGE` → **30/30 processados por R2**, **0 por R1**, **0 em `wpp:send-message`** (legado). Determinístico (2 execuções).
  - 30 `CONNECT` → distribuídos entre R1 e R2 (splits observados 15/15, 14/16, 13/17), soma 30, ambos > 0.

## Considerações de rollout (ler antes do deploy)

- **Janela de deploy rolling:** o consumer novo deixa de ler os streams físicos device-bound. Jobs escritos por um *producer antigo* nesses streams durante o rolling update só são drenados pelos consumers antigos até saírem. Janela curta (cadência do Swarm); callers reenviam. Vale observar timeouts de correlação durante o update. (Streams persistem no Redis; nada é perdido.)
- **At-least-once:** `drainPending`/reclaim são at-least-once (igual ao resto do pipeline de streams); duplicatas toleradas via operações rastreadas por `correlationId`.
- **`RECONNECT`/`RESET`:** chamam `destroySession` (libera ownership) antes de recriar — janela mínima (1 RTT) em que um job concorrente pode parkear; é drenado no re-claim seguinte.
- **Limitação conhecida (fora de escopo):** réplica totalmente morta cujo inbox nunca é lido não é varrida (não há sweeper global de `wpp:inbox:*`).

## Notas
- `bun run lint` limpo (0 erros). `typecheck`: os arquivos deste PR têm **0 erros**; erros restantes do `tsc` são **pré-existentes** em módulos não tocados (`billing`, `decision-platform`, `wpp-business/analytics`, `shared/container/index.ts`) — idênticos a `main`.

## Validação staging (pós-merge, só com aprovação)

title: fix(wpp): consumerName por hostname (process.pid colide entre réplicas) — follow-up #158
body:
## Follow-up de #158 — bug encontrado na validação em staging

Ao validar #158 em staging (3 réplicas do `wpp-session-worker`), o roteamento por afinidade **não funcionou**: havia só **um** inbox stream (`wpp:inbox:wpp-consumer-8`) e nenhuma chave no owner-directory. Causa: `consumerName = wpp-consumer-${process.pid}` — mas `process.pid` **não é único entre réplicas de container**. Cada container roda `dumb-init`(PID 1) → `bun`(7) → `bun`(8), então `process.pid = 8` em **todas** as réplicas → todas colidem no nome `wpp-consumer-8`, leem o mesmo inbox com o mesmo nome de consumer, e uma mensagem pode cair numa réplica sem o socket → **o "No active session" persistiria**.

O e2e de #158 passou porque usava nomes explícitos (R1/R2); produção usa `process.pid`.

## Fix
`defaultConsumerName()` deriva a identidade do **hostname do container** (o Swarm dá um hostname único por task — ex. `1b34e72b9741`), com fallback pra `process.pid` em bare-metal/local. Usado tanto no `WppConsumer` quanto no `SessionManager` (mantidos consistentes; o worker já sincroniza via `setConsumerName`).

Verificado: o stack de staging **não** fixa `hostname:`, então o Swarm atribui o container-id (único por réplica).

## Testes
- Novo teste em `queue-routing.test.ts`: hostnames distintos → nomes distintos (prova ausência de colisão entre réplicas).
- Regressão: 129 testes WPP verdes (incl. a prova multi-réplica `affinity-e2e`). typecheck/lint limpos nos arquivos do PR.

Próximo: deploy em staging + repetir o probe dos 12 envios (esperado 12/12).

title: fix(file-storage): URL pré-assinada interna p/ callers server-side (conserta mídia/transcrição WPP)
body:
## Mídia/transcrição: URL pré-assinada interna para callers server-side

### Contexto
A validação em staging do fix de session-affinity (#158/#159) expôs um problema **separado** de infra do file-storage. Com o roteamento corrigido, o `DOWNLOAD_MEDIA` passou a chegar na réplica dona e o Baileys baixa a mídia — mas o worker então faz `PUT` dos bytes numa URL pré-assinada apontando pro **domínio público** `https://s3.bb.stg.catalisa.app`, **inalcançável de dentro do swarm** (`ConnectionRefused`/timeout). Resultado: a mídia nunca materializa → `GET /messages/media/:id` fica em `202` eterno → a transcrição falha com `BB media still materializing`. (Estava mascarado antes: o `DOWNLOAD_MEDIA` morria no "No active session" sem chegar no upload.)

### Fix (automático e determinístico)
Seleção de endpoint por propósito da URL, **sem flag por chamada e sem config por ambiente**:
- **upload server-to-server (interno) → endpoint INTERNO** (`S3_ENDPOINT`, ex. `minio:9000`, alcançável de dentro do cluster);
- **upload de cliente externo → endpoint PÚBLICO** (inalterado);
- **download → sempre PÚBLICO** (repassado a consumidores externos, ex. a operacao-digital).

O sinal determinístico já existia: o facade BB→BB autentica como o **usuário sentinela** `INTERNAL_FILE_STORAGE_USER_ID` (`00000000-…`). O `files.router` detecta esse sentinela e assina o upload com o endpoint interno; o facade local passa `internal=true` direto. O `wpp-session-worker` **não muda** — passa a receber a URL interna automaticamente.

Camadas: `S3Service.generateUploadUrl(...internal)`, `FileService.createFile/getUploadUrl(...internal)`, `files.router` (sentinela), `LocalFileStorageFacade` (`internal=true`).

### Testes + docs
- `s3.service.test.ts`: upload/download interno vs público (endpoint correto). Default = público.
- `local-file-storage.facade.test.ts`: facade passa `internal=true`.
- 104 testes file-storage/s3/facade verdes; typecheck/lint limpos.
- Doc: `docs/file-storage-internal-presigned-urls.md`.

### Validação pós-deploy
Em staging: receber áudio/imagem no device operacao-digital → `GET /messages/media/:id` vira **202→200** (materializa) e a transcrição completa, sem `ConnectionRefused`/`materializing`.

⚠️ Prod tem o mesmo desenho (`s3.bb.catalisa.app`) → este fix é necessário pra mídia funcionar em prod quando um device conectar.

title: fix(workflows): CONDITIONAL multi-branch routing corruption-proof (builder save no longer breaks routing)
body:
## Problem (production incident)
Any workflow with a **multi-branch (>2) CONDITIONAL** silently broke its routing the moment it was opened+saved in the visual builder: every branch collapsed onto index 1 (`branchName: "False"`), so all but one branch became unreachable ("Branch not taken" → empty responses).

## Root cause (verified)
`apiToCanvas.ts` reconstructed branch edges from `dependsOn: ["<cond>:N"]` but only handled the legacy boolean `true`/`false` case — every **numeric** index fell through to `branch-1`/"False". `canvasToApi` then persisted that collapse back into both `dependsOn` and `layout.edges`, and the graph executor trusted the corrupted `data.edgeType`.

## Fix (generic — single source of truth is the `sourceHandle`)
- **apiToCanvas** (the defect): reconstruct numeric branch indices + `default`/else correctly, real branch name from config, dedup with the `branch.actions` pass.
- **edge-graph.service** (live graph executor): derive the canonical **index-based** `edgeType` from `sourceHandle` *before* a stale `data.edgeType`; drop the name-based form that could never match `determineEdgeType` (`branch:<index>`).
- **dag-executor**: defer the eager layout-edge skip to the reliable `matchedIndex` + `dependsOn` gating when a target has an explicit branch dependency.
- **scripts/repair-conditional-routing.ts**: conservative audit/repair for already-corrupted workflows (recovers from authoritative `sourceHandle` or declarative `branch.actions`, normalizes all three representations, flags ambiguous cases; dry-run by default).

## Tests
- Frontend round-trip (`apiToCanvas.test.ts`): 5-branch reconstruction + `apiToCanvas↔canvasToApi` preserves `rota:0..4` (3/3 green).
- Backend (`edge-graph.service.spec.ts`): index-based edgeType + corruption-proof derivation with stale `data.edgeType` (35/35 green).

## Validation
- Repair script applied on staging: 5 conditionals already consistent, 2 (consórcio demo) normalized, 0 flagged; **idempotent** on re-run.
- Routing E2E on staging: all 6 intents (SIMULACAO/DUVIDA/HUMANO/STATUS/PROCEDIMENTO/COMISSAO) route to the correct specialist with non-empty responses.
- Deploy build (both packages) green; pre-existing unrelated `activities`/SDK errors confirmed not introduced here.

Versions: painel-cliente-api 1.16.15, painel-cliente 1.14.7.

title: fix(calendar): Outlook free/busy correctness for scheduler agent
body:
Fixes the operacao-investimentos scheduler agent offering busy times / erroring on single-day queries. Four chained bugs in the Outlook calendar provider:

1. `getBusyPeriods` called MS Graph `getSchedule` with `schedules:['me']` ('me' is not a resolvable SMTP address → empty all-free schedule → double-booking). Now uses the connection's `externalEmail` (threaded via `CalendarProviderOptions.accountEmail`).
2. `getSchedule` lacked `Prefer: outlook.timezone` and the mapper didn't convert → busy blocks shifted by the local↔UTC delta. Now pins the response TZ and converts to UTC instants via `parseInTimezone`.
3. Single-day query (`startDate === endDate`, date-only) sent `startTime === endTime` (zero-length window) → "Failed to get Outlook busy periods". Now expands date-only bounds to `T00:00:00`/`T23:59:59`.

Google provider already uses `/freeBusy` correctly and is unaffected. Unit tests added for getBusyPeriods. Deployed + validated stg+prod 2026-06-24.

title: feat(calendar): external calendar-connect invite link (secure single-use, BB-backed)
body:
## What

A logged-in **owner** mints a **single-use, 24h-TTL** link. An **external person with no panel login** opens it and connects their own Outlook/Google calendar via BB Calendar. The resulting `Credential` (`serviceName='calendar-bb'`) is owned by the invite owner. Mirrors the capture-links public-link security model.

Plan: `docs/plans/2026-06-25-external-calendar-connect-invite-link.md`

## Why it's safe & reconfig-free (verified vs building-blocks-v2)

- BB calls run under the **service token**, not a user JWT → a logged-out visitor can drive the whole BB OAuth; ownership is assigned 100% panel-side.
- BB `connect` accepts only `{configId, redirectUrl, scopes?}` (no caller `state`) and **echoes `redirectUrl` verbatim** after its callback → we carry the invite code in `redirectUrl`. **No Microsoft/Google app reconfig** (provider `redirect_uri` stays BB's own `/callback`).

## Security

- 256-bit opaque token; single-use status machine (`PENDING→STARTED→CONSUMED`, `EXPIRED`/`REVOKED`); per-IP `@Throttle` on public endpoints.
- **Ownership derived only from `invite.ownerId`** — no field in any public request can influence which panel user owns the connection.
- **Attribution race closed**: start-snapshot of BB connection ids + `startedAt` lower bound + **partial UNIQUE index** `credentials(bbConnectionId) WHERE serviceName='calendar-bb'` (P2002 → next candidate). Adds plaintext `Credential.bbConnectionId`; the authenticated `completeOAuth` now also populates it (also closes the PR #253 multi-pod double-claim tech-debt).

## Tests
23 new unit tests (claim attribution + invite lifecycle); existing calendar/credentials specs green; root build + frontend vite build clean.

## Staging
Deployed + smoke-tested on stg (api `1.16.17`, panel `1.14.8`). Migration applied to `panel_staging_db` via idempotent SQL (`prisma db execute`, not `migrate deploy` — shared DB). Verified: create → public view (branding) → start returns a **real Microsoft consent URL** → all gates correct (complete-before-start 400, unknown 404, revoked 403, no-consent complete = designed 404).

⚠️ Browser OAuth consent → `complete` → Credential creation validated manually by the owner (curl can't drive provider consent).

title: fix(wpp): normalize pairing-code phone to digits (fixes 401 bind from '+' prefix)
body:
## Problema
O pairing code (Baileys, não business) gerava o código mas **não vinculava** quando o número vinha com `+`. Confirmado ao vivo em staging: devices do painel com `pairingPhoneNumber = +5511930802555` davam `401` no bind; número só-dígitos pareava normal.

## Causa raiz
Baileys `requestPairingCode` faz `jidEncode(phoneNumber, 's.whatsapp.net')` **sem remover não-dígitos** → com `+` o device se registra como JID inválido `+5511...@s.whatsapp.net` → WhatsApp rejeita o `link_code_companion_reg` com 401 (código gera, mas nunca pareia).

## Fix
Normaliza pra dígitos em dois pontos:
- `BaileysDriver.requestPairingCode`: `phoneNumber.replace(/\D/g, '')` antes do `sock.requestPairingCode` (última linha antes do Baileys; cobre qualquer caller), rejeita < 10 dígitos.
- `pairingCodeSchema`: `.transform` pra dígitos → `pairingPhoneNumber` persistido e payload do job também limpos.

Teste unitário atualizado (`baileys-driver.test.ts`): valida normalização (`+55 11 99999-9999` → `5511999999999`) e a guarda de < 10 dígitos. Suíte do driver verde (45/45).

## Extra (commit separado)
`chore: untrack accidental self-referential node_modules symlink` — o PR #163 commitou um symlink `node_modules` self-referential que quebra `bun install`/tooling com ELOOP na main. node_modules já está em `.gitignore`/`.dockerignore`; só removo a entrada rastreada acidental.

## Validação
- Local + staging + prod já validados ao vivo com o stack rc.9 (pairing pareia com número sem `+`).
- Este fix faz o caminho do painel (que manda `+`) funcionar também.

title: chore(painel-cliente-api): bump @catalisa/panel-sdk ^0.1.5→^0.6.0 (workspace/tarball, mata filtro defensivo)
body:
## O que muda

Mata o drift de versões do `@catalisa/panel-sdk`: o painel-cliente-api pinava `^0.1.5` (última versão publicada no registry npm) enquanto o workspace `apps/panel-sdk` está em **0.6.0**. O runtime em staging/prod já rodava código 0.6.0 via overlay manual de `dist` no Dockerfile — este PR torna isso oficial e remove o workaround.

- **`apps/painel-cliente-api/package.json`**: `@catalisa/panel-sdk` `^0.1.5` → `^0.6.0`; `version` `1.16.17` → `1.16.18` (convenção patch, cf. 1.16.16→1.16.17).
- **Lockfile raiz**: npm workspaces agora resolve o irmão `apps/panel-sdk` via symlink hoisted (`node_modules/@catalisa/panel-sdk → apps/panel-sdk`); a cópia aninhada 0.1.5 do registry (`apps/painel-cliente-api/node_modules/@catalisa/panel-sdk`) sai do lock (-15 linhas).
- **Dockerfile** (não pode depender do registry — 0.6.0 NÃO está publicado e não há credencial npm):
  - `sdk-builder`: `npm pack` após o build → `catalisa-panel-sdk-0.6.0.tgz`.
  - Estágios `deps` e `pruner`: `COPY` do tarball + `npm install <tarball>` **antes** do install geral — o primeiro install reescreve o spec para `file:`, então o install geral nunca pergunta ao registry pelo panel-sdk.
  - Overlay manual de dist removido (ex-linhas 66-67 e 112-113) — redundante com o install via tarball.
- **Filtro defensivo (PR #351) removido** em `tools-executor.service.ts` (`list_leads`): o SDK 0.6.0 traduz `type`/`status` server-side; sem pós-filtro local nem fetch inflado de 100 itens. Cap defensivo de 20 itens mantido.
- Spec `tools-executor.list-leads-filter.spec.ts` adaptado: prova que `type`/`status` chegam intactos ao SDK e que o cap de 20 vale mesmo com filtros.

## Evidência: SDK 0.6.0 traduz type/status e exporta calendarEvents

- `apps/panel-sdk/src/resources/leads.ts:91-96` — `buildListQuery` mapeia `params.status`/`params.type` para o array de `AdvancedFilter` com `operator: 'eq'`.
- `apps/panel-sdk/src/types/common.ts:126` — `buildPaginatedQuery` serializa cada filtro como `filter[${f.field}][${f.operator}]=valor`.
- `apps/panel-sdk/src/client.ts:169` e `:237` — `public readonly calendarEvents: CalendarEventsResource` instanciado no client; exportado em `apps/panel-sdk/src/index.ts:68`.

## Decisão: lockfile aninhado (`apps/painel-cliente-api/package-lock.json`)

**Mantido intocado (stale).** Ele é ancestral (name/version `1.0.2`, nem menciona o panel-sdk) e não é usado por nada: o Dockerfile usa `npm install` (nunca `npm ci`), que ignora/reconcilia o lock em-container, e o dev local resolve pelo lockfile da RAIZ (workspaces). Regenerá-lo standalone é impossível — `npm install` standalone falharia contra o registry (0.6.0 inexistente lá). Se quisermos, um follow-up pode deletá-lo.

| Check | Resultado |
|---|---|
| `npm install` (raiz, workspaces) | ✅ `node_modules/@catalisa/panel-sdk → apps/panel-sdk` (symlink 0.6.0); sem cópia aninhada 0.1.5 |
| `npx tsc -p tsconfig.build.json` | ✅ **0 erros** — os ~13 erros de build (calendarEvents etc.) sumiram só com os tipos novos, sem nenhum fix de código |
| `npm run test` (Jest) | ⚠️ **5701 passed, 1 failed, 55 skipped** — a falha é **pré-existente em master** (ver abaixo) |
| `docker build --target pruner` | ✅ exit 0; imagem contém panel-sdk **0.6.0** com `dist/` via tarball |
| Smoke na imagem | ✅ `require('@catalisa/panel-sdk')` carrega; `client.calendarEvents` = object, `client.leads.list` = function |

`modules/workflow-templates/__tests__/workflow-templates.spec.ts` › "install › should add builtin tools for each agent": espera `addBuiltinTools(user, agent, tools)` mas o service agora passa um 4º arg `{allowExternalContext: {...}}` — introduzido pelo commit `dc4a7740` (já em master), que mudou `workflow-templates.service.ts` sem atualizar o spec. title: feat(wpp): terminal status logged_out + guard requires_repair + connect budget
body:
## Contexto — incidente 2026-07-03 (bans temporários de WhatsApp em beta tester)

Device deslogado (401 LoggedOut) ficava `closed` — indistinguível de queda transitória. O reconciler de saúde da operacao-digital re-kickava `devices.connect` a cada ~3min com credencial morta: **26h+ de 401-loop contra o WhatsApp → bans temporários no número da usuária**.

## O que muda

1. **Status terminal `logged_out`** (enum + migração `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE`): `LoggedOut`/`BadSession` → `logged_out`; `Banned` → `banned`. `closed` volta a significar só "queda reconectável".
2. **Guard no choke point** `getOrCreateSession` (cobre rota externa, consumer e reconnect interno): device terminal sem repair → `409 CONFLICT requires_repair` + `connection_log reconnect_skipped`. Fast-path 409 na rota `POST /:deviceId/connect`.
3. **Repair explícito**: `connect { force: true }` wipa o auth state persistido (`BaileysAuthStateProvider.clear`) e reseta o device para registro limpo (QR/pairing novos). Não há outro caminho para reabrir device terminal.
4. **Orçamento de connect por device**: Redis, janela 1h, default 30 (`WPP_CONNECT_BUDGET_PER_HOUR`); excedente → `CONFLICT connect_budget_exceeded` + log. Fail-open se Redis falhar. Garante o "nunca mais" mesmo se um consumidor futuro se comportar mal.
5. **Evento `DEVICE_DISCONNECTED` não-recuperável** ganha `requiresRepair: true` + `deviceStatus` para consumidores pararem de auto-reconectar imediatamente.
6. **Fix `handleReset`**: limpava só chaves Redis legadas; agora wipa as creds reais (Postgres/WaAuthRepository).

## Compatibilidade

- Auto-reconnect interno para quedas transitórias (428 etc.) **inalterado** (backoff+circuit breaker existentes).
- Consumidores que hoje só olham `status === 'open'` continuam funcionando; ganham o novo status para diferenciar.
- Migração é `ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS` — zero downtime.

## Testes

`vitest run tests/unit/wpp` — **1598 verdes / 98 arquivos** (guard, budget, repair, mapeamento terminal, reset, regressões).

title: fix(wpp): socket duplicado entre réplicas + ressurreição pós-destroy (causa-raiz do churn 428)
body:
## Causa-raiz (investigação em cima do wpp_connection_logs de staging)

Os conflicts vêm em **rajadas rítmicas de ~5s** — dois sockets da mesma sessão se derrubando alternadamente até o WhatsApp **invalidar a credencial** (401). Dois iniciadores, ambos com flagra nos logs:

1. **`session_restore` duplica socket**: job de restore (boot de réplica) cai em réplica que NÃO é dona do socket vivo → `getOrCreateSession` só olha o mapa local → segundo socket. Flagra: restore 02:57:03 → conflict 1s depois (q6e7e3aj, 28/06); e o caso da beta tester (restore 06:53 → conflict+401 às 09:41 de 02/07).
2. **Destroy manual ressuscita**: `driver.disconnect()` emitia close `reason=0` (recuperável) → reconnect agendado segundos após o destroy. Flagra: 04:59:38 de 28/06 (destroy → 2 reconnects → 3 connecting simultâneos → rajada de 440).

## Fix

- **Owner pre-flight** no `getOrCreateSession` (choke point): claim atômico no `OwnerRegistry` (SET NX, TTL 45s) antes de criar socket; réplica não-dona recusa com `CONFLICT owner_held` + `reconnect_skipped` no log. Cobre restore, connect externo e reconnect interno. Fail-open se Redis cair.
- **`DisconnectReason.ManualDisconnect` (-1)**: drivers emitem no disconnect intencional; o close handler não agenda reconnect; `destroySession` cancela timer pendente (mesmo sem sessão no mapa).

Complementa o #184: o budget de 30/h já **continha** essas rajadas; este PR elimina a origem.

title: feat(slack): Slack channel Building Block — Phase 1 (OAuth, events, send, dispatcher, routers)
body:
## Slack Building Block — Phase 1 (HTTP contract locked)

New Catalisa Building Block `src/slack` that makes Slack a first-class operacao-digital channel, mirroring the `email`/`wpp` modules. **The only component that talks the Slack API.** Delivers events to operacao-digital's `POST /webhooks/bb-events` via the same webhooks-engine dispatcher mechanism as WPP.

Implemented via TDD (`superpowers:subagent-driven-development`): one fresh implementer per task + combined spec/quality review per task. **23 vitest unit tests green; `tsc --noEmit` clean for all slack files.**

### What's in (Tasks 1.1–1.8)
- **Prisma** `SlackConnection` + `SlackDispatcher` (`slack` schema, migration `add_slack_module`).
- **OAuth user-token** (`@slack/web-api`): authorize-URL builder + code→token exchange.
- **SlackConnectionService** — `connect` (encrypted state) + `handleCallback` + encrypted token storage (`SLACK_CREDENTIAL_MASTER_KEY`, AES-256-GCM, mirrors email crypto).
- **SlackDispatcherService** — provisions a webhooks-engine subscription (`eventFilters: slack.v1.message.received/.sent`, `x-webhook-secret`).
- **SlackSendService** — `chat.postMessage` as the user; `getDecryptedToken`.
- **Events endpoint** — `url_verification` challenge, **HMAC-SHA256 signature verify + 5-min anti-replay** (timing-safe), noise filter (DMs + `@mentions` + watched channels; drops bot/edit subtypes), fan-out via `EventPublisher.safePublish` → Redis Stream `iam-events`.
- **Channel registry** (`conversations.list`) + routers (connection/dispatcher/messages/channels/events; callback + events are public) + `app.ts`/`main.ts`.
- **Wiring**: `SLACK_READ`/`SLACK_WRITE` permissions, env vars, container module (`SLACK_OAUTH_CONFIG`), mount in `src/app.ts`.
- **Deploy**: docker-compose + swarm staging/prod + `build.mjs` entry; manual app runbook in `docs/slack/SETUP.md`.

### Frozen HTTP contract (BB ⇄ operacao-digital)
`POST /api/v1/slack/connections/connect` · `GET /api/v1/slack/connections/callback` · `GET /api/v1/slack/connections` · `GET /api/v1/slack/channels` · `POST /api/v1/slack/dispatchers` · `PATCH /api/v1/slack/dispatchers/:id` · `POST /api/v1/slack/messages/send` · events `slack.v1.message.received|sent`.

### Decisions (locked)
User-token identity (reads your DMs, replies as you); DMs + mentions + chosen channels; multi-workspace; Pro+ gating (operacao-digital side); v1 = read + approve + auto-send.
**Risk:** Slack app-review for user-token `*:history` scopes → documented bot-app fallback (BB-only change). See `docs/slack/SETUP.md`.

### Known follow-ups (post-Phase-1)
- `DELETE /api/v1/slack/connections/:id` (disconnect) — email has it; needed by operacao-digital Phase 4.
- `slack.facade.ts` for `MODULE_SLACK_URL` cross-module calls (only when run as a separate service).
- `x-webhook-secret` stored plaintext in `customHeaders` (security-pass note; parity with wpp-business).

### Not in this PR
operacao-digital-side Phases 2–6 (schema/ingest, send routing, connect/multi-account, gating, mobile) — separate repo (`app.operacao-digital.ai`).
